someone-to-you-coverage.label: SOMEONE->YOU EVENT COVERAGE (T108's registry ratchet, static/fast). The registry (substrate/reference/someone_to_you_event_registry.json) enumerates every event where person A's action creates work/attention for person B — the T108 bar: each needs a notification path + a tap that lands ON the item; 'none' rows are the SILENT-WORK class (assignment discovered by accident). This holds two things: (1) every row well-formed with notification in the declared vocab; (2) the silent-row count NEVER grows past the accepted baseline (4 as of 2026-08-25: WO-assignment, post-reported-to-supervisor, submission approved/rejected, supervisor password reset) — shipping a new someone->you event without a notification lane FAILs by name; fixing one ratchets the baseline down. Registry rows are hand-enumerated with source receipts — add a row when a new event type ships (the new-roster-KIND lesson).

join-lands-on-roster.label: T6+T7 paired join journey (LIVE two-context Playwright) — the shared instrument close. An OUTSIDE worker (member of a different hive) joins the supervisor's hive by invite code through the SAME join_hive_by_code path the UI submit calls, while the supervisor's hive.html board watches. PASS bar: the join is VISIBLE on the watching roster after at most one reload, the DB row landed, and the probe membership is deleted + verified afterward (scoped delete: exact hive+worker, 15-min window; the prover ABORTS on dirty pre-state rather than deleting rows it did not create). Also MEASURES (never asserts) the realtime half: hive.html has no postgres_changes channel on hive_members, so realtime=false is today's recorded truth — the receipt flips the day a channel lands. Retry-once (live gates flake under load). Re-drive: node tools/prove_join_lands.mjs. Skips cleanly if node or the local stack is absent.

g5d-reauth-restore.label: T8: g5d-reauth-restore gate — T8's return-trip context contract (2026-08-26). Runs tools/prove_g5d_reauth_restore.mjs: on each covered page, set a filter, kill the session, re-auth through index.html?signin=1&return=<page>, and assert the page comes back WITH the filter still applied. Session expiry must cost one sign-in and zero context. Covered this slice: logbook (filter-category) + pm-scheduler (cat-filter) — the two pages wired through the central whAutoRememberFilters helper. Pages with bespoke persistence are later slices; the prover states its scope. Instrument lesson baked into the prover: the G5a wiring lands DEEP inside each page's async init(), seconds after the filter element parses — the setter is therefore SELF-VERIFYING (retries until the wh_view_* store actually holds the save) so a probe race can never again read as a page defect. Discipline: retry-once, node direct (ampersand path), utf-8 pinned, line-anchored PASS, SKIP when node/stack absent.

timed-journey-family.label: T9/T10/T13: timed-journey gate — the T9/T10/T13 shared oracle, slice 1 (2026-08-26). Runs tools/prove_timed_journey.mjs: each case is one user JOB with a stated budget - the prover walks the scripted core path and reports measured wall time vs budget. Slice 1: T13's handover-read (worker @390 opens shift-brain; usable = verdict resolved + carry-forward list populated or honestly empty). The machine measures the PLATFORM's share (time until the read is possible), never the human's reading time; a breach is a slowness-regression signal. Write-journeys (T9 time-to-logged, T10 completion loop) are later slices. Discipline: retry-once, node direct (ampersand path), utf-8 pinned, line-anchored PASS, SKIP when node/stack absent.

stock-ripple.label: T11: stock-ripple gate - T11's cross-page write-propagation oracle (2026-08-26). Runs tools/prove_stock_ripple.mjs: stage a part at min_qty+1, read index's low-stock tile (pre), issue 1 through inventory's OWN Use modal (the atomic inventory_deduct RPC), reload index - the tile must read pre+1. Write-side sibling of cross_surface_agreement (which locks READ-parity only). Hygiene: the part's qty is snapshotted + restored, probe transactions (WH-T11-PROBE) deleted with NO time window (marker rows are artifacts by definition - a window once spared an older orphan), both verified; ABORTs on no stageable part. Discipline (carried from validate_offline_queued.py): - retry-once before failing (full-suite live gates flake under load). - node invoked DIRECTLY, never npx (the repo path contains an ampersand). - utf-8 pinned on the subprocess decode; PASS matched line-anchored. - SKIPs cleanly when node / the local stack is absent — a gate that cannot run must say SKIP, not PASS. - the prover ABORTS (exit 2) on dirty pre-state rather than deleting rows it did not create; that surfaces here as FAIL with the abort line.

The low-stock tile's multi-band handoff is a RECORDED follow-up, not a silent skip. Discipline (carried from validate_offline_queued.py): - retry-once before failing (full-suite live gates flake under load). - node invoked DIRECTLY, never npx (the repo path contains an ampersand). - utf-8 pinned on the subprocess decode; PASS matched line-anchored. - SKIPs cleanly when node / the local stack is absent — a gate that cannot run must say SKIP, not PASS. - the prover ABORTS (exit 2) on dirty pre-state rather than deleting rows it did not create; that surfaces here as FAIL with the abort line.

fil-parity.label: T45: fil-parity lint — T45's translation-parity gate (2026-08-26). Scans every _t('en','fil') call site for IDENTICAL en/fil arguments — the signature of a string that was ADDED to the EN branch without a Filipino translation (my 2026-08-25 error-taxonomy sweep created exactly this debt: new taxonomy strings landed EN-only inside _t() calls). Not every identical pair is debt: proper nouns, codes, and ALL-CAPS tokens ('OK', 'PM', 'QR') legitimately read the same in both languages — those are excluded by shape (short, or all caps/digits/punct). Everything else counts. Forward-only ratchet: the count may only fall. Baseline stored inline in fil_parity_baseline.json (created on first run with the measured count).

fee-parity.label: T103: fee-parity gate — T103's stated-vs-charged oracle (2026-08-26). Every fee percentage a page STATES to a user is a promise; the DB is what actually charges. They are wired independently — the glass hardcodes '10%' while `listing_reservation_amount` resolves a per-hive `reward_pct` knob through `service_knob_pct` (defaulting from the platform table) — so a knob change silently makes the copy a lie. That gap is exactly the surprise-charge class this gate exists to prevent. What it checks, per claim in CLAIMS below: 1. the stated percentage still appears on its page (the copy has not moved without this gate noticing); 2. the DB's own effective rate for that knob equals the stated number. The DB side is read LIVE via psql (the platform default plus every hive override, so a single divergent hive fails the gate rather than hiding behind an average). SKIPs when the stack is down — a gate that cannot read the DB must say SKIP, never PASS.

error-taxonomy-ratchet.label: T176: error-taxonomy ratchet — T176's 'new errors are born compliant' gate (2026-08-26). The platform has three taxonomy helpers — whReadError / whWriteError / whAiError — that turn a raw failure into a sentence naming the CAUSE, the state of the user's WORK, and the NEXT STEP. Adoption was driven page by page across several arcs. The risk now is regression by accretion: a new `showToast('Something went wrong')` costs nothing to write and quietly re-opens the class. WHAT THIS COUNTS: user-facing failure strings handed to showToast / setStatus / textContent / innerHTML inside (or right after) a catch or an `if (error)` branch, where NO taxonomy helper appears on the same line. That is the RAW-APPEND class. Forward-only ratchet against tools/error_taxonomy_baseline.json — the count may fall (and the baseline auto-lowers), never rise. It deliberately does NOT try to judge sentence quality: a lint that guesses at prose produces false reds, while a count of raw appends is objective and is exactly the regression signal. ★ZERO IS NOT THE GOAL. Audited 2026-08-26 by reading the remainder one by one: much of what is left is well-written raw sentences that already name cause, work state and next step ('Wrong username or password.', 'A logbook entry can only be corrected by its author', 'Someone else changed this feedback. Your note was not saved') — they simply do not route through a helper. Rewriting those to lower the number would make the copy WORSE to move a metric. Convert what ECHOES A DRIVER MESSAGE or says nothing useful; leave sentences that already do the job.

cascade-confirm-parity.label: T139: cascade-confirm parity — T139's blast-radius oracle (2026-08-26). A delete confirm is a CLAIM about consequences, and the FK graph is the truth. When a table has ON DELETE CASCADE children, deleting one row silently destroys rows on other surfaces — an asset's Weibull fits, a project's change orders, a PM plan's completion history. If the confirm does not say so, the person approves a consequence they were never shown. WHAT IT DOES 1. Reads the LIVE FK graph (psql): every table with ON DELETE CASCADE children. 2. Finds every client delete site: `.from('<table>')` … `.delete()` in the HTML. 3. Looks back for the nearest whConfirm/confirm text guarding that site. 4. FAILs a site whose table cascades and whose confirm names NO consequence — no child-count, no 'removes/deletes/cannot be undone' clause, or no confirm at all. It checks that a consequence is STATED, not that the wording is perfect: prose grading produces false reds, while 'cascades silently, says nothing' is objective and is the class that hurts. Forward-only against tools/cascade_confirm_baseline.json. SKIPs when psql is unreachable — the FK graph is the oracle, and a gate without its oracle must say SKIP, never PASS. ★INSTRUMENT FIX 2026-08-26 (T50): this gate was VACUOUS. Its consequence pattern included `removes?` and `deletes?`, so 'Remove this asset from the registry?' - four words naming only the ACTION - matched on 'Remove' and passed, and nearly every destructive confirm is phrased that way, so it reported 0 while asking nothing. A consequence is what happens BESIDES the thing you just asked for; the verb is the ask. Demonstrated by resurrection: against the pre-fix wording the old pattern found 0 and the tightened one finds the logbook asset delete, whose row CASCADES seven children (asset_edges, asset_embeddings, pf_intervals, rcm_fmea_modes, sensor_readings, sensor_topic_map, weibull_fits) and detaches five more - reachable by a supervisor on an APPROVED asset, so a plant's reliability history could go behind a four-word question. Confirm rewritten to name both halves (what dies, what survives); tightening revealed no other site, so it cost no backlog.

pending-submission-reach.label: T108's LAST silent row. A supervisor's only signal that work was waiting on them was a realtime postgres_changes subscription living on hive.html - it fired while, and only while, they had the board open, so a supervisor reading the logbook or with the app closed learned of a submission by happening to visit. Mig 20260826000003 puts a trigger on asset_nodes and inventory_items instead of wiring call sites, because pending rows come from asset-hub (submit + resubmit), inventory (two paths), logbook and integrations' BULK CMMS upsert - six-plus paths across five pages, where a missed one is invisible: the row lands, nobody is told, nothing errors. FIVE assertions, and two of them are what make the design safe rather than merely functional. THE STORM TEST: twenty rows inserted at once must produce ONE push, not twenty - the copy deliberately names no row so enqueue_user_push's 2-minute dedupe collapses them, which turns the existing dedupe window into the storm guard instead of adding a second mechanism. THE BLOCKING TEST: with the push helper deliberately renamed away, the submission must still land - a notification is an extra, the user's work is not, and this codebase has already paid once for a guard that broke the writes it rode on, so the gate proves it rather than trusting the EXCEPTION clause. The prover repairs itself, re-checking the renamed helper at start and end, because a probe that can outlive its own damage is not acceptable. SKIPs without docker/stack.

community-notifications.label: T108's last three silent rows. The someone-to-you event registry named eight ways a person is addressed by name; five were wired in earlier passes and three stayed BADGE-ONLY, meaning the platform knew and the person did not. A MENTION was the sharpest: parseMentions runs on both the create and the edit path and renderContentWithMentions paints the result, so being named was a first-class fact that reached everyone EXCEPT the person named - the nav-hub badge counts posts generally, which is a different sentence. A REPLY was T31's finding: the asker learned an answer had arrived only by coming back to look. A BEST ANSWER was recorded in the XP ledger and discovered by revisiting. Mig 20260826000002 adds three guarded RPCs on the notify_wo_assigned shape - the caller names a ROW, never a recipient and never the copy, because a client that could pass an auth_uid and a body would be a push cannon pointed at the hive. Six assertions, THREE OF THEM NEGATIVE (self-mention, self-reply and an un-accepted reply must all stay silent): a notifier that fires on everything passes a positive-only test and turns a hive into spam. Driven as a signed-in member, never as postgres - these are SECURITY DEFINER functions guarding on auth_worker_names(), so an owner-run proof would show they work for exactly the caller they must never trust. Probe rows marked and cleanup re-counted. ★AND IT NOW CARRIES T149'S EDIT-DOESN'T-RE-NOTIFY CHECK, whose measurement corrected an assumption: the 2-minute dedupe does NOT protect against a re-notify after an EDIT, because it compares whole payloads and the push body carries the post's content snippet - an edited snippet reads as different news and a second push fires. So the only thing between a supervisor's typo fix and a second buzz for everyone named in an announcement is that the EDIT PATH DOES NOT CALL notify_post_mentions. The gate asserts that single-call-site fact directly, and records the dedupe's blind spot as a FACT rather than pretending it is a defence - anyone adding that call in good faith would create a re-notify bug the dedupe would not catch. SKIPs without docker/stack.

push-deeplink.label: T105's arrival-fidelity oracle for Web Push. sw.js's notificationclick matched an already-open tab with c.url.includes(target.split('?')[0]) - the PATH, query discarded - and returned focus. Every url notify-push sends carries its destination in the QUERY (?tab=services, ?asset=, ?post=), so a provider with marketplace-seller open on ?tab=listings tapped a job-offer push and got their existing view focused, with nothing to say a destination had been promised and missed: the same class as a sign-in wall that drops the return-to. The prover loads the SHIPPING sw.js, installs the listener it registers, and dispatches a synthetic click against a fake clients registry - so it tests the file that ships, not a re-implementation. Three cases: no tab -> openWindow at the full target; tab on a different query -> NAVIGATED there; tab already there -> focus only, never a reload under someone mid-task. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix worker for the wrong-query case ONLY, with cases 1 and 3 green in both worlds. Static tier - no browser, no stack; node only because sw.js is JavaScript.

notification-taxonomy.label: T107's one-honest-concept oracle for 'things for me'. The hive board's bell held four entries on the live board - PM Due Soon, Assets With PM Overdue, Open work orders, Low stock - every one a PLANT CONDITION already painted as a tile on the same page and again in alert-hub, blended with the approval entries, which are the only ones actually about the person reading them: one bell, two concepts, no way to tell which you were looking at. And the only unread signal was a 3% white tint on a dark surface, present in code and invisible in use, so a badge over ten rows gave no way to see WHICH were new. Asserts STRUCTURE, never wording: the two lanes are named, the plant lane links to the surface that owns those conditions, unread carries a marker BOTH a sighted user and a screen reader can find, and every pushNotif type is classified - a new one lands here as a decision rather than drifting into whichever lane the default sends it. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix page for 3 of 4, and the 4th mutation-proven with an injected 'mention' producer.

policy-rls-parity.label: T163's 'the privacy policy is a claim' gate. privacy-policy/index.html promises 'We never share your hive data with another hive without your explicit consent' and NAMES the classes; RLS is what has to keep that promise, so this puts the two side by side. Per class it impersonates a REAL member of hive A (authenticated role + their JWT claims - the shape RLS actually sees) and asks for hive B's rows; the promise holds only at zero. NON-VACUITY is asserted both ways: the other hive must genuinely hold rows (else 0 proves nothing) and the same member must still read their OWN hive (else a blanket-deny would pass while the product is broken). CONSENT-AWARE: an author-published community post is not a leak but the consent clause working, so consented rows are subtracted from the leak test while the un-consented remainder must still be invisible - the gate's first run called 8 such posts a LEAK and the classifier, not the product, was wrong. TEETH-PROVEN: removing the consent predicate makes it correctly report the 8 public rows as visible. SKIPs without docker (RLS is the oracle).

queue-drain.label: T14's OTHER HALF (LIVE Playwright + psql): the offline-queued family proves a write is HELD and announced; this proves it DRAINS. Offline (navigator.onLine overridden AND the route cut): the enqueue lands in the queue's own IndexedDB store and ZERO writes reach the server. Back online with an 'online' event: the row appears in the target table, EXACTLY ONCE (re-checked after a further settle window so a second drain tick cannot hide), and the queue store empties. The offline prover's header deferred this deliberately because 'a drain probe that reconnects into a shared database writes real rows' - so this one writes a MARKED row, deletes it, verifies the delete, and ABORTs rather than measuring on dirty state. THREE probe-shape errors were caught and fixed before any verdict was banked (async getPending awaited; RLS needs auth_uid on the row; the queue item shape is {id, op, payload}, not a flat row) - each would have been a FALSE RED against a working queue. Subject: dayplanner's schedule_items queue (no FK cascade, no ledger side-effects). Retry-once.

trust-claim-backed.label: T70: a verification badge requires the thing it verifies. The seller profile is where a buyer decides whether to trust a stranger with money, so every pixel that reads as an endorsement is a claim the PLATFORM makes on that stranger's behalf - and the recorded incident shows what an unenforced one costs: the 'Certified' chip used to render on the cert_verified flag ALONE across three surfaces, and three sellers were found with cert_verified true, certifications NULL and cert_verified_at NULL, a violet chip asserting an admin had verified trade credentials THAT DID NOT EXIST. CENSUSED EVERY TRUST CLAIM ON THE PROFILE and the page is in good order - each is computed from data rather than decoration: Top rated (ratingAvg >= 4.5 AND ratingCount >= 5), Quick reply (avgResponseHours < 4 AND replyCount >= 5), Tier (stated thresholds - silver 11 sales, gold 51 - plus 'set by WorkHive from completed sales, not self-assigned'), ID Verified (gated on kyb_verified), Certified (routed through whCertBadgeEarned on all three surfaces). ★ONE LOOKED LIKE THE ORIGINAL BUG AND IS NOT: the certifications SECTION reads cert_verified on its own, but the whole block sits inside `if (certSection && certs.length)`, so a non-empty list is guaranteed by construction - read before accusing. THE ASSERTION guards the fixed class rather than a present defect: no buyer-facing surface may present a certification claim from cert_verified alone; it must call the central predicate or guard on the certifications list in the same breath. ★MODERATION SURFACES ARE EXCLUDED BY NAME, and not for convenience: marketplace-admin, founder-console and platform-actions are where verification is GRANTED, so they must see the raw flag including the exact 'set but no certifications on file' state this gate keeps off a buyer's screen - blinding the moderator to what they moderate would invert the goal. Teeth proven by reverting the profile badge to the flag alone, which resurrects the original incident's shape.

ai-render-provenance.label: T87/AI6: the RENDER half of machine authorship. validate_ai_write_provenance proves the WRITE half at 6/6 - every AI write into a human-read domain table declares machine authorship ON THE ROW - and that is necessary but not sufficient, because a row can carry its provenance faithfully while the page throws it away on the way to the screen. ★THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT WAS HAPPENING: logbook's 'past repairs on this machine' panel, the one a technician reads BEFORE OPENING A MACHINE, queried fault_knowledge selecting only problem/root_cause/action/knowledge/worker_name/created_at and rendered each row attributed BY NAME. fault_knowledge is a table the AI also writes into (visual-defect-capture), so a machine-captured observation would have appeared as a repair a named colleague performed. The write was accountable; the READ discarded the accountability. Fixed: the select now fetches source and ai_model, and the render appends 'AI-captured (<model>)' beside the name - verified live with a seeded row, one badge among five, the four human entries untouched, probe removed and residue re-counted 0. ★THE BADGE TESTS source LIKE 'ai_%', NOT != 'manual', because that is the contract the DATABASE enforces - CHECK ((source ~~ 'ai\_%') = (ai_model IS NOT NULL)) over a closed vocabulary of manual / ai_visual_capture / cmms_import - so the badge cannot drift from the guarantee, and cmms_import (an import, not a machine author) is correctly left unmarked. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS, ALL CAUGHT BY THE TEETH TEST: blanking comments with plain spaces preserved byte offsets but destroyed LINE numbers, so it first reported the finding at an Escape-key handler; a .select('id') after an .update() was mistaken for a display read when it is an optimistic-concurrency no-op detector; and a 600-char scan window ended before logbook's own .select() because the explanatory comment above it is ~700 chars - the gate silently stopped seeing the query it was built for and reported PASS with the fix reverted. A window sized to today's code narrows every time someone documents something.

glossary-registry.label: T177: the platform must teach its own vocabulary. WorkHive puts domain acronyms straight onto the glass - MTBF beside a number, OEE on a card, SPI in a project summary. For a reliability engineer that is correct and efficient; for the audience this platform explicitly courts - new graduates, workers coming off paper - an unexplained acronym is a number they can neither act on nor argue with, and 'I did not understand the screen' is indistinguishable from 'the screen was wrong'. THE RULE: every registered term appearing in an app page's visible text must be EXPLAINED somewhere reachable - expanded in place, or taught in the learn cluster. Both count, because a guide is a real answer and so is a phrase in the sentence itself. MEASURED 2026-08-26: thirteen terms on the glass and ELEVEN were already handled well - MTBF, MTTR, OEE, RCM, FMEA, RPN, CPM, LOTO, SOP and P-F each have a learn guide spelling them out, which says the platform's teaching habit is sound. ★THE ONE THAT WAS NOT: project-manager showed supervisors 'EVM: SPI 0.87, CPI 1.02, status ... (BAC ₱..., EV ₱...)' - SIX acronyms in a single line - and nothing anywhere on the platform explained one of them; earned value was the only vocabulary the product used without teaching. Fixed at FIRST USE in that line ('Earned value (EVM): schedule performance SPI ..., cost performance CPI ..., ... (budget at completion ₱..., earned value ₱...)'), because a glossary a reader has to go and find is a glossary they do not read. ★assistant.html IS EXCLUDED WITH ITS REASON: it carries a capability CATALOG describing every other page to the model ('...daily progress, EV/SPI/CPI, and sign-off'), which is model-facing rather than UI and double-counts vocabulary belonging to the pages it names - pages this gate scans on their own. Flagging it would demand a glossary inside a system prompt. Teeth proven by reverting the fix, which reproduces the exact pre-fix finding.

toast-is-readable.label: T182: a message shown too briefly was never shown. A toast is how this platform says 'saved', 'not saved', 'you cannot do that yet' - the entire receipt for most actions - and a receipt that vanishes before it can be read is WORSE than none, because the action looks silent so the person repeats it. Not hypothetical here: the recorded incident had nine REFUSALS displayed for zero milliseconds, i.e. never displayed at all, on exactly the paths where the user most needed to know why they were stopped. MEASURED 2026-08-26 and the class is EXTINCT: 937 showToast calls, 906 on their page's default and 31 with an explicit duration, all between 4000 and 7000ms; every one of the 27 per-page showToast implementations holds its toast 2200-3500ms; nothing anywhere is under 1500ms. TWO ASSERTIONS, guarding an absence rather than fixing a present defect: no call passes an explicit duration below the floor, and no implementation holds its message for less. ★THE FLOOR IS 1500ms AND DELIBERATELY LOW - this gate does not litigate whether 3000 beats 3500, a judgement 27 pages have already made sensibly and which a gate would only turn into enforced taste; it catches what is objectively broken, a message a human cannot finish reading. ★THE CENSUS PARSES ARGUMENTS RATHER THAN SCANNING A WINDOW, and that is the lesson: a first version looked for the nearest ', <number>)' after each call and reported ten short toasts, EVERY ONE FALSE - it had matched slice(0, 24), setTimeout(..., 60) and other numerics belonging to different calls entirely, including a '24ms toast' in utils.js that does not exist. Only balanced-paren splitting knows which arguments belong to which call. Teeth proven on both assertions.

form-control-named.label: T180: every form control says what it is. A control with no accessible name is a box a screen-reader user is asked to fill in without being told what goes in it - and on this platform that was not theoretical: the unnamed ones were a PM frequency selector, a CMMS column mapper, a scope-item include checkbox and its estimated-hours field, each sitting in a LIST of near-identical rows where 'combo box' announced twelve times running is indistinguishable from noise. Fixed six, and every label names the ROW rather than the field, because these are heard out of visual context: 'Frequency for <task text>', 'Source column for <field label>', 'Include scope item <title>', 'Estimated hours for <title>', plus two validator-catalog filters sitting beside a search box that already had one. Verified in the LIVE DOM on all four pages (0 unnamed, 0 pageerrors), which also covers the dynamically-rendered controls a static pass cannot reach. ★THE CENSUS WAS WRONG THREE TIMES AND THE CORRECTIONS ARE THE REAL CONTENT: 41 -> 18 -> 8 -> 6, every step removing FALSE accusations rather than real defects. (1) Checking only label[for=id] missed the WRAPPING form - '<label>Safety-critical <input type=checkbox></label>' - which needs no `for` and is how every checkbox and radio here is labelled; that alone was 23 wrong accusations including all six of hive.html's intent radios. (2) Reading raw source matched <input> and <select> written inside HTML, CSS and JS COMMENTS - prose DESCRIBING controls, like logbook's 'A filter <select> may not be squeezed narrower than the option it is showing' - so 62 of the 311 'controls' were sentences. (3) Two survivors were labelled by TEMPLATE INTERPOLATION: resume.html builds `const _alab = aria-label="..."` and injects ${_alab} into the tag, an attribute that is real at runtime and invisible to a static reader. The gate therefore SKIPS any control whose attributes carry an unresolved ${...} and REPORTS the count, because a static oracle must decline what it cannot know rather than guess. ★PLACEHOLDER IS NOT ACCEPTED AS A NAME: it vanishes the moment the field is focused, which is exactly when the reminder is needed.

icon-meaning-registry.label: T179: one glyph, one meaning. An icon-only control teaches by repetition - a worker learns that a small x makes something go away, and after the tenth time they stop reading and just tap. That learned reflex is the whole value of an icon and the whole danger, because the moment the same glyph does something ELSE, the reflex fires anyway. CENSUSED every icon-only button across the app pages; five glyphs in use, two carrying trouble. ✕ meant Close, Remove, AND 'Delete resume <title>' - the same mark for 'dismiss this panel' and for 'permanently destroy the resume you spent an hour building'. Fixed by adopting the platform's OWN declared delete glyph (audit-log.html:790 maps edit '✎', delete '🗑'), so the resume delete is a wastebasket and ✕ is left meaning dismiss. × appeared on three project-manager buttons carrying title='Remove' and NO aria-label: ★THE TITLE DOES NOT SAVE IT, because the accessible-name order is aria-labelledby, aria-label, CONTENT, then title - content wins, a screen reader announces 'multiplication sign' and never reaches the title, and on touch there is no hover at all. Each now names what it removes ('Remove scope item <title>', 'Remove link <label>', 'Remove <name> from this project'), since three identical 'Remove' buttons in one list are their own kind of unusable. Also found and named a bare ← in logbook's multi-step entry form, sitting directly beside Save Entry where the difference between going back and saving is the user's whole entry. TWO ASSERTIONS: every icon-only button has an accessible name beyond its glyph, and no glyph carries both a DISMISS meaning and a DESTROY meaning. ★TWO SCOPING DECISIONS, both stated rather than silent: 'Remove' is NOT treated as destroy - taking a link off a list is undoable list-editing, and lumping it with delete would force a second glyph for something users correctly read as dismissal; and icon-ONLY means nothing but the glyph, after an earlier 'at most 3 other characters' allowance flagged six perfectly good icon+label buttons ('⬇ CSV', '⬇ PDF', '🟢 Low') whose visible text already IS their accessible name. Teeth proven on both assertions, the clash half being a true resurrection against the pre-fix ✕.

cold-page-teaches.label: T175: every page introduces itself to a first-time reader. A brand-new account has no assets, no PMs, no history - every list on every page is empty, and an empty page has one job: say what it is FOR and what the first action is. Get it wrong and the reader concludes the product is broken or not for them, on the one visit they are guaranteed to make. WALKED 19 PAGES with a genuinely cold account (created, walked, deleted, residue re-counted at 0 across auth.users, worker_profiles, voice_journal_entries and hive_members - the CASCADE from erasure-path-intact doing exactly what it promises). Every page speaks; two bounce, and they bounce to hive.html, the right destination for someone with no hive rather than a dead end. THE ONE REAL GAP, fixed: analytics-report presented a fully-armed generator - period chips, audience toggle, 'Generate Report' - to a reader with no hive and therefore no data, stating no precondition. Its siblings already refuse that state by name, so it now carries the same gate in the same words ('Reports need a hive... Go to Hive'), hiding BOTH <main> and #ar-print-wrapper - the latter a deliberate sibling of <main> for the print rule, whose empty-state hint otherwise told a hive-less reader to 'Click Generate Report' directly beneath a gate saying Go to Hive. ★THREE INSTRUMENT ERRORS ON THE WAY, NONE BANKED: (1) the probe cleared wh_last_worker as well as the hive and 14 of 19 pages bounced to marketing - pure artifact, since signup SETS that key (index.html:3196) and the shared guard redirects on a missing WORKER NAME, not a missing hive; COLD means no hive, not no identity. (2) The threshold was 'chars < 200', which flagged four of the BEST cold states on the platform - hive.html at 134 ('Create a Hive | Join with Code'), asset-hub at 188, shift-brain at 137, integrations at 193 - pages that are short BECAUSE they are focused; brevity is not emptiness. (3) It read querySelector('main'), and innerText on a display:none element still returns raw text, so on the very page it had just gated it captured the HIDDEN generator and missed the VISIBLE gate outside <main>; it now reads body innerText, which respects visibility. It asserts only the objective - something rendered, nothing threw, the account cleaned up - and PRINTS each page's cold text, because an oracle that grades prose is an oracle that will be wrong about prose.

waiting-is-spoken.label: T181: waiting must SAY it is waiting. A page that fetches its content leaves a gap between paint and data, and what fills that gap is the whole question - a skeleton or a 'Loading...' line says WAIT, while an empty region says THERE IS NOTHING HERE, and a reader acts on that: they leave, they re-tap, or they report missing data that arrives 200ms after they looked away. MEASURED LIVE across 8 signed-in pages with REST throttled 1.2s so the gap is real rather than a race usually lost: ZERO silent gaps - four pages fill it with skeletons (logbook, community, alert-hub, analytics), four with loading text (inventory, asset-hub, marketplace, pm-scheduler). ★IT ASSERTS THE FLOOR, NOT THE VOCABULARY, AND THE NARROWING IS DELIBERATE: the census called waiting 'not yet one product's language', which is true as an observation, but WHICH metaphor a page picks is a design judgement, and failing a page for choosing text over a skeleton would enforce taste across 24 pages and generate dozens of arguable findings. Whether the gap says ANYTHING is not a matter of taste, so the floor is gated and the idiom split is REPORTED - the design question stays visible without a machine deciding it. ★A CENSUS FINDING CORRECTED BY READING THE CODE: analytics appeared to mix metaphors (a skeleton and two spinners in one sample) and does not - the skeleton CONTAINS the spinner (space reserved, action animating inside) and the others mark in-flight generation, which is the declared system working. ★AND THE ORACLE WAS WRONG FIRST: the original silence test read 'during.chars < 120', and teeth-testing it by stripping inventory's Loading lines produced idiom=NOTHING and still PASSED, because the page rendered 389 characters of CHROME while the awaited region sat empty - an absolute threshold over the whole main region measures the furniture, not the gap. It now compares GROWTH, and with that correction the same teeth test fails and names the page.

fab-anchor-stable.label: T184: the one control that must never move. The nav-hub FAB is on every page in the same corner and it is the platform's single piece of muscle memory - a worker's thumb goes there without looking. Every other inconsistency between 24 pages costs a moment of thought; this one costs a MISSED TAP, repeatedly, on the control whose whole job is getting you out of wherever you are. MEASURED AT 390: x = 303, 312 and 318 across eight pages, a 15px spread, while every page carried an identical '#wh-hub { right: 16px }' and an identical 56px FAB. ★THREE HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT SETTLED IT, and that is the part worth keeping: 'a scrollbar is narrowing the viewport' (refuted - innerWidth minus clientWidth was 0 on every page), 'an ancestor transform is creating a containing block' (refuted - the hub is a child of BODY everywhere, no ancestor carried transform/filter/contain/will-change), 'inventory sets scrollbar-width: thin' (refuted - no such declaration). What settled it was a virgin 'fixed; right:0; width:0' probe reporting where the containing block's right edge ACTUALLY sits: 375 on community, 384 on inventory, 390 on logbook - while documentElement.clientWidth read 390 on all three, which is precisely why nothing in the DOM revealed it. THE CAUSE: a fixed right-anchored element is measured from the SCROLLPORT, and the reserved gutter narrows it whether or not a bar is drawn - so the spread was the CROSS-PRODUCT of two unrelated per-page decisions, 'html { scrollbar-gutter: stable }' (components.css:231, linked by some pages) and '::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 6px }' (declared inline by others): 15px reserved -> 303, 6px -> 312, none -> 318. Neither was ever made with the FAB in mind. THE FIX belongs at the altitude that owns the stack - nav-hub.js now injects both halves on every page, beside the reserve and lift rules already there for the same stated reason ('this is one shared bar, so it takes one shared reserve'), and BOTH halves are required because the gutter's width IS the scrollbar's width. Spread now 0 across all eight. ★y IS DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: --wh-fab-lift raises the stack on pages with a fixed bottom element (pm-scheduler rides 65px higher), which is collision avoidance, not drift - forcing it down would put the hub on top of that page's own bottom bar. Also asserts zero pageerrors, since the rule now ships from a file on all 24 pages. RESURRECTION PROVEN: with the injection disabled the gate reports exactly the original 303/312/318 spread, and green on HEAD.

composer-caps-visible.label: T168: a cap must announce itself. A maxlength with NO counter is a silent wall - the textarea simply stops accepting keystrokes, and the person typing does not read that as 'you reached 1000 characters', they read it as a broken keyboard, and they lose the thought they were part-way through writing. The guard is right; the silence is the defect, and that is the whole of T168 - guards that protect without insulting the person they stop. FOUND ON community.html, which had built the right pattern and applied it UNEVENLY: the post composer (2000) and the report box (500) each carried a live 'n / max' counter, and the reply box (1000) carried none - one page, three composers, two of them honest. Added the counter in the page's own idiom, wired its input listener, and reset it at BOTH clear sites (opening a thread, and after a reply posts), because a counter still showing the last message's length is a STALE reading and worse than no counter at all. Live-verified: all three now read '37 / cap' while typing and return to '0 / cap' when cleared, 0 pageerrors. ★THE STATIC SCAN THAT FOUND IT WAS WRONG TWICE FIRST, AND THAT IS WHY THE PROVER IS LIVE: inferring the counter's id from the field's id ('<id>-char-count') reported #post-content as uncounted, when its counter is #post-char-count - the convention is not a convention. A counter is whatever visible element MOVES WHEN YOU TYPE, so the only honest oracle types into the field and watches. Teeth proven by disabling the new counter's id: flagged 'reply-content: no counter', exit 1.

compliance-claim-honesty.label: T171: what an ISO-minded evaluator would check. Swept all 117 public pages for certification and compliance language, and the headline result is good AND worth stating precisely, because 'we claim no certifications' is easy to assert and had never been verified: there is NO WorkHive self-certification anywhere - no SOC 2, no ISO 27001, no 'GDPR-compliant', no HIPAA, no PCI-DSS, no bank-grade or military-grade security. All 30 raw hits were a standard the CUSTOMER is audited against (ISO 9001/14001/45001, DOLE OSHS), a PERSON's credential (TESDA NC II/III, CMRP, PSME/IIEE), or the skill matrix's own 'certified level' vocabulary. ★THE ONE REAL OVERCLAIM WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, NOT A BOAST: dole-iso-audit-trail-from-logbook said WorkHive logbook entries 'SATISFY Clause 10.2', the PM dashboard 'SATISFIES Clause 7.1.5', safety observations 'SATISFY Clause 9.1.1'. A clause is satisfied by an ORGANISATION's management system, evidenced by records - a tool holds the evidence, it cannot confer conformity - and the sentence reads as reassurance, so a plant could walk into a surveillance audit believing a feature had covered them. Rewritten to 'gives you the records Clause 10.2 asks you to retain' / 'evidences Clause 9.1.1', plus a callout stating the distinction outright: same value claimed, no false comfort. Live-verified rendering, 0 pageerrors. TWO ASSERTIONS: (clause) no feature may satisfy/meet/fulfil a NUMBERED clause - and note what is deliberately NOT caught, since 'the digital record satisfies three properties' and 'export patterns that satisfy auditors' both appear on that same page and are both fine, because a record CAN satisfy a property and an export CAN satisfy a sampling need; only a numbered clause as the object is the error; (selfcert) no page may claim a certification the platform lacks - zero today, guard-the-absence, because that is the single most tempting sentence to add to a sales page and the most expensive to be wrong about. Teeth proven on both.

erasure-path-intact.label: T164: the deletion the privacy policy promises must actually be possible. The policy tells a person to email admin@workhiveph.com with a 'Data Rights Request' and their personal data is purged within 30 days while compliance records are retained - a legitimate PDPA path, since a MANUAL route is fine if it is HONORED. Honoring it means the database must let the deletion happen and remove the right things. READ FROM THE LIVE FK GRAPH 2026-08-26 and the model is sound, matching the policy's own stated tension: CASCADE on 10 tables carries personal data away with the account (worker_profiles, voice_journal_entries, resume_documents/versions, worker_achievements, push_subscriptions, mfa_enrollments, the service_* trio) while SET NULL on 20 lets operational records SURVIVE with the identity detached (logbook, pm_completions, asset_nodes, inventory_transactions, community_posts, hive_members, skill_badges...) - the plant keeps its maintenance history, the person stops being in it. Nothing RESTRICTs. THREE ASSERTIONS, each guarding a way this quietly stops working: (blocked) no FK may be RESTRICT/NO ACTION, since one such migration fails every erasure request at the database with no symptom until someone exercises the right; (throws) ★no SET NULL may point at a NOT NULL column - it passes every graph inspection and then RAISES at DELETE time, which is why the gate reads attnotnull and not just confdeltype, because a graph that looks correct is not the same as a deletion that runs; (drifts) no existing table may change action, since CASCADE->SET NULL leaves personal data behind after a purge that reported success while SET NULL->CASCADE destroys the plant history the policy promised to retain - both directions are failures, so the baseline pins the exact mapping. New tables are ADMITTED with their action reported provided they pass blocked and throws, so the gate never stalls schema work. Teeth proven on ALL THREE: a throwaway RESTRICT table and a NOT-NULL SET NULL table (both flagged, then dropped), plus a flipped baseline entry.

review-cadence-kept.label: T162: a promise to re-check is a promise. The competitor-comparison pages are the most perishable content on the platform and they are written WELL - every competitor price dated ('published entry pricing, August 2026'), sourced ('vendor published pricing and feature pages, accessed August 2026'), caveated ('SaaS pricing moves, confirm current terms with the vendor'), and generous to the competition ('the strongest mobile-first product in the category'). Nothing in the comparisons themselves needed fixing. ★THE RISK IS HIDDEN INSIDE THAT QUALITY: each page also prints 'Pricing verified against vendor and directory listings on 5 August 2026' and 'This comparison is reviewed quarterly for pricing and feature accuracy'. Those are not descriptions, they are COMMITMENTS with a clock running - and left alone they decay into the worst kind of claim, an explicit confident promise of currency printed beside prices nobody has re-checked in a year. A reader trusts the page MORE because of that sentence, which is precisely what makes it expensive when it stops being true. THE ASSERTION: where a page states a verification date AND a review cadence, the date must still be inside the cadence it promised (quarterly = 92 days). Measured 2026-08-26: 3 pages, all verified 5 August 2026, 21 days old and comfortably inside. ★THIS GATE IS BUILT TO GO RED - around 5 November 2026 for these three, unless someone re-verifies. That is the point, not a defect: it converts a marketing sentence into a maintained obligation, and the fix when it fires is a real one (re-check the prices and move the date, or delete the commitment). NO GRACE PERIOD, deliberately - the page names its own cadence, so the cadence is the bar; the passing output prints the days remaining so it arrives as a countdown rather than a surprise. Teeth proven by ageing one date to 5 January: 233d against a 92d promise, exit 1.

dated-claim-freshness.label: T161: content ages with supervision, not heroics. A statistic on a public page is a claim a reader - or an answer engine - will repeat, and the dangerous shape is not an OLD year but a year that silently became a LIE: 'as of 2024, the average plant...' was true when written and is quietly false now, because nobody re-reads a sentence that already shipped. ★THE INVENTORY CHANGED WHAT THIS GATE ASSERTS, and that is the lesson: a first pass across 114 public pages flagged 33 'claims 3+ years old' and nearly every one was a CITATION or a STANDARD EDITION - ISO 14224 (2016), CIBSE Guide D:2015, IEC 62305:2010, DENR DAO 2016-08, Nakajima 1988 for the origin of OEE. Those years are part of the source's IDENTITY; flagging them would have demanded the pages stop citing their standards precisely, the exact opposite of the goal, and 33 false findings on the way. SO IT ASSERTS THE SHAPE, NOT THE AGE. Two things rot and neither is a citation: (as-of) a present-tense claim pinned to a past year - 'as of 2024', 'currently ... 2023', 'latest figures 2022' - allowed only within the current year and the two before it, the window SLIDING with the clock so the gate keeps supervising without anyone re-tuning it; and (future) a statistic dated in a year that has not happened, always a typo or a template copy, which reads as authoritative until someone checks. BOTH ARE ZERO TODAY across 115 pages - this is a guard-the-absence gate in the no-clock-driven-push family, because a property that holds by CARE rather than by structure lapses in silence. Teeth proven on both shapes at once: an injected 'as of 2021' and a '2029 survey' -> 2 flagged, exit 1.

structured-data-parity.label: T154: machine-readable truth = human-readable truth. JSON-LD is what an answer engine QUOTES when it cites this platform, and nobody proofreads it because nobody SEES it - so it drifts away from the page underneath and keeps being served, confidently, to the machines that summarize us. TWO CONTRACTS, both born from real drift. FAQ: every FAQPage Question name must appear in the page's visible text - the class T1 caught on the landing page, where the LD still told the provisioning-waitlist story after the page had moved to instant signup; an FAQ rich result PROMISES the page answers that question, so if the words are not there the promise is to content that does not exist (508 questions across 115 public pages, all present). NAME: an Article headline must still be recognisable as the page's own og:title/<title> - FOUND HERE, predictive-alert-thresholds-plants had been retitled to lead with 'ISO 10816 Vibration Thresholds and Predictive Alert Limits', a deliberate move toward the citable standard, while its LD headline kept the older vaguer 'Predictive Alert Thresholds for Industrial Plants', so an answer engine reading the structured data got the version WITHOUT the ISO anchor that makes the page worth citing (synced; 53 headlines now match). ★HowToStep NAMES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GATED, AND THE EXCLUSION IS THE FINDING: a first pass flagged 31 'gaps' across 12 HowTo pages and every one was editorial paraphrase - the OEE guide's LD says 'Measure planned production time' where the page heads that section 'Step 1: Planned Production Time'. Same step, different register. A step name is a LABEL for a procedure; demanding substring identity would have shipped 31 false findings and taught everyone to ignore this gate. The FAQ question and the headline are different in kind - both are read VERBATIM by their consumers, so identity is the actual contract there. Teeth proven on BOTH halves: a fabricated question and a reverted headline, 2 flagged, exit 1.

canonical-resolves.label: T158: a canonical must name a URL that EXISTS. rel=canonical is a claim - 'the real version of this page lives here' - and when the URL it names does not exist, the page tells every crawler its authoritative copy is at nothing. FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-26, VERIFIED AGAINST PRODUCTION rather than inferred: workhiveph.com/workhive/public-feed.html returned 404 while workhiveph.com/public-feed.html returned 200, and FIFTEEN pages shipped the dead form - a /workhive/ segment left over from an earlier deploy path, still being served long after the site moved to the domain root. ★WHY IT SURVIVED EVERY EXISTING CHECK: they all asked whether a canonical was PRESENT, and all 15 were present, well-formed, absolute and unique - and pointed at a 404. Presence is the easy half of a claim; this gate checks the half that costs something. ★THE ONE THAT MATTERED MOST was public-feed, the anonymous shop window and the only one of the 15 meant to be found by strangers: a shared link to it carried a signal saying the real page was elsewhere, at a URL that does not resolve. Now 145 on-site canonicals all name a page that exists. STATIC BY DESIGN - the path IS the defect, and a live HTTP check would make the gate depend on the network to state a fact about a string. TEETH PROVEN by re-breaking public-feed's canonical: 1 flagged, exit 1.

public-feed-dated.label: T158: the public window does not pretend to be fresh. public-feed is the shop window - an anon visitor's first sight of whether anyone is actually here - and a community feed's worst failure is not being QUIET but being quiet while LOOKING live, because a reader who cannot date what they are reading assumes it is current. MEASURED 2026-08-26: 15 public posts, newest 42 DAYS old, ZERO published publicly in the last 30 days, and of 111 posts only 14% are public. On a seeded fixture those numbers say nothing about the product - but they are exactly the state in which a feed either tells the truth or flatters itself, and this one tells the truth: every card carries its date, so a reader judges freshness for themselves. THE ASSERTION IS THE DATE, NOT THE FRESHNESS: freshness is a community outcome no gate can honestly demand, so demanding it would produce a permanent red that teaches nothing; what IS enforceable is that the page never hides how fresh it is. ★WHY GATE SOMETHING THAT ALREADY PASSES: the timestamp is the smallest and most droppable element on a card, and a redesign that tightens the layout and loses it costs nothing visible while quietly converting an honest quiet feed into one that looks live - the single change that would turn this surface from truthful to misleading. TEETH PROVEN by replacing the date span with a literal: 15/15 cards undated, exit 1. It also refuses to pass on ZERO cards, since no undated cards over no cards is a failed load, not a clean bill.

funnel-cls.label: T160: the SEO funnel must not jump while you read it. CLS is where a page loses a searcher without erroring - text settles, the reader's eye is already moving, and the line they were on is somewhere else - and on the funnel it costs twice, because Core Web Vitals feed ranking, so the pages most dependent on search were the ones shifting. MEASURED, ISOLATED, THEN FIXED. The learn template shifted 0.384 CLS at 390, nearly 4x the 0.1 bar. ★THE RECORDED SUSPICION WAS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID SO: the note blamed an element injected at ~1s, and a MutationObserver armed alongside the shift observer recorded NO insertion of any size. The timeline showed a 0.182 shift at 903ms and document.fonts.ready at 907ms; blocking the font stylesheet took CLS to 0.000 while blocking the Tailwind CDN only reached 0.156. The font swap was the whole cause. THE FIX was one parameter - display=swap to display=optional across 113 public pages: optional gives the font ~100ms then never swaps, so the page cannot jump, and measured on a real load it STILL renders Poppins. The only reader who now sees the fallback is on a genuinely slow first load, which is exactly the reader who previously got the jump instead. Verified 0.000 CLS across learn, tools and the landing page. ★IT ASSERTS THE PARAMETER, NOT A CLS NUMBER: a lab CLS reading on loopback is optimistic and noisy, and a gate that fails intermittently gets ignored - the parameter is deterministic and it IS the defect.

tools-cta-honesty.label: T3/T153: the calculator pages state the account requirement. The 60 /tools/ pages are the top of the funnel - a searcher looking for 'OEE calculator' lands on one, and what it promises decides whether the next click is trust or a bounce. MEASURED 2026-08-26 and the human-facing story is HONEST: none of the 60 embeds a calculator (they are landing pages that explain a calculation and hand off) and every one says so plainly - 'free with a WorkHive account. Sign-up takes about 30 seconds.' ZERO still carry the 'no sign-up needed' claim T3 recorded, which linked into a gated page and was false twice over. The gate keeps a fixed claim fixed, because that wording lived in a TEMPLATE - it came back everywhere at once when it came back at all. ★A RECORDED FINDING IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ENFORCE: every one of the 60 declares JSON-LD @type SoftwareApplication with an Offer of price 0 and a url pointing at the LANDING page, so a search or answer engine reads 'there is a free web application here', follows the url, and finds a page about an application that lives somewhere else. The human CTA is honest; the MACHINE claim overclaims. Pointing that url at the app would make it true in one line, but rewriting the structured data of 60 pages changes how the platform is presented in search - an outward-facing decision nobody can quietly reverse - so it is written up for Ian rather than done. Teeth-proven by restoring the exact old wording.

share-card-completeness.label: T156: a shared link should look intentional. T125 established what sharing here actually looks like - workers paste links into Viber and Messenger group chats - which makes the Open Graph card the first thing most people see of a page, often before the page itself. THE FINDING: 60 of ~116 public pages shipped NO og:image and no twitter:card, and they were all the /tools/ CALCULATORS - the top of the funnel, the pages most likely to be shared by a worker who just used one. Every one rendered as a bare grey link while the learn cluster's 53 articles rendered a proper card. public-feed had an image and a title but no og:description, so its card showed a headline, a picture, and whatever text the platform chose to guess. Fixed by reusing the SAME asset the learn cluster already uses rather than inventing a second one: two social images drift and one ends up stale. ★IT CHECKS THE IMAGE FILE EXISTS, not merely that the tag does - a card pointing at a missing PNG renders exactly like a card with no image, and the tag being present makes it look handled, which is the worst combination because nobody re-checks a field that is filled in. App pages are deliberately out of scope: a signed-in surface behind an auth wall is not shared to a group chat. Teeth-proven both ways - card removed RED, image pointed at a missing file RED.

long-fetch-bounded.label: T146: a hang must END, not spin forever. A fetch to an AI or transcription edge function is the one a plant floor will hang - a dead spot, a cold function, a slow uplink - and without a bound there is no failure at all, just a control stuck in its working state saying nothing. That is the eternal-skeleton shape wearing a spinner, and it is worse than an error because an error at least tells someone what to do next. THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST RUN: written after finding voice-journal's transcribeBlob unbounded, it immediately found THREE MORE - report-sender's transcribe, voice-handler's transcribe, and analytics' ORCHESTRATOR, the longest-running call on the platform, where a supervisor waiting on a report could not tell 'still thinking' from 'never coming back'. All four now route through the platform's own fetchWithTimeout rather than a second hand-rolled controller: it already owns the AbortController, the transport-retry policy and the null-on-abort contract. ★THE BOUNDS ARE SIZED FOR THE SLOWEST LEGITIMATE SUCCESS, NOT A DEVELOPER'S PATIENCE - 45s for a long spoken entry over a weak uplink, 120s for a full AI analytics phase - because a timeout tuned short turns working software into a lottery for the plants furthest from the server. Deliberately scoped to slow-by-nature endpoints: a quick REST read is already covered by whQueryTimeout, and demanding a timeout on every call in the codebase would be noise. ★CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (T40): this gate accepted a bare AbortController or a bare `signal:` as proof of a bound — and those are a CANCEL BUTTON, somewhere for a person to press, not a clock that fires on its own. analytics-report carried both and was still unbounded: the 22-page retry sweep graded it SILENT, sitting on 'Compiling analytics across all 4 phases' forever under a read outage because nothing would ever abort it if the reader simply waited — and this gate passed that page every run. A real bound now requires a TIMER: fetchWithTimeout, AbortSignal.timeout, a setTimeout that calls abort, or a Promise.race against a timed promise. The controller may still sit beside those (it is how the abort is delivered) but can no longer stand in for them. A --selftest pins all five cases, the first being the pre-fix analytics-report source, which must be RED.

learn-graph.label: T152: the teaching cluster is navigable in BOTH directions. 53 articles only teach as a cluster if a reader can move through them, and two different failures break that while being invisible to each other. AN ORPHAN is an article no hub link reaches: it exists, it is indexed, a searcher can land on it, and nobody browsing the library will ever find it - writing it was work that reaches nobody. A DEAD END is an article that links onward to nothing: a reader who finishes it has to go back and start again, which is where a session ends. Measured: 53 articles, 53 reachable from the hub, ZERO orphans, ZERO dead ends, and the hub links to nothing missing. The gate keeps it that way, because adding an article and forgetting the hub entry is a one-line omission nobody notices. ★IT ALSO CHECKS THE REVERSE OF AN ORPHAN - a hub link to an article that does not exist - because a library index offering a guide that 404s is worse than not listing it, and this cluster has been renamed before. ★AND ONWARD LINKS MUST REACH OTHER LEARN ARTICLES, not merely somewhere: a page whose only outbound link is a signup CTA is a dead end for a reader who came to learn, however many links it technically has. Teeth-proven by renaming one hub slug, which fired BOTH arms at once - the article became an orphan and the hub gained a promise it could not keep.

answer-presence.label:
T151: a searcher's question answered above the fold, swept across all 53 learn articles. Somebody arrives from a search result with a question the snippet promised this page answers; what they meet in the first screen decides whether they stay, and the failure mode is not a broken page but one that opens with throat-clearing and buries the answer four scrolls down. ★THE ORACLE IS ANSWER-PRESENCE, NOT META-VERBATIM - T151 learned that the hard way when an earlier pass checked whether the meta description's words appeared on the page and produced a false red, because a description SUMMARIZES rather than quotes. Four assertions per article: an H1 exists; substantive opening prose follows it; that opening carries a distinctive term from the title; and a freshness stamp is visible, because a searcher landing on undated maintenance guidance cannot tell if it is current. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY VERDICT WAS TRUSTED, each found by READING the flags rather than acting on them: a {3,} filter silently dropped this platform's most important short terms (PM, AI, OEE) so an article opening 'Most Philippine plants run PMs' read as off-topic; an exact match called 'measurement' a miss for a title saying 'Measuring'; and scanning only

elements flagged the WorkHive-vs-MaintainX page, which opens with a textbook answer ('Choose MaintainX if... Choose WorkHive if...') written in a

of lines - the

tags it found were the byline and a repeated pricing disclaimer, so the gate read the furniture and missed the answer. It now reads VISIBLE TEXT, and allows one paragraph of runway, because enforcing sentence-one would legislate prose style rather than measure arrival. All 53 pass. Mutation-proven both ways: burying an answer behind preamble goes RED, and stripping a freshness stamp goes RED.

hive-rename-reaches.label: T140: a rename must reach the OTHER devices. ★THE TRAJECTORY'S RECORDED PREMISE WAS WRONG IN BOTH HALVES, and this gate is the correction. Its basis read that hive rename 'does not exist - no UI, no update path (grep: zero rename/hive_name edit sites in hive.html)' and concluded that no stale-name propagation class could exist. hive.html DOES rename a hive, and a live test showed the consequence: after another device renamed the plant, the measured session kept showing the OLD name on its board and in its chrome, because every page trusts localStorage.wh_hive_name and nothing re-read hives.name - a cache written at join/switch time, so 'eventually' can mean weeks. A grep that misses one line turns a real defect into a recorded absence. FIXED CENTRALLY: whReconcileHiveName (utils.js) asks the server what the hive is called once per load and corrects the cache and the glass when they disagree, best-effort by construction (a failed check keeps the cached name, which is what the page would have shown anyway) and inside the board's allSettled so it can never stop a page loading. ★THE TEST'S SHAPE IS THE ONLY ONE THAT CAN SEE THIS: the rename happens OUTSIDE the measured session, straight into the database, exactly as another supervisor's browser would - renaming through the same page would prove only that a page can update itself. Three assertions, the third being the one that matters: cache corrected, title corrected, and the old name NOWHERE on the page, because chrome that fixes its title while a sidebar keeps the old name is still showing two truths. Resurrection: all three RED pre-fix. The hive's name is restored in a finally block and the restore is verified.

approval-race.label: T145: two supervisors, one pending item, ONE outcome. The sharpest concurrency case on this platform - both press Approve within the same second - and the walk found it already correct, needing no fix. This gate exists so it STAYS correct: the optimistic guard is one .eq('status','pending') away from being deleted by somebody tidying a query, and the failure is invisible in normal use because you only meet it when two people happen to act at once. ★A REAL RACE, NOT TWO AWAITED CALLS: awaiting the first update before firing the second proves nothing, since the second simply sees the finished state. Both are dispatched concurrently and settled together - the only shape that exercises a guard, and this codebase already carries a scar from a double-submit test that awaited its own clicks. Four assertions: exactly one update reports a changed row; the other reports ZERO rows (a no-op the UI can explain, not an error); the item ends approved once by one person; and the audit records ONE approval, because a log showing two approvals of one thing is a log nobody can use. ★IT PICKS ITS HIVE BY THE PROPERTY IT NEEDS: the first version pinned a fixture with ONE supervisor and SKIPped - a race test that cannot find two racers is not a pass, and a pinned hive would have quietly disabled this gate the day the fixture changed. Measured live: Christine Dizon won, Pablo Aguilar got zero rows, one DB outcome, one audit entry.

oc-guard-speaks.label: T138: a concurrency guard that says nothing is a LOST EDIT. An optimistic-concurrency guard filters an UPDATE on the row's updated_at so a write loses if somebody else changed the record first - that is the easy half. The half that decides whether it HELPS is what happens next: if nothing checks that ZERO ROWS changed, the update silently does nothing, the form closes, and the person walks away believing they saved work that no longer exists. A guard that returns without speaking is WORSE than no guard, because it converts a visible conflict into an invisible loss. ★THE CENSUS CORRECTED THIS TRAJECTORY'S OWN RECORD: the basis read that logbook amends, community post edits and PM scope edits were 'presumed LAST-WRITE-WINS'. They are not. There are TEN hand-rolled guards across EIGHT pages (asset-hub, community, founder-console, integrations, logbook, platform-actions, pm-scheduler, project-manager x3) plus inventory through the central ocUpdate - eleven protected edit surfaces, not two - and every one of the ten detects the zero-row case AND tells the person. The gate does NOT demand migration to ocUpdate: that is ten rewrites of live edit paths for a refactor, and the property that protects a person is 'the guard SPEAKS', not 'the guard is shared'. The install-the-guard lesson still governs anything NEW - reach for ocUpdate first - and this exists so a hand-rolled one cannot ship silent. ★IT WOULD RATHER MISS THAN LIE: the window is the 40 lines after the filter, so a guard whose reporting lives further away reads as a miss, which is the safe direction for a gate whose other failure mode is a false accusation about working code. Teeth-proven with an injected silent guard.

inventory-listing-handoff.label: T104 / T30: the sell hop keeps its intent. inventory offers 'Sell surplus' only on rows holding 3x+ their minimum, with the reason in the control's own title, and hands off to marketplace.html?post=1&from_inventory=<id>; marketplace RE-FETCHES the row server-side, so the prefill is authoritative and cannot be spoofed through the URL - a person can only list from inventory their own session may read. VERIFIED-GOOD then locked: a handoff that drops what the system already knows makes the seller retype it, which is the same intent-loss as a wall that forgets where you were going, landing on the least-motivated user in the funnel - someone listing a spare part for the first time. Measured: title, part number, quantity (into the description), category classification and the source id all arrive. ★THE MOST INTERESTING ASSERTION IS AN ABSENCE: the PRICE is deliberately NOT prefilled and the gate holds it that way, because what a plant PAID is not what it should ASK, and a guessed price is the one field a seller must own - prefilling it would be the system making a commercial decision on their behalf. The mutation test confirmed that arm is independent: with the prefill disabled every other assertion flipped RED while priceLeftToTheSeller stayed green. The prover picks a real surplus row by the same 3x rule the button uses rather than hardcoding an id, so a reseed cannot turn it into a false red, and it SKIPs cleanly when the fixture holds no surplus row.

listing-preview.label: T100: see it as a buyer before it is a commitment. The walk found the AI listing assist SOUND - it names its own inputs and invented no specs from a bare title - and recorded exactly ONE gap: a seller could not see their listing AS A BUYER WILL before publishing. Posting is a commitment: it spends a credit hold, it goes to moderation, and it is the first thing a stranger judges the seller by, so J3's bar applies. ★THIS GATE EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIX FAILED TWICE, SILENTLY, in ways only a CLICK could find. (1) The handler called getElementById at script-parse time and returned early when the composer was not yet in the DOM - the button rendered perfectly and did NOTHING: declared, never wired. (2) Rewritten as a delegated listener, it was inserted INSIDE the submit handler's function body, so it only registered once a seller pressed Post - the one moment a preview is useless. BOTH loaded with ZERO console errors, and a gate that merely checked the button EXISTS would have been green through both. Four assertions, all behavioural: it opens; it shows the draft the seller typed; a blank price reads 'Negotiable' while a filled one renders through whFmtPeso (a preview that formats money its own way is showing the seller something the buyer will not see); and it closes again, because a preview that traps you is a modal. Resurrection BOTH ways: RED with no preview control at all, RED again with the listener deliberately un-wired.

no-probe-residue.label: T136: demo and probe content must never read as real. Every walk in this program writes marked rows and deletes them, but that discipline is per-walk and per-author - it holds exactly as well as the last person's memory. A BROAD sweep on 2026-08-26 found 245 marker rows surviving earlier sessions: 3 in VOICE_JOURNAL_ENTRIES (probe transcripts AND the AI's replies to them, in the platform's most private surface, inside a worker's own journal); 1 in LOGBOOK.knowledge ('probe: checked, within tolerance' in a real-looking entry - T136's earlier pass had found and removed the pm_completion twin of this and missed the logbook copy: one probe, two homes); and 241 in HIVE_AUDIT_LOG. ★THE AUDIT ROWS ARE THE LESSON: they were MINE, from the same day. My pending-submission prover created probe assets and deleted them, and the audit trigger honestly recorded every deletion - TRUE rows describing objects that were never real, in a compliance-class table the retention gate correctly forbids any scheduled job from purging. A probe that touches an AUDITED table leaves residue its own cleanup cannot reach, because the residue lands in a DIFFERENT table than the one it wrote to; removing it needed a deliberate scoped delete, never a cron. AND THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST RUN: after a targeted WH-T108B cleanup it still found 34 rows under a different marker (WH-EFFECT-PROBE, dating back to 2026-08-18) that the scoped delete had missed. Scoped to user-facing tables and deliberately NOT the seeder's fixtures - demo DATA is legitimate, and a gate that could not tell seeded plant data from probe residue would fire forever.

page-contrast.label: T116: the contrast zero that IS certified, and the one page where it is not. tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs is a mature TWO-ORACLE instrument - axe for WCAG 2.x, live-state-runner's APCA maths for this platform's dark surfaces - and it had NO GATE, so a contrast regression was invisible to the board. ★READING THE INCOMPLETE SET IS WHY THIS EXISTS: axe reports 0 violations across 26 pages, and alone that is a FALSE 100, because it also reports 1,534 INCOMPLETE - 'element's background color could not be determined' - since axe cannot see behind composited alpha or a gradient, which is most of this platform. A zero over an abstention that large means nothing by itself. WHAT MAKES IT REAL is the second oracle: APCA measured 3,007 text nodes with 0 failing, 0 inconclusive and NO truncation, and on 23 of 24 pages its denominator is LARGER than axe's abstention set - so the nodes axe declined to judge have a verdict from an instrument built to composite alpha, average gradient stops and resolve background-clip:text glyphs. ★THE EXCEPTION IS NAMED RATHER THAN ROUNDED AWAY: on assistant, axe left 18 incomplete while APCA measured 15. The counts are in DIFFERENT UNITS (elements vs text nodes) so it is not proof of three unjudged nodes - it is the one page where the covering argument is not clearly safe, recorded as a residual instead of folded into the green. Asserts violations 0, APCA failing 0, inconclusive 0, no truncation (a cap must never hide under '0 failing'), and refuses to grade a --teeth run, which plants deliberately failing nodes into the same report file.

width-utilisation.label: T114 + T115: the widths between phone and desk. T114 asks whether 768 - the awkward middle nobody designs for - is coherent; T115 recorded a nit at 1920 of prose lines running 104-131ch, well past the 45-90ch of a comfortable reading measure. ★THE RECORDED NIT WAS THE INSTRUMENT, and that is this gate's main finding: every one of those long 'prose lines' was a SOURCE CHIP - 'Live - refreshed on load - Based on...', 'Saved snapshot, computed 5h ago - ...' - the platform's freshness metadata, SCANNED in a glance rather than read left-to-right. Capping those at a reading measure would WRAP them, turning a one-line label into three, which is worse than what it was meant to fix. With chips excluded the longest genuine prose line is 59-93ch: inside the comfortable range, logbook@768 marginally over at 93. There is no line-length defect, and a future session should not go hunting one. WHAT THE FILL NUMBERS SAY: at 768 the pages fill 87.5-100% of the viewport, so the middle width is used rather than treated as a big phone; at 1920 index, analytics and pm-scheduler run full width while hive (35%) and logbook (57%) cap their column - a legitimate readability choice, recorded so it stays visible. The ratchet holds longest-prose-line per page+width; FILL is reported but NOT gated, because 'uses the width' is a design judgement and a gate demanding a fill percentage would be enforcing an opinion. The ch measure is taken from each block's OWN font metrics via canvas, not guessed from a max-width.

money-formatting.label: T133: absent is not zero, especially in pesos. whFmtPeso exists for one recorded reason - Number(null) is 0 and finite, so a null amount slips through as a confident 0.00. A filed top-up of PHP300 once rendered as PHP0.00 and a ledger line of unknown value rendered as +0, a sentence saying the entry moved nothing. The helper prints a GAP for absent and still prints 0 for a real zero, because a person can act on 'we do not know' and cannot act on a wrong number. THE FINDINGS: founder-console - the owner's own cockpit - had ZERO adoption and a formatter that was literally Number(n || 0), the bug itself, while the same file carried a note saying a money number frozen at zero 'does not read as by design, it reads as a feed that died'; its GCash top-up row had no null guard at all. marketplace-seller's earnings formatter used Number(n), so an absent figure printed NaN on the dashboard of the person being paid. marketplace's service picker guarded <= 0, which catches null but NOT undefined - Number(undefined) is NaN and NaN <= 0 is FALSE - so an absent rate fell through as NaN to a buyer. All routed through the helper. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST RUN FLAGGED FOUR FALSE POSITIVES and they were NOT acted on: a ternary spans lines, so the GUARDED FALLBACK half of `whFmtPeso(n) : '+Number(n||0)` looked hand-rolled because the helper sat on the line above. 'Fixing' those would have damaged correct code whose fallback exists so the page still renders when utils.js has not loaded. It now reads a window and honours an explicit null branch. Scoped to money surfaces by design - a gate policing every peso sign would catch option labels and prose and be switched off.

counted-noun-ratchet.label: T131: software that cannot count to one. '1 entries found', '1 assets', '1 parts' - individually trivial, collectively the thing that makes a product feel unfinished, and n=1 is not an edge case here: it is what a filtered list shows the moment a search gets specific. WHAT IS COUNTED is a count interpolated straight into a plural noun with NO singular branch nearby, and the count must be one that can GENUINELY be 1 - a .length, a *Count, a *_count, a *Total. Deliberately NOT cases like ${period} days, which is 30/60/90 by construction and never reads '1 days': the first pass of this measurement counted 82 that way, and a census padded with cases that cannot occur produces a number nobody trusts and a gate everyone learns to ignore. The honest figure was 30. ZERO IS NOT THE GOAL and this ratchet must not be read as demanding it - the sites span 13 files, mostly secondary and admin surfaces, and rewriting all of them in one sweep would be a large unreviewed change to render paths for a grammar nit. What was FIXED is the one a worker meets daily: the counter under the logbook's search box, which said '1 entries found' the moment a search narrowed to a single result. Baseline 27 after that fix; growth is the failure. The idiom to use is the platform's own, already present in several files - ${n} asset${n === 1 ? '' : 's'} - no helper and no new dependency. Teeth-proven by injecting one new offender: RED, then removed.

idle-network.label: T118: what a page costs while NOBODY IS TOUCHING IT. A worker at 8% battery at the end of a shift and a tablet left running on a workshop wall are the same measurement. index had been measured once; the rest of the roster never had, and a polling loop is exactly the cost nobody notices while developing on mains power. MEASURED: eight pages, 8s to settle then 75s of watching with no interaction. Seven are completely silent; alert-hub makes ~11 requests per 75s from setInterval(loadAll, 60000) - correct for a board somebody is watching, and roughly 500 requests an hour if left on a wall. ★THE WINDOW MUST OUTLAST THE SLOWEST POLL OR A ZERO MEANS NOTHING: the first run watched for 45 SECONDS and reported ZERO on all eight pages, including alert-hub, whose 60s poll simply never fired inside the window - the cleanest-looking result in the sweep was the busiest page. ★AND THE PAUSE IS PROVEN, NOT TRUSTED: what makes a 60s foreground poll defensible rather than a battery leak is that it stops when nobody is looking, so the probe HIDES THE TAB and asserts the requests stop - measured, 0 requests in 75s hidden. A poll still running in a backgrounded tab would be invisible to every foreground measurement. ★WHAT IT CANNOT SEE, said plainly so a zero is not misread: WEBSOCKETS. Supabase realtime holds a socket open and its frames are not HTTP requests, so a zero here means 'no polling', never 'no activity' - and an already-open socket is genuinely cheaper than repeated polling, making this a scope note rather than a gap to close by inflating the number.

composer-audience.label: T166: 'who sees this?' answered where it is WRITTEN.
