Every write surface makes a person decide how candid to be, and that decision happens at the composer - answering it on a welcome card, a help page or a toast after the fact is answering it too late or to the wrong person. THE FINDING: voice-journal.html had ZERO audience statements while being the platform's MOST private surface - voice_journal_entries carries auth.uid() = auth_uid on read, update AND delete, so nobody else in the hive can reach a single row. The only place a worker was ever told lived on hive.html's join-flow welcome card: seen once, on a different page, at a moment they were not writing anything personal. A privacy guarantee a person cannot see is one they cannot rely on. THE WORDING IS READ OFF THE RLS, NEVER FROM MEMORY, and this trajectory carries the scar - a welcome card written the same week claimed the Voice Journal was the ONLY worker-private surface while the policies said otherwise (skill_profiles, badges and exam_attempts are auth_uid-scoped too). So the gate checks BOTH ENDS: the claim on the page AND the policies in the database, failing if a page claims a privacy the policies do not give - a promise the database does not keep being worse than no promise at all. Deliberately a SHORT NAMED LIST of surfaces where a person commits words others might read, not every input on the platform: a gate demanding an audience label on search boxes and filters would be switched off within a week. Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix voice-journal.

retention-matches-policy.label: T137: a promise to KEEP is as checkable as a promise to delete. The privacy policy states that compliance records (DOLE OSHS, ISO audit logs) are retained 10 years for general records and 15 for incident investigations - and this trajectory has ALREADY caught the platform making a retention promise it did not keep, claiming a 90-day retention of voice recordings when the product stores no audio at all. Measured 2026-08-26 and this promise holds: five retention crons exist and every one purges a TECHNICAL or DERIVED table (achievement_xp_log, agent_memory, embedding_cache, gateway_audit_log, hive_route_calls); none touches a compliance-class record, and hive_audit_log holds 9,019 rows with nothing scheduled to remove them. WHY IT NEEDS A GATE AND NOT A NOTE: that agreement is currently an accident of nobody having written the cron. Purging old logbook rows to save space is exactly what somebody adds on a slow afternoon, and the moment it lands a legal document about DOLE OSHS and ISO compliance becomes false - silently, with no user-visible symptom, because the records that would prove a plant's maintenance history in a regulatory dispute are precisely the ones nobody notices missing until they are needed. Asserts that no scheduled job deletes from logbook, pm_completions or hive_audit_log while the policy makes that promise; if the retention policy genuinely changes, the policy text and this list change together, which is the point of pairing them. It SKIPS rather than passes if the policy sentence disappears, so the gate cannot go quietly vacuous. Deliberately does NOT assert record AGES - nothing is 10 years old yet, so that check would pass forever without measuring anything. Teeth-proven by scheduling a logbook purge cron: RED, then removed.

legal-claim-honesty.label: T172: the terms may not promise what the product lacks. terms-of-service said, in two places, 'You may export your data at any time and delete your account' and 'You may stop using WorkHive and delete your account at any time'. NEITHER SURFACE EXISTS - there is no export-my-data control (T77) and no account-deletion door (T164). A marketing page overclaiming is bad; a TERMS page overclaiming is a promise at legal weight, made to a Philippine user exercising a PDPA right, and it is the document they would point to. THE FIX WAS NOT TO DELETE THE RIGHT: the right is real and the privacy policy already documents how it is honoured - email admin@workhiveph.com with the subject 'Data Rights Request'. The terms now say exactly that, and say plainly it is handled by hand rather than through a button. Same right, true sentence. Both the HTML and its .md twin were corrected, because a promise surviving in either copy is a promise still unkept. THE ASSERTION: no legal surface may claim a SELF-SERVE capability the product does not have - and each banned phrasing is PAIRED WITH THE CONTROL that would make it true, so the day somebody ships account deletion the claim becomes allowed by the same gate that forbids it now. NOT A PROSE LINT: it checks specific self-serve promises against specific missing controls, because a gate that graded legal writing would produce false reds forever and teach everyone to ignore it. Resurrection: RED on all three pre-fix claims.

name-keyed-aggregates.label: T127: the day two machines share a name. SEVEN reliability functions group logbook rows by the machine NAME and none uses asset_node_id - get_mtbf_by_machine, get_mttr_by_machine, get_failure_frequency, get_downtime_pareto, get_repeat_failures, get_oee_by_machine, compute_anomaly_signals. Names are not unique: this database already holds 24 duplicate asset names inside a single hive - Caterpillar 3516B twice, Cummins QSK60-G4 twice - which is not a data-entry mistake but the ordinary reality of a plant that bought two identical generators. WHY THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT TODAY IS LUCK, NOT DESIGN, and it was measured: ZERO machine strings map to more than one asset_node_id and ZERO duplicated names appear in the logbook at all, because nobody has yet logged a repair against the SECOND Caterpillar. The moment somebody does, its failures merge into the first one's MTBF, its downtime joins the first one's Pareto bar, and its anomalies are scored against a history that is not its own - silently, inside numbers used to decide maintenance strategy for a machine that might be about to fail. THIS GATE DOES NOT RE-KEY THOSE FUNCTIONS: that is a real design change with blast radius across every analytics surface and deserves to be decided rather than slipped in. It makes the failure LOUD instead of silent, failing the moment a machine string maps to more than one asset OR a duplicated asset name appears as a logbook machine. Teeth-proven by staging the exact future - a repair logged on the second duplicate-named asset - which turned it RED, then removing it. A CLEAN RUN IS NOT AN ALL-CLEAR: it means the collision has not happened yet. The 98% of logbook rows already carrying asset_node_id are what would make the re-key cheap when it is decided.

supervisor-hygiene.label: T190/T56: authority must not outlive membership, and a hive must not lose it. Two invariants, opposite failures, both about who can approve things in a plant. (outlived) A member kicked or deactivated must not still carry role 'supervisor' - authority surviving departure is the quiet kind of permission rot, because nothing changes on screen until the day that row is consulted for an approval, and team churn in a plant is continuous. (orphaned) Every hive must retain at least ONE active supervisor - without one nobody can approve an asset, clear a report or promote anyone, so the work does not stop loudly, it just quietly cannot be completed, and the remedy is the exact thing that is missing. T56 named this the last-supervisor case, and hive.html's transfer-then-leave flow exists so it cannot happen. MEASURED: 3 hives, 4 active supervisors, ZERO departed members holding the role, ZERO hives without one. ★IT READS STATE, NOT CODE, and that is the point: hive.html's guard is a claim about a PATH, while this is a claim about the WORLD - whatever combination of kicks, role changes, transfers and direct writes happened, the invariant either holds now or it does not. ★ON A SEEDED FIXTURE THIS IS A WEAK SIGNAL BY ITSELF and that is worth saying: 3 hives is not a stress test, so its value is as a standing invariant that fires the first time a churn path breaks it, not as proof the churn paths are correct today. Teeth proven by kicking a supervisor (caught by name) and restoring; fixture re-counted unchanged.

migrations-additive.label: T199: a migration must not break the page already open. Deploys happen while people are working - a worker who opened the logbook at 13:58 and presses Save at 14:00 is running the OLD page JavaScript against the NEW schema, and whether that write lands is decided entirely by whether the migration was ADDITIVE. Adding a nullable column is invisible to the open page; dropping one, renaming one, or making one NOT NULL without a default is not - the in-flight write fails at the worst possible moment, after the person has typed everything. MEASURED across 561 migrations: only NINE non-additive operations exist in the whole history, every one a deliberate named cleanup from May-June 2026 (the Phase 5b/5c retirement of the old assets model, four drop_phantom_columns_* migrations removing columns that were never real, one NOT NULL to make a benchmarks upsert key work, and the Stripe removal), and NONE since 2026-06-30. ★IT IS AN ALLOWLIST, NOT A COUNT: those nine are grandfathered BY NAME with their reason, so the gate still fires on a new non-additive migration even while an old one is deleted - a count would silently absorb that. ★WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not prove a deploy is safe, since an additive migration can still break an open page through a changed CHECK constraint or a trigger, and the deploy-window question (PHT night rather than 2pm on a workday) is a runbook decision, not a schema property. It catches the one class objectively readable from the SQL. Teeth proven with an injected DROP COLUMN.

absence-guard-reachable.label: T198: an 'it could not be computed' branch must be REACHABLE. A page that distinguishes 'computed, and the answer is nothing' from 'we could not compute it' has done the hard part of honest degradation - so the failure this catches is subtler and worse than not having the branch: the branch EXISTS, somebody wrote it deliberately, and the fallback hands it a value that can never trigger it. THE INSTANCE THAT PROVED THE CLASS: project-manager's renderCpm() guards `if (!cp)` and prints 'The critical path could not be computed right now', while its client fallback returned critical_path: { item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {} } - AN EMPTY OBJECT IS TRUTHY, so the guard never fired on the path it was written for, and a shutdown project whose real schedule is '12d, 7 of 7 items on the critical path' rendered as 'CRITICAL PATH 0d - 0 of 7 items' with a full Gantt beneath it. Fixed with critical_path: null. THE ASSERTION: where a consumer's if (!x) branch says something could not be computed, no producer in that file may assign x an empty-but-truthy value - measured at 11 such guards platform-wide and ZERO defeated, so the CLASS is extinct rather than the one instance being patched. ★AN EMPTY ARRAY AS A PLAIN DEFAULT IS NOT THIS: parts: [], rows: [], work: [] are correct ways to say 'none', and a first sweep flagged 33 of them; what makes it a defect is a consumer that DISTINGUISHES uncomputed from empty and a producer that collapses the distinction. ★AND THE DETECTOR FAILED ITS OWN RESURRECTION TEST FIRST - its producer pattern could not match a value containing nested braces, and the real defect contained slack_per_item: {}, so it reported 0 with the bug present. A detector that cannot find the bug it was written for is worse than none; it now allows one nesting level and is proven to go 1 -> 0 across the fix.

edge-down-admits-it.label: T198: a dead edge fn must not become a confident answer. Edge functions fail independently of the database - a cold start times out, one is mid-deploy, a region hiccups - and the page keeps working, which is the point of the client fallback; the danger is the fallback filling the gap with a POSITIVE-LOOKING ZERO. ★MEASURED AND REAL: project-manager's clientRollup returned critical_path: { item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {} } when project-progress was unreachable, and renderCpm() carries a PJ8 guard written for exactly this - if (!cp) prints 'The critical path could not be computed right now' - but AN EMPTY OBJECT IS TRUTHY, so the guard never fired on the path it was written for. With the function down, a shutdown project whose real schedule is '12d, 7 of 7 items on the critical path' rendered as 'CRITICAL PATH 0d - 0 of 7 items on critical path' with a full Gantt beneath it. Not a blank and not an error: a confident INVERSION, on the screen a supervisor uses to plan a plant outage, telling them nothing is critical for a project where everything is. Fixed by returning critical_path: null so the existing message speaks - every consumer already used optional chaining. ★THE EVM HALF OF THAT SAME FALLBACK HAD ITS MARKER (evm_reason: 'unavailable') AND THE CPM HALF WAS LEFT BEHIND - the sibling-fix pattern this codebase keeps meeting. Asserts BOTH directions: with the function forced to 503 the pane says it could not compute, and with it up the pane still renders a real schedule, because a gate that only checked the failure case would pass on a pane that is permanently broken. Resurrection-proven against the pre-fix empty object.

media-fails-alone.label: T197: storage down must not take the write with it. Supabase Storage is a separate service that fails independently, so the question is whether the feature that ATTACHES a photo takes the whole submission down with it - a seller who has written a listing, priced it and typed a description should not lose that because a bucket is refusing writes. Same decoupling ethic T12 established for the voice journal, where an AI 429 was losing the worker's typed note: the SECONDARY enrichment must never destroy the PRIMARY work. MEASURED with every bucket write forced to 500 while the database stays up: the picker announces the real reason ('storage unavailable') instead of swallowing it, #post-image-url is CLEARED so the listing submits with no photo rather than a broken link, and the rest of the form is untouched and still submittable. ★IT INJECTS A STORAGE-ONLY OUTAGE, not a general one - failing everything proves nothing about isolation; the point is that ONE service is down and the others carry on, which is the only shape that distinguishes a decoupled feature from a lucky one. ★AND THE PROVER FAILED ITS OWN FIRST TEETH TEST, which is the reusable part: it checked toast.offsetHeight > 0, and the toast CONTAINER is always in the DOM, so an EMPTY toast counted as 'the user was told' and silencing the error still passed. It now requires the toast to contain actual words - a string is not an announcement until it has some. ★THE READ SIDE ADDED 2026-08-28: everything above is about ATTACHING a photo while storage is down; the other half is a photo already STORED and now unreachable, which five render sites across four marketplace pages emitted as a bare with no error handling. Measured before assuming, and the roadmap's premise was wrong - it predicted 'layout wreckage', but a failed image holds its box exactly (218x164, naturalWidth 0, complete true) because the card's CSS sizes it, so nothing reflows. What the reader loses is not geometry but MEANING: a broken-image glyph that never says whether the listing has no photo, the photo is gone, or the page is broken. One capture-phase document listener in utils.js (error does not bubble but it DOES capture) now replaces an unreachable STORED photo with a labelled box that keeps the failed image's own dimensions and names which photo is missing via its alt text - scoped by src to /storage/v1/object/ so a decorative logo is never relabelled 'photo unavailable'. Teeth-proven both ways: neutering the fallback fails it, and removing the scope guard so decorative images get eaten fails it too.

permission-in-context.label: T46/T105: ask for push when the worker WANTS it. A notification prompt at first paint is the fastest way to lose the permission permanently - the person has no reason to say yes yet, they say no, and the browser remembers that answer forever with no in-app way to undo it. There is no second chance, so WHEN the prompt fires matters more than how the feature is built. MEASURED - two call sites, both exemplary: marketplace-seller's svcEnablePush() runs from an onclick ('Turning on…') behind online/support/signed-in checks and refuses honestly when the answer is no ('Alerts stay off until you allow notifications'); voice-handler's _requestPushPerm() fires ONLY when the worker has VERBALLY opted in (_isPushOptInReply) and only while the state is still 'default', inside the open user-gesture window, so a prior denial is never re-prompted. TWO ASSERTIONS: every requestPermission() sits behind a permission-state check or an explicit user action, and no call site is reachable from a load-time path. ★A LOOKBACK WINDOW CANNOT SEE A GESTURE BINDING, and the first version proved it by calling a correctly-gated prompt 'bare': svcEnablePush IS bound to an onclick 350 lines earlier, far outside any sane window. The binding is a property of the enclosing FUNCTION, not of nearby text, so the gate now resolves the function name and asks whether the file wires it to a click anywhere - the same structural-over-proximity correction that keeps coming up. ★IT CHECKS THE ASK, NOT THE FEATURE: whether push is wired, which VAPID key, whether the message is good all belong elsewhere; this is only about the one moment that cannot be taken back. Teeth proven with an injected DOMContentLoaded prompt.

partial-metric-declared.label: T47: a partial OEE must say so. OEE is a product of THREE factors - Availability x Performance x Quality - so computing two and calling the result 'OEE' is not a rounding difference, it is a different and HIGHER number, because the missing factor can only reduce it. A plant reporting 88% to management when the three-factor figure would be lower has not made a small error; it has made a claim it cannot defend the moment somebody asks how it was computed - and that reader is exactly who T47 is about. THE PLATFORM GETS THIS RIGHT and the gate keeps it right: analytics renders 'OEE (AVG, PARTIAL) 88% · Avg across 20 assets · WORLD CLASS · ISO 22400-2:2014 · Availability x Quality only. Add each asset's cycle time to include Performance.' - value, denominator, standard, WHICH FACTORS ARE IN IT, and what to do about the missing one, so a skeptic can hand-check the arithmetic and knows precisely what they are checking. THE ASSERTION: wherever a headline OEE figure renders, the same card names its factor basis - a partial marker plus the factors included, or a full three-factor statement; what it may never be is a bare 'OEE 88%'. ★IT DOES NOT ASSERT THE VALUE NOR DEMAND FULL OEE: whether this hive has cycle times is a data question, not a defect, and the honest response to missing data is to say what is missing, which is what the card does. The failure gated is SILENCE about the basis, not the partiality. Teeth proven by stripping the factor clause: namesFactors false, exit 1.

embedding-source-enqueues.label: T31: a registered knowledge source must actually enqueue. The RAG corpus is built by a mirror - embedding_registry names each source table and the knowledge table it feeds (logbook -> fault_knowledge, pm_completions -> pm_knowledge, skill_badges -> skill_knowledge), a trigger enqueues each new row into embedding_outbox, and embed-entry drains it. Registering a source WITHOUT its enqueue trigger is the quietest possible failure: the config says active, the knowledge table simply never grows, and nothing reports a problem because nothing errored. Asserts every active registry row has a matching enqueue trigger; measured 3 of 3. Teeth proven by registering community_replies with no trigger - which is exactly T31's own scenario, since accepted community answers are NOT currently indexed anywhere. ★WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT, AND WHY: the outbox holds 6,223 pending rows (logbook 4,617 of 8,058; pm_completions 1,606 of 1,611), which reads like a broken pipeline and is not - the drain is embed-entry called FROM THE BROWSER at write time, so rows inserted by the SEEDER, with no browser present, enqueue and sit (last drain 2026-08-20, when someone last worked through the UI). Gating on backlog depth would be a permanent red against a fixture, which is how a gate teaches people to ignore it. ★THE ARCHITECTURAL POINT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GATED: the outbox has no drainer other than a client, so any write that does not pass through a browser - a seeder, a CSV import, the server-side PM mirror - enqueues and never drains, with no cron backstop. Whether to add a scheduled drain costs embedding calls and is therefore Ian's decision, not this gate's.

write-failure-speaks.label: T147: a failed write must not be silent. `if (!error) { paint }` with no else is the quietest bug this platform can ship - the write fails, the screen does not move, nothing is said, and from the user's side that is indistinguishable from a dead control. The natural next move is to press it again, which is how one silent refusal becomes repeated writes. FOUND ON community's toggleReaction, BOTH branches: tapping an emoji whose insert or delete failed left the count sitting still with no message. Fixed with the vocabulary the same page already owns (submitReply uses whWriteError), and the add path names the one case where doing nothing IS correct - a duplicate reaction (23505) says 'You have already reacted with this emoji' rather than reporting a failure the person cannot act on. VERIFIED LIVE with an injected 500: the count correctly does NOT move (no false optimistic paint) and the toast reads 'Your reaction was not saved. Tap again to retry.' MEASURED AFTER: 223 awaited db writes destructure `error` across the app pages and ZERO now guard with a bare `if (!error)` and no else; resurrection-proven, since removing the new else-branches puts the count back to 1. ★DELIBERATELY NARROW: it does not demand a particular message, nor that every write speak - plenty correctly stay quiet because the render that follows IS the receipt. It catches one specific shape, where the code explicitly took the error into its hands by destructuring it, branched on it, and then dropped it. That is never intentional.

repaint-spares-typing.label: T142: a live update must not evict a typist. The recorded incident is precise - a 15-second poll rebuilt a region while somebody was typing in it and the repaint threw focus to <body>. The DRAFT survived, which is exactly what made it hard to notice: the text was still there, so the person kept typing into nothing. Realtime is the same hazard with worse timing, because the update arrives when a colleague acts rather than on a schedule anyone could learn. THE INVARIANT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT BEHAVIOURAL: a container a realtime handler REPLACES must not contain a typing surface. If the composer is not in the subtree being rebuilt, no repaint can evict it and no focus-restoration code is needed - which is better than restoring focus correctly, because restoration has to be right every single time. MEASURED, and both of T142's named subjects hold: community updates one card via _updateRenderedCard() for the ordinary case and rebuilds #feed-list ONLY when a pin moves (a genuine reorder), with both composers outside it - the post box on the page, the reply box inside #thread-overlay - confirmed in the LIVE DOM rather than from source offsets, after a character-offset reading had wrongly suggested nesting; and hive reloads targeted display cards (loadAdoptionCard, loadMaturityStairway) holding no inputs at all. ★IT ASSERTS CONTAINMENT, NOT FOCUS SURVIVAL: driving a real focus test needs the composer open and an update to land, and proves one path on one run, whereas containment is what makes every path safe and is checkable every run. ★AND IT READS THE POST-RENDER DOM, WHICH IS WHY THE FIRST TEETH TEST DID NOT FIRE - a textarea pasted into the empty #feed-list markup is wiped by the page's own render before the probe looks. The faithful test puts one in the CARD TEMPLATE so the render itself places it inside the rebuilt container, and the gate then reports 16 typing surfaces and fails.

portable-record.label: T58: what the platform calls PORTABLE must survive leaving. WorkHive pitches a 'portable career record' to OFW-track engineers - people whose whole reason to use it is showing evidence to the NEXT employer - so portable is not a marketing adjective here, it is a testable property: does the worker still have it once they are no longer a member? MEASURED AS THE WORKER under RLS, inside a transaction that rolls back: logbook entries 571 while active -> 0 as 'kicked' -> 0 as 'deactivated'; skill badges 12 -> 12 -> 12. The portability story is HALF true and the halves are cleanly separable - badges and certifications are held against the WORKER and travel, while logbook entries are hive-scoped by the logbook_read policy (an ACTIVE membership is required) and stop being readable the moment membership ends. ★THAT SCOPING IS CORRECT TENANCY, NOT A BUG: a plant's maintenance records are the plant's, and letting a departed worker read them is precisely the cross-tenant leak this platform gates everywhere else. ★THE APP WAS ALREADY HONEST AND THE MARKETING WAS NOT: hive.html's leave confirm says 'Your past logbook entries stay in the hive's records' - exactly right, at the moment it matters - while two learn pages promised the opposite ('portable evidence that you can take with you wherever you go. Whether you're applying for a job in Saudi Arabia...', and a personal export available 'at any time'). Both now carry the CONDITION (export while still a member) instead of the promise, in the JSON-LD and the visible FAQ together; the gamification page's badge claim was left untouched because measurement says it is TRUE. THE ASSERTION: a worker with no active membership can still read their skill_badges - the half the corrected claims now rest on - so if a future policy makes badges hive-scoped too, the pitch becomes false again SILENTLY and this says so. ★HOW IT IS KNOWN TO DISCRIMINATE, since a policy cannot be flipped without a migration: the identical probe against logbook reports 571->0 while badges report 12->12, same worker, same transaction, same mechanism. Non-destructive (BEGIN/ROLLBACK), and it re-checks that memberships are still active before trusting its own reading, because a probe that modified the fixture would otherwise report a pass on damage.

first-paint-throttled.label: T37: something must be on screen fast. Plant wifi at its worst is the condition this platform is actually used in, and the first second decides whether a worker believes the app is working at all - PP1's bar is that SOMETHING paints quickly (chrome, a heading, a skeleton) rather than a white screen while data is fetched. It measures FIRST CONTENTFUL PAINT, not settle time, and the distinction is the point: a page that takes 6s to fill with data but paints its frame in 400ms feels alive, while one that paints nothing for 2s feels broken even if it finishes sooner. REST is throttled 1.5s so the measurement is about the SHELL - a page whose first paint waits on data is exactly the failure being sought. MEASURED: all 8 core signed-in pages paint in 208-456ms against an 1800ms budget. ★AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS PROVER MANUFACTURED A FINDING, which is why it is built the way it is: reusing one browser context and walking pages in sequence, analytics.html - the SIXTH in the run - reported 2220ms against 212-292ms for everything else, and 2220 sits suspiciously close to the 1500ms injected delay plus overhead. Measured ALONE it paints in 400ms unthrottled and 368ms THROTTLED; the 2220 was contention from the five pages before it, still holding delayed routes and competing for one renderer. The number described the HARNESS, not the page. So the prover closes each page before opening the next and - the part that matters - RE-MEASURES anything over budget in a FRESH context before reporting it, so only a page still slow BY ITSELF is a finding. A performance gate without that step eventually accuses a healthy page, and that accusation is expensive because someone then hunts a cause that is not there. Teeth proven end to end at a 120ms budget: 6 pages flagged, each confirmed alone.

scroll-gate-at-open.label: T18: a read-gate must not depend on an event that may never fire. skillmatrix gates its exam behind 'read the lesson first' - the Take-exam button starts disabled and a scroll handler enables it once the reader reaches the bottom. Correct intent, and it had a hole: the button was enabled ONLY from inside that handler. ★A LESSON WHOSE CONTENT FITS THE BOX NEVER SCROLLS, so the scroll event never fires, checkScroll never runs, and the reader is left in front of a permanently disabled 'Take exam' beside a hint telling them to scroll something that does not scroll - with no way out of that screen but closing it. Latent only because every lesson written so far happens to overflow, and lesson bodies are AUTHORED CONTENT, so the first short one ships the trap to whoever writes it. FIXED by evaluating the gate once at open, after the scroll reset: self-correcting, because for a non-scrolling box scrollTop + clientHeight already exceeds scrollHeight - 80 so the check passes immediately, while a long lesson at scrollTop 0 still fails it and the gate holds. ★VERIFIED LIVE ON BOTH BRANCHES, since the risk of this fix is that it opens the gate for everyone: long content (scrollHeight 822 vs clientHeight 502) still reports disabled=true with the hint shown, short content (54 vs 54) reports disabled=false with the hint cleared, 0 pageerrors. ★AND THE GATE ITSELF FAILED ITS FIRST TEETH TEST: the invocation count matched `function checkScroll()` - the DECLARATION - so deleting the real call still left a count of 1 and it reported PASS on the exact defect it exists for. A negative lookbehind for 'function ' fixed it; the teeth test refusing to go red is the only reason that was caught. Narrow by design: this is one known control, and inferring 'enabled only by an event' across the platform would be guessing at intent.

lang-declared.label: T159: the page must say which language it is in. A screen reader picks its pronunciation rules from <html lang>, so Filipino text announced under lang='en' comes out as English phonemes applied to Tagalog - not accented, but unrecoverable. WCAG 3.1.1 asks for the page's language and 3.1.2 that a change of language be marked. ★THE HARD HALF IS THAT THIS PLATFORM IS BILINGUAL BY TOGGLE, NOT BY URL: one page, _t(en, fil) at every string, and a wh_lang preference - so the declaration is not a static fact set at build time, it has to FOLLOW the toggle, which is exactly the half a static audit misses. MEASURED and the discipline is clean: all 156 public pages declare <html lang> (none silent); utils.js:219 sets documentElement.lang from the stored locale on EVERY page load, so a reader who chose Filipino gets the right declaration even on pages with no translation engine of their own; and all three pages that WRITE wh_lang (index, analytics, analytics-report) also assign documentElement.lang in their toggle handler, so switching mid-session updates the declaration without a reload. TWO ASSERTIONS: every public page carries <html lang>, and any page that writes the wh_lang preference must also assign documentElement.lang - a toggle that changes the words while leaving the declaration behind is WORSE than no toggle, because the page then asserts a language it is not in. ★NO hreflang IS ASSERTED, deliberately rather than by omission: hreflang describes ALTERNATE URLs for the same content and this platform has none - the locale lives in localStorage, so /learn/x is one URL serving whichever language the reader chose, and demanding hreflang would be demanding a second site. Whether to publish a Filipino public corpus at all is T159's open posture question and Ian's to answer; this gate holds the part that is true under either answer. Teeth proven on both halves.

no-drag-only.label: T117 / WCAG 2.5.7: nothing may become reachable ONLY by dragging. A worker in gloves, a person with a tremor and anyone on a trackpad share one need - no function should require a dragging movement. The census found the platform CLEAN, and every gesture it has is harmless: nav-hub and companion-launcher let a person DRAG the floating button out of the way while opening it stays a TAP; session-timeout listens for touchstart as an activity SIGNAL, not a gesture requirement; wh-persona sets draggable=false, disabling dragging rather than requiring it. The one genuine keyboard trap in this family was already closed centrally - .wh-scroll-x regions scrolled by swipe were unreachable from a keyboard (axe scrollable-region-focusable, eight on project-report), fixed where the shared class lives rather than per call site. THE GATE FOUND A HIT ON ITS FIRST RUN and it was checked rather than assumed: integrations.html registers a drop handler for CMMS imports - and it is guarded by if (dropZone && fileInput), with a real labelled input type=file wired to the SAME handleFile on change. Drag-and-drop over a working file picker is exactly what 2.5.7 asks for, so it is justified by name with that reason recorded. A NEW gesture file fails - not because dragging is forbidden, but because 'is there a tap that does the same thing?' is a question somebody must answer out loud before it ships. Scoped to product surfaces: vendor bundles and the measurement tooling whose JOB is to find drag handlers are excluded, since a lens that greps for dragstart would otherwise fail a gate about dragstart. ★MERGED WITH T75 (2026-08-26), which asked the same question of dayplanner and found it has NO drag machinery at all - the walk's premise was wrong, there was no drag to alternate. That pass added the rule that now decides the FAB repositioners: a handler assigning only style.left/right/top/bottom MOVES a control and confers no capability, so it passes, while one that also mutates data (insert, splice, sort_order) is load-bearing and must offer a tap. Deciding by what the handler WRITES rather than by which file it lives in keeps the exemption from becoming a licence. ★AND A REAL MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: driving T75 I wrote a second version of this gate straight over the T117 file, having read 'updated successfully' as 'created', then removed 102 unrelated gate registrations with an over-greedy cleanup regex. The duplicate-id guard caught the first, a HEAD diff caught and repaired the second. A duplicate id is a signal to MERGE two efforts, never to register the same name twice.

auto-read-retry.label: T126: a failed READ recovers itself on reconnect. Reconnect handling here was write-only - offline queues drain on online, logbook syncs, banners repaint - but a failed READ sat behind a Retry button waiting for a tap, and manual assumes somebody is standing there. A wall-mounted alert board has nobody, so one network blip left a plant staring at a stale error for the rest of a shift; a phone in a pocket has nobody at the moment the signal returns. whListError now registers its retry for auto-recovery. SIX assertions, and three are RESTRAINT rather than recovery, because an auto-retry that misbehaves is worse than none - it hammers a backend that is already unwell: it re-runs on an online event (the defect), does NOT re-run on a second reconnect inside 3s, leaves alone any section that is no longer showing an error (a person who fixed it by hand must not have their view yanked), and DROPS an element removed from the DOM instead of retrying it forever - the listener-lifecycle leak this repo already gates for. NO TIMER, EVER: it fires on connectivity events only, because a polling retry would turn a backend outage into a self-inflicted load test. Resurrection goes RED on the two assertions that decide it (helperPresent, retriedOnReconnect); two others also read false pre-fix purely because they assert exactly-one-call against a world that made zero, and the gate says so rather than counting them as evidence. THE OTHER HALF OF T126 STAYS OPEN BY DESIGN: the hourly idle sign-out is CORRECT for shared plant tablets, so a kiosk exemption is a product decision for Ian, not a silent weakening of a protection that exists on purpose.

interruption-steps.label: T122: nothing lost, at EVERY step. The first walk injected an interruption at ONE step of the logbook wizard and found it green - but a multi-step form saves on its own schedule, so the step where the draft is NOT yet written is invisible to a probe that only tests the step where it is, and a phone rings whenever it rings. This fills the wizard progressively and at the end of each step injects the harshest realistic interruption, a FULL RELOAD (the OS killing a backgrounded tab), then asserts everything typed so far comes back. THE MECHANISM IS logbook OWN saveDraft/restoreDraft, NOT whAutoSaveDraft - T122 first write-up credited the shared helper, and logbook does not use it. That matters beyond tidiness: the shared helper got OWNER STAMPING in T121 so one worker draft cannot surface for the next person on a shared plant phone, and logbook - the platform richest personal-text form - missed that change entirely. Checked rather than assumed: logbook is safe anyway by a different route, DRAFT_KEY being wh_logbook_draft_ + WORKER_NAME, so the next person page computes a key it cannot read. Two mechanisms, one guarantee, worth knowing which is which before someone unifies them and removes a protection they did not know was there. AND THE PROBE REFUSES TO MEASURE A VALUE THAT DID NOT TAKE: its first run reported the draft lost f-root-cause, which is a select where assigning a non-option value silently yields empty - nothing had been set, so nothing could be lost, and the defect did not exist. Mutation-proven with restoreDraft disabled: 0 of 3 steps keep their work, every lost field named.

numeric-paste.label: T123: an unparseable paste must not blank a number box in silence. ★THE CLAIM HERE IS DELIBERATELY NARROWER THAN THE ONE FIRST WRITTEN, because the resurrection refuted it. The first measurement set el.value = '1,500' directly, watched the field empty with validity VALID, and got written up as 'pasting a thousands separator silently empties the box'. Running the finished prover against the PRE-FIX utils.js then passed four of five cases: with a REAL clipboard, Chromium's paste pipeline already strips the comma, the spaces and the trailing unit before sanitization. ASSIGNING a value and PASTING one are different mechanisms and only one is what a person does - the resurrection existed to catch exactly that, and did. THE DEFECT THAT SURVIVED, and it is real: an unparseable paste ('abc') blanks the field and says NOTHING, and in a quantity box a silent blank is easy to miss while the consequence is submitting no quantity. It announces now. THE NORMALIZATION IS HARDENING, LABELLED AS SUCH: whCleanNumericPaste makes the behaviour the platform's own rather than depending on one engine's undocumented paste filtering; whether other engines empty the field instead is UNMEASURED (only Chromium is installed) and neither gate nor prover claims otherwise. The probe uses a real clipboard, never a synthetic ClipboardEvent - that shortcut produced a second false reading, because the already-clean case deliberately falls through to the native paste and a synthetic event has no clipboard behind it.

dialog-floor.label: T113: every dialog measured at the 320px budget-Android FLOOR. cj_dialog_layout sweeps 390/641/1280 - the widths with banked owed rows - and 320 had never been measured at all, so this runs the same prover under WH_DIALOG_WIDTHS=320 as a SEPARATE gate rather than widening the existing one: silently adding a fourth width would change what cj_dialog_layout means without anyone deciding to, and its rows describe the three it has. THE FIRST FLOOR RUN FOUND THREE REAL DEFECTS in a place nobody had looked. (1) pm-scheduler's PM completion sheet hung its PRIMARY ACTION 21px past the panel - btn-primary is width:100% by design but shares one flex row with Cancel, and at 320 the content box is 278px, which cannot hold both however the remainder is divided; two attempts to make them share went 21 -> 10 -> 14px, the measurement saying so, and they now stack, which is the ordinary mobile pattern. (2) analytics' results panel pinned THREE columns by inline style regardless of width and pushed tiles 52px past it; auto-fit keeps three where they fit. (3) public-feed showed a 229x12px link - and it was NOT a floor defect at all: it lives in whListError, so it sat in ~20 pages' read-failure states and was failing at 390 too, unnoticed. THAT THIRD ONE IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE GATE: measuring a width nobody had measured surfaced a platform-wide defect in the exact state a person reaches when something has already gone wrong. The prover's own rail protects it - it refuses to call an empty denominator a pass, which is how the first run (0 of 50 graded, a probe bug) was caught in five minutes instead of banked as 'the floor is clean'.

fixed-chrome-budget.label: T113's floor-viewport budget. 320x640 is the budget-Android floor this platform targets, and at that size the question is not whether things FIT but how much room REMAINS after the platform's own furniture - a fixed nav, a hub FAB, an AI widget, a page-guide chip. Each is individually reasonable, none was ever measured TOGETHER, and that is how a page ends up spending a third of its screen before one row of content is drawn. Measured across the eight pages a field phone lives in: mean 26.1% covered, worst 36.6% (pm-scheduler), and on seven of eight the largest single contributor is the same 64px guide chip - a component this codebase has already caught covering every modal's Save. Coverage is a UNION of viewport rows, never a sum: overlapping chrome costs one band, and summing would report a number nobody experiences. Forward-only per page. ★THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEFORE ANY NUMBER WAS BANKED, which is why this one is trustworthy: run 1 said index was 87.5% covered and blamed #cursor-glow, a 440px pointer-following gradient that is pointer-events:none, z-index 0 and 5% alpha - decoration sitting BEHIND everything; run 2 said logbook was 50.9% and blamed a 280px div.card that turned out to be the Log a Repair FORM, sticky top-6 and 843px tall on a 640px screen, which cannot stick at all and scrolls exactly like the content it is. Banking either would have sent someone deleting furniture that does not exist or a panel a worker needs. The surviving rules: chrome is what INTERCEPTS A THUMB or gets ANNOUNCED, and chrome PERSISTS WHILE CONTENT MOVES UNDER IT.

outbound-email-honesty.label: T111: comms held to the same bar as the glass. The DP manipulation-absence dims are measured on PAGES, so EMAIL escapes them entirely - and it is the one surface that reaches a person who may not even have an account, cannot be corrected once sent, and is where urgency-shaped copy is most tempting and least visible to any UI test. T111's census found exactly ONE outbound template (send-report-email), audited it clean, and fixed its real gap: the footer said only 'Sent via WorkHive Report Sender', so the recipient of an outward irreversible email could not tell WHICH PERSON sent it nor how to stop receiving them. That fix shipped with no gate. FOUR assertions: (1) exactly the known set of functions builds outbound email - the census made LIVING, so a new marketing or re-engagement lane cannot appear un-audited, which is the very scenario this trajectory is named for; (2) the footer names the sending PERSON; (3) it carries a stop path AND an accurate one - recipients live in the sender's own contact list, so 'ask the sender to remove you' is truthful where a fake one-click unsubscribe would be a worse lie than none; (4) no urgency/scarcity/guilt vocabulary in the literals the TEMPLATE owns - checked against template copy only, never report content, because reports carry real words like overdue and risk and a lint policing those would demand the product misdescribe genuine urgency to satisfy a gate. Teeth-proven three ways: the pre-fix footer (both arms RED), an injected 'Your hive needs you - act now' (RED), and a new un-audited resend-calling function (RED).

no-clock-driven-push.label: T109: the structural reason this platform needs no quiet hours YET, guarded so it stays true. The walk found no quiet-hours machinery anywhere AND - the part that mattered - nothing that CLAIMS it, so the platform is silent rather than lying. What makes that absence defensible is measurable: EVERY push producer is EVENT-DRIVEN (mention, reply, best answer, assignment, approval decision, report, submission, service completion). Not one is clock-driven, so a phone cannot buzz at 3am unless somebody in that hive acted at 3am - which on a round-the-clock plant is a night shift and is legitimate news. The day a scheduled digest or nightly reminder ships that stops being true instantly, because a clock-driven push CHOOSES its own hour, and choosing 3am for someone is precisely what quiet hours exist to prevent. Asserts no cron job invokes anything that enqueues a push - a DB function calling enqueue_user_push (checked transitively one hop, since fanout_completion_push is reached through a trigger) or an edge function that does. notify-push and the outbox drain are exempt BY NAME: they deliver what is already queued, decide nothing, and must run every minute or nothing arrives. THIS GATE IS MEANT TO FIRE ONE DAY - when the digest T106 records as a scoped decision gets built, it goes red, and the red is the point: it forces the quiet-window question to be answered BEFORE the first scheduled push reaches a phone. Mutation-proven by scheduling a 3am-PHT digest cron: caught by name, then unscheduled. SKIPs without docker.

push-dedupe-window.label: T110: the ONLY place a notification storm is bounded before delivery. enqueue_user_push inserts one service_outbox row per event and the drain sends one push per row, so nothing between an event and a phone collapses repeats - two triggers on one PM going overdue, a supervisor's repeated save, a retrying client each become their own buzz. Mig 20260826000001 added the narrow safe half (an identical push still UNSENT within 2 minutes hands back the pending row's id) but shipped WITHOUT a gate, and it has since become load-bearing: four producers were added the same week (mentions, replies, best-answer, and a trigger on every pending submission), and the submission trigger depends on this window BY DESIGN - its copy names no row precisely so a bulk CMMS import of 200 assets collapses to ONE push. If the dedupe regresses that trigger stops being a summary and becomes a cannon. FIVE assertions, and the third separates a correct dedupe from a mute button: a repeat whose predecessor was already DELIVERED must be treated as NEWS and get its own row, because suppressing it would silently drop real notifications. Also asserts a different body and a different RECIPIENT each get their own row - a blanket one-push-per-user-per-window would swallow genuinely different news and merge two people's deliveries. Runs entirely inside a transaction that is ROLLED BACK, and then verifies nothing survived: the gate writes nothing it must clean up. Resurrection: with the dedupe removed (also inside a rollback, since DDL is transactional) identical pushes returned different ids and wrote 2 rows - both assertions RED. SKIPs without docker.

automation-log-status.label: T112's bug-CLASS gate, built after finding two live instances. automation_log carries CHECK (status IN success|failed|skipped|warning). resend-webhook-receiver wrote 'failure' (the word is 'failed') and send-report-email's circuit breaker wrote 'deferred' - both refused with 23514, and NEITHER read the insert error, so supabase-js returned it into the void and both functions carried on reporting success. The bounce receiver would have answered Resend 200 'recorded' while storing NOTHING, leaving the sender-side bounce surface permanently empty with every layer above it looking healthy; the breaker's trip would never reach the log an operator reads exactly when the breaker trips. Neither had fired - the receiver fails closed without its signing secret and the breaker needs Resend to be failing - so both were latent, primed to go off at the first real bounce after Ian sets the secret and at the first email outage. Asserts (1) every status literal is in the allowed set, read from the MIGRATION and cross-checked against the LIVE constraint, because a repo that says one thing while the database enforces another is its own defect a one-sided gate cannot see; and (2) a forward-only ratchet on UNCHECKED automation_log inserts (12 of 14 today - not zero, because rewriting every audit path in one pass to move a number is a large unreviewed change for no measured defect; what must not happen is a NEW one, since an unchecked insert is what turned both bugs from a loud 23514 into silence). Resurrection: RED on the pre-fix functions for both instances.

bounce-idempotency.label: T112: one delivery id, one bounce row. resend-webhook-receiver ended in a bare INSERT, while Svix (which Resend uses) delivers AT LEAST ONCE, retries on any non-2xx or timeout, and carries a stable delivery id in the svix-id header for exactly this purpose - which the function read to verify the signature and then threw away. A retried delivery wrote a SECOND bounce row: the sender-side bounce surface would list one failed send twice, and any count over it over-reports how bad deliverability is, which is the direction that gets acted on. Fixed with a PARTIAL UNIQUE EXPRESSION INDEX (mig 20260826000004) rather than a check-before-insert, because two near-simultaneous retries both pass a SELECT-then-INSERT - a shape this codebase already has a scar from. FOUR assertions, and the fourth is what distinguishes the two designs: two writers racing on one id in CONCURRENT transactions must end with exactly one row and one refusal, measured rather than argued. DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: the HTTP round trip stays owed (the fn is not served locally and its secret is Ian's), but a live smoke could only show one duplicate handled, whereas the index shows none can ever be stored. SKIPs without docker.

report-link-fidelity.label: T106's arrival-fidelity oracle for EMAIL. Every 'View in WorkHive' link in send-report-email pointed at a bare page root, so a PM Overdue report - a document whose entire subject IS the overdue set - landed its reader on the unfiltered schedule, and both logbook reports landed on that page's default MINE view while the report itself is hive-wide: T19's two-windows-one-metric mismatch arriving by email, at whoever the supervisor forwarded it to. Measured before changing anything - ?filter=overdue is a real chip value on pm-scheduler AND genuinely filters (live: ontrack 0 rows, duesoon 2, overdue 10 vs 10 bare), so the parameter works rather than merely highlighting a chip. THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS is not that links carry params but that every param they carry is one the TARGET PAGE ACTUALLY READS, checked against the generated param_route_registry: a link decorated with ?window=7d would look more specific while delivering nothing, which is worse than a bare link because it reads as context that was never handed over. Also asserts every target page exists - a link into a renamed page is a dead end reached from an inbox, where nobody can press Retry. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: that all eight carry a param; five target analytics.html and project-manager.html, which read NO params at all, so their links are already as specific as those pages allow and demanding more would push someone to invent one that does nothing. Resurrection BOTH ways: RED on the pre-fix bare links, and RED again on a mutation adding a plausible ?window=90d that analytics never reads.

offline-queued.label: T14: offline_queued family gate — T14's lock spoke (2026-08-25). Runs tools/prove_offline_queued.mjs across ALL 8 queue-page cases (the complete whCreateQueue roster + logbook's own queue) and FAILs on any case that cannot prove the queue-and-tell oracle: offline, the write is HELD (the queue's own store grows or the record is on screen), the person is TOLD it will sync, and nothing claims the refusal wording. WHY A GATE: the CG family's offline cell was `offline_refusal` — the WRONG oracle for queue pages (green credited a refusal that must not exist). The prover replaced it for these 8 pages; without a registered gate the family regresses silently (the queue-registration defer race THIS oracle caught on pm-scheduler — 2 of 5 runs lost — is exactly the class that returns quietly). Discipline carried from the bank's own lessons: - retry-once per case before failing (full-suite live gates flake under load; the pm-completion case's comment records the re-run-first rule). - node invoked DIRECTLY, never npx (the repo path contains an ampersand). - skips cleanly when node or the local stack (Flask :5000 / Supabase :54321) is absent — a gate that cannot run must say SKIP, not PASS. Re-drive one case: node tools/prove_offline_queued.mjs --case <name>

findability.label: T173: Findability benchmark gate — T173's lock (2026-08-25). Wraps tools/findability_benchmark.mjs: 20 common tasks phrased as USER QUESTIONS, each answered from a cold page via the global hub in <= 2 interactions, asked AS the persona who owns the question (worker default; supervisor-lane questions declare role:'supervisor' — the hub's role scoping is design, not a defect). Its FIRST runs caught four real wayfinding defects (Hive Board supervisor-gated against its own worker-daily declaration; Voice Journal and Reports hidden from the personas who own them; Eng. Design excluding supervisors, who ARE the engineer persona in practice). This gate keeps the 20/20 from regressing. Skips cleanly when node or the local stack is absent. Re-drive: node tools/findability_benchmark.mjs

someone-to-you.label: T108: someone->you event coverage gate — T108's registry discipline (2026-08-25). The registry (substrate/reference/someone_to_you_event_registry.json) enumerates every event where person A's action creates work or attention for person B. The T108 bar: each event needs a notification path and a tap that lands ON the item; 'none' rows are the silent-work class to extinguish. WHAT THIS GATE HOLDS (a forward-only ratchet, not a green demand): 1. The registry file exists, parses, and every event row carries the required fields (event, source, notification, finding) with notification in the declared vocab. 2. The count of 'none' (silent-work) rows never GROWS past the accepted baseline — shipping a new someone->you event without a notification path FAILs here by name. Fixing one (none -> badge-only/notified/realtime) tightens the baseline. Baseline lives inline (SILENT_BASELINE); update it DOWNWARD as silent rows are fixed.

join-lands.label: T6/T7: join-lands-on-roster gate — T6+T7's shared instrument close (2026-08-26). Runs tools/prove_join_lands.mjs: a two-context paired journey where an OUTSIDE worker joins the supervisor's hive by invite code (the same SECURITY DEFINER join_hive_by_code path the UI submit calls) while the supervisor's hive.html board is open. PASS bar: the join is VISIBLE on the supervisor's roster after at most one reload, the DB row landed, and the probe row is cleaned + verified. The prover also measures (never asserts) the realtime half: hive.html registers no postgres_changes channel on hive_members, so realtime=false is the current truth — recorded in the output so the day a channel is added the receipt flips. Discipline (carried from validate_offline_queued.py): - retry-once before failing (full-suite live gates flake under load). - node invoked DIRECTLY, never npx (the repo path contains an ampersand). - utf-8 pinned on the subprocess decode; PASS matched line-anchored. - SKIPs cleanly when node / the local stack is absent — a gate that cannot run must say SKIP, not PASS. - the prover ABORTS (exit 2) on dirty pre-state rather than deleting rows it did not create; that surfaces here as FAIL with the abort line.

persona-follows-account.label: T85: the companion follows the account — T85's cross-device oracle (2026-08-26). The persona lives in TWO places: localStorage, which every renderer and prompt-builder reads, and worker_profiles.preferred_persona, the account-level choice. Only index.html and voice-journal.html bridged them, each with its own copy of the query. assistant.html — reachable directly, from the nav hub, a deep link, or simply a different browser — read localStorage alone. MEASURED: account set to hezekiah, localStorage empty, assistant resolved ZANIAH. That is not a wrong default, it is the worker's choice being ignored, and it is SILENT because the wrong answer IS the default — nothing errors, the companion is just not the one they picked. ★AND THE COPY IT REPLACED CLOBBERED ON FAILURE: index's inline version destructured { data: profile } without checking the error, so a transient blip left profile null, fell through to 'zaniah', and WROTE it — permanently resetting a Hezekiah user because one read failed. An absent or unreadable preference is not evidence of a preference. Both surfaces now use one helper (wh-persona.js hydratePersonaFromCloud) that writes only when the cloud names a choice. The prover drives BOTH directions, since a one-way check would pass on a page that always overwrites: the choice must REACH a fresh device, and an injected 500 on the profile read must CHANGE NOTHING. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD direction one resolves 'zaniah'. Sibling to CL9, which found the same class in companion-launcher — that check guarded ONE file while the identical bug sat in assistant.html; its scope is now all five persona surfaces, plus a rule against stamping a CONSTANT on a persona column (voice-handler logged 13 of 13 tts_quality_log rows as 'zaniah').

edge-refusal-reaches-user.label: T82: edge refusals reach the user — the static census. supabase-js collapses EVERY non-2xx from functions.invoke into ONE FunctionsHttpError whose message is the literal string "Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code". The status and body survive only on error.context (a Response), so a caller reading error.message never sees them - and shows that placeholder to a person. ★THE CLIENT THEN SILENTLY UNDOES THE WORK THE BACKEND DID: rate-limit.ts answers a drained hive with 429 and "AI call limit reached for this hive. Try again in an hour." - cause named, clearing time named, exactly the bar the AI-error taxonomy exists to hold. MEASURED on asset-hub (met by genuinely exhausting the hourly quota): the worker read "Could not reach Asset Brain: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code", a CONNECTION-flavoured sentence for a QUOTA event, sending them to check their signal instead of waiting an hour. whAiError could not rescue it either - it keys on /429|rate.?limit|quota/ and the placeholder carries none of them. Fixed centrally: utils.js whFnError() reads error.context, so the function's own sentence survives and only a body-less failure falls back to the status taxonomy. The unwrap had been hand-rolled in companion-launcher, analytics and assistant - three copies, thirteen other files without it. WHAT IT COUNTS: invoke error branches that put error.message in front of a person (toast, innerHTML, textContent, a whListError/whReadError call) without consulting error.context or whFnError. ★IT COUNTS RATHER THAN FORBIDS - 39 invoke sites, 19 speaking the placeholder at first measure; a gate that failed all of them on day one would be turned off. Forward-only against tools/edge_refusal_baseline.json; asset-hub's four sites were cleared in the same pass, 19 -> 16. ★AND IT ONLY FLAGS BRANCHES THAT SPEAK: an invoke whose error is logged, swallowed or rethrown shows nobody the placeholder, and charging for it would measure code shape rather than harm.

edge-refusal-survives-client.label: T82: edge refusals survive the client — the live half. supabase-js collapses EVERY non-2xx from functions.invoke into ONE FunctionsHttpError whose message is the literal string "Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code". The status and body survive only on error.context (a Response), so a caller reading error.message never sees them - and shows that placeholder to a person. ★THE CLIENT THEN SILENTLY UNDOES THE WORK THE BACKEND DID: rate-limit.ts answers a drained hive with 429 and "AI call limit reached for this hive. Try again in an hour." - cause named, clearing time named, exactly the bar the AI-error taxonomy exists to hold. MEASURED on asset-hub (met by genuinely exhausting the hourly quota): the worker read "Could not reach Asset Brain: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code", a CONNECTION-flavoured sentence for a QUOTA event, sending them to check their signal instead of waiting an hour. whAiError could not rescue it either - it keys on /429|rate.?limit|quota/ and the placeholder carries none of them. Fixed centrally: utils.js whFnError() reads error.context, so the function's own sentence survives and only a body-less failure falls back to the status taxonomy. The unwrap had been hand-rolled in companion-launcher, analytics and assistant - three copies, thirteen other files without it. THE ASSERTION: with both Asset Brain lanes forced to the real 429 payload, the answer pane shows the FUNCTION'S sentence (quota named) and never the placeholder. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the pane reads "Could not reach Asset Brain: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code" and the gate fails. ★The 429 is INJECTED rather than waited for, so the probe is deterministic and spends no AI call.

ai-draft-shows-its-basis.label: T80: an AI draft shows its basis — T80's review oracle (2026-08-26). fmea-populator reads a year of corrective logbook entries, clusters them by root cause, and writes suggested failure modes to rcm_fmea_modes with source='ai_logbook' and approved_at NULL. An engineer then approves them, and APPROVAL is what makes a mode count in v_fmea_truth and drive maintenance strategy. FOUND: the row announced itself honestly - a 'from AI logbook scan' pill and a confidence badge, provenance done properly - and said NOTHING about what it read. The engineer was asked to approve a failure mode with no way to check the claim, on a screen whose output shapes how a machine gets maintained. The function held the exact cluster and simply never recorded it; the `notes` column existed and sat unused. Confirmed in the fixture: a live ai_logbook row ('Lip seal leaking', 0.552 confidence) with notes NULL. Same lesson AH15 learned about citations - the one thing a citation is FOR is letting a reader verify. Now stamped as the window and root cause a person can filter the logbook by ('AI draft from 6 corrective logbook entries (root cause: seal wear) between ... Review against those entries before approving.'), not raw uuids, which nobody can check by reading. ★IT CHECKS BOTH HALVES (the AI6 pair): a basis written but never rendered helps no one, and a render with nothing to show is a blank line. Teeth: reverting either side fails it; reverting both reports both. Verified live end to end - the grounding line and confidence badge render on the row, 0 page errors, probe row removed and re-counted to 0. ★AND ONLY FOR DRAFTS AWAITING A HUMAN: a mode an engineer wrote needs no such note; the point is not provenance theatre, it is that whoever is asked to APPROVE can check.

voice-refuses-ambiguous-asset.label: T79: voice refuses an ambiguous asset — T79's commit oracle (2026-08-26). The voice router turns "I replaced the seal on Pump 2" into a logbook.create intent and resolves the machine; when more than one matches it returns asset_resolution ambiguous:true with the candidates. FOUND: ambiguity was RENDERED and never ENFORCED. The intent card turned the asset pill red and appended '(multiple matches)' - and Confirm still wrote the entry to ar.primary, whichever candidate ranked first. A worker's repair record landed on the wrong machine, and the only warning was a colour; on a plant floor that is maintenance history attached to the wrong equipment, the one thing the history exists to get right. ★AND THE GUARD FOR THIS ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS DEAD: _preflightAction was defined, exported in the test-helper block, and certified by validate_ai_companion_integration_audit's preflight check - which asserted its four blocker STRINGS appeared in the file. They did, inside a function nothing ever called. Its writeVerbs were slot-style ('log_entry') while the router emits 'logbook.create', so even a call would have matched nothing. Presence is not wiring: that audit now requires a real call site plus the router's own kinds, and fails against pre-fix HEAD on both counts. THE ASSERTION, driven against the shipped file in a browser: a write kind with an ambiguous resolution is refused with blocker 'ambiguous_asset', the SAME kind with one clear match is NOT refused for ambiguity, and the refusal names the candidates and says nothing was saved. ★DIRECTION TWO IS THE POINT - a guard that refused everything would satisfy direction one while making voice logging useless. Teeth: pre-fix the probe reads 'ambiguous -> allowed'.

no-eaten-escapes.label: Platform: no eaten escapes — a control character in source is a regex that cannot fire (2026-08-26). Written through nested quoting layers (a shell heredoc, a nested python -c, an editor round-trip), a \b can arrive on disk as a literal BACKSPACE byte. The file parses, the regex compiles, and the alternative it guards can never match, because no real string contains a backspace. Nothing errors; the check quietly stops checking. MEASURED, five instances in one session: shift-brain.html (x2) and report-sender.html carried /\b429\b|rate.?limit|too many requests/i with both boundaries turned into control bytes, so a bare '429' or 'Request failed with status 429' was NOT recognised as rate limiting - proven against the shipped file, '429' -> false before and true after, on the very pages that tell a person why their report or shift plan did not run; tools/prove_route_numbers.mjs lost its suffixed-unit branch and over-reported naked numbers; and two gates written the same day had partly-dead matchers. An earlier session found 28 at once, including a \b429\b fix that was itself dead and passed only because the text happened to say 'Too Many Requests'. ★A SNIPPET IS NOT THE ARTIFACT - that session proved its boundary in a separate snippet and shipped a dead regex; this gate reads BYTES off disk, because a console renders 0x08 as nothing, which is exactly how the bug hides (it printed a repaired-looking /429|.../ while still holding the control character). ★WHY BYTES AND NOT A REGEX: every other detector here could be a victim of the bug it hunts; a byte count has no matcher to break. ★SCOPE: repo-wide, 15,089 files - validate_page_ui_provers.py has the same check scoped to provers, and all three shipped instances sat outside it, which is the too-narrow-scope failure this class keeps producing.

scheduled-claim-has-a-schedule.label: T63/T66: a cadence promise needs a scheduler — cron.job is the oracle (2026-08-26). A page telling a reader something happens 'daily' or 'monthly' is making a claim about a SCHEDULER, settled against the live database rather than against prose. FOUND on integrations.html: 'New SAP work orders then flow in daily' and 'WorkHive polls your CMMS API daily' - measured, 26 cron jobs and not one touching cmms-sync, which runs only when someone presses Sync now. Worse than copy: the Sync Schedule control DEFAULTED to 'Daily', saved sync_freq, and plant-connections rendered that value in its status table - three surfaces agreeing on a cadence nothing runs, while nothing anywhere reads sync_freq. What was REAL stayed (the webhook a CMMS posts to, and the push-back cmms-push-completion fires as each job closes). ★THEN THE SAME DEFECT ON A SECOND PAGE, which is why the scope moved: ph-intelligence.html claimed a monthly rhythm in EIGHT places - 'Published monthly', 'refreshes monthly', 'Reports are generated monthly', and worst 'next monthly refresh due soon', a promise about a future event nothing would deliver - with no cron touching intelligence-report either. Scoping a gate to where a bug was NOTICED rather than where the CLASS lives is the failure this session kept finding in other people's checks. ★AND A SAMPLE IS NOT A CENSUS: the first pass on that page read a slice of visible text, caught four claims and declared it clean; a grep for the word found four more. ★ITS OWN VOCABULARY NEEDED FIXING TWICE - it flagged <option> labels (offering a choice is not promising it runs) and then its own honest disclaimer, so selects and denials are excluded; and it miscounted 26 cron jobs as 51 by splitting multi-line commands. ★SKIPS WITHOUT ITS ORACLE. Teeth: reverting either page alone flags that page's claims while the other stays clean.

new-claims-are-opt-in.label: T84: new claims are opt-in — T84's resume-polish oracle (2026-08-26). resume.html's review sheet is a good pattern: the AI only SUGGESTS, and nothing reaches the document until the worker approves it. But two different acts arrived with the same default. REWRITE - polishing a bullet the worker wrote - is shown as 'Was: <their text>' and pre-ticked; their content, improved, with the change visible, which is fine. ADD - the 'suggested highlights' from tailor_to_jd - is PUSHED into their experience, was also pre-ticked, and carries no 'Was:' because there is no before. Those are NET-NEW CLAIMS ABOUT THE WORKER, generated with the JOB AD in context: exactly the pressure that produces a line they cannot back up in an interview, on the document they hand an employer. FOUND: both checked:true, so the default path (Tailor, then Apply) added up to five such claims without one deliberate act of accepting any. The prompt DOES instruct the model to keep highlights truthful and grounded in stated skills - worth having, and kept - but a prompt is the only thing enforcing it, and pre-ticking removed the human check meant to be the backstop. New claims now start unchecked, and the tailored summary gained its 'Was:' so its diff is visible like the polish path's. ★IT READS THE APPLY FUNCTION, NOT THE LABEL: addition versus edit is decided by what it does to the document (.push vs assignment), which no wording can disguise. ★AND IT DOES NOT BAN PRE-TICKING - making every suggestion opt-in would push workers toward tapping Apply without reading, the very behaviour this prevents; only new claims about a person carry the burden. ★ITS OWN MATCHER WAS BLIND FIRST: it bounded the apply body with [^;]{0,400} and every real apply is several statements long, so it matched nothing and PASSED against the world it was built to catch - caught only by teeth-proving, which is why it is not registered vacuous.

rating-admits-refusal.label: T88: a rating admits refusal — T88's feedback-loop oracle (2026-08-26). Every companion reply carries thumbs up/down. The tap used to lock both buttons and paint the chosen one green or red IMMEDIATELY, then fire the insert and discard whatever came back. ★AND THE MOST LIKELY FAILURE DOES NOT THROW: supabase-js returns { error } on an RLS refusal rather than raising, so the try/catch around that insert never fired for it - the code's own comment records that anon callers 'silently skip'. A worker tapped thumbs-down, watched it turn red, and nothing was stored. That is worse than having no thumbs at all: it teaches them their feedback is read when it is not, on the surface whose entire purpose is to collect it. MEASURED with the insert answered 403 the way a real RLS denial answers: _recordReplyRating returned undefined and the UI had already committed. It now returns false, the buttons come back, and the worker is told to tap again; on success it returns true and only then does the button take its accepted colour. ★BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a function that always reported failure would satisfy the first half while silently discarding every real rating - refused -> false, allowed -> true, with the row counted in the database. ★NOT COSMETIC: ai-quality aggregates these thumbs, and 3+ negatives in 7 days flags ai_quality_escalation for supervisor outreach, so silently dropped ratings quietly bias all of it. Probe rows marked WH-T88-PROBE and deleted, with a re-count proving cleanup.

temporal-answer-names-its-window.label: T91: a temporal answer names its window — T91's audit oracle (2026-08-26). temporal-rag-orchestrator answers 'what changed since last month?' by decomposing a range into periods and folding per-period analyses into one comparison. Its FOLD_SYSTEM rule 7 tells the model to open with the resolved absolute range, because 'last week' is ambiguous - trailing 7 days versus calendar week, and the PHT boundary - and the numbers cannot be audited without it. FOUND: that rule was the ONLY thing enforcing it. The handler returned fold.answer verbatim and the resolved range never appeared in the response at all, so a model that skips rule 7 (models do) produces an answer whose numbers belong to a window nobody can name - two_windows_one_metric arriving through an LLM instead of a query, on figures a supervisor may carry into a meeting. ★THE REPO ALREADY HAD THE ANSWER: its WAT split says compute the hard facts in code and let the model write prose from them, exactly how the resume summary synthesis is built. The periods carry their own resolved boundaries, so the range is known before the model is called. It is now stated in code - prepended only when the model did not already do it, so a compliant answer is never labelled twice - and returned structurally as `covering`, so a consumer never parses prose to learn which window it is reading. Helpers were exercised against the artifact: omitted -> prepended, complied -> not duplicated, no periods -> unchanged. ★A PROMPT RULE IS NOT AN ENFORCEMENT - this gate exists because rule 7 was already written, and correct, and insufficient. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD all three checks fail.

narration-rail-holds-every-figure.label: T83: the narration rail holds EVERY figure — engineering-calc-agent's spoken-headline oracle (2026-08-26). The calc is computed deterministically; a model then writes the report narrative plus a spoken `narration` that must 'quote the single headline design value verbatim'. A rail already guarded that, commented 'AI-1 grounding rail: silence the spoken line if it quotes an unverifiable figure'. ★IT CHECKED THE OPPOSITE OF ITS OWN COMMENT: `nums.some(...)` passed as soon as ONE number matched a computed result, so 'Provide a 61 kW unit at 45.2 kW bus' passed on the 45.2 while the 61 was invented - and the invented number is the one SPOKEN as the headline, on a calculation an engineer signs. Measured against pre-fix HEAD that narration returned true; it now returns false, and pure fabrication is still caught, so this is a strict tightening rather than a rewrite. ★`every` ALONE WOULD HAVE BEEN ITS OWN FAILURE - a rail that mutes honest narrations teaches people to ignore it. Narrations legitimately carry figures that are not results: the INPUTS they were computed from, small counts ('2 units'), and standard designations ('IEC 62305-3', 'PEC 2017'). Those are exempted by name; everything else must match a computed value within tolerance, and at least one must be a real RESULT so that merely echoing the inputs does not count as quoting the answer. Seven cases were exercised against the shipped function, one per exemption. Teeth: all five checks fail against pre-fix HEAD.

missing-brief-says-so.label: T81: a missing brief says so — T81's AMC freshness oracle (2026-08-26). The 6am PHT cron writes one amc_briefings row per shift_date and alert-hub reads only TODAY's. That scoping is right and stays: yesterday's brief must never pose as this morning's. ★BUT WHEN THE CRON MISSED, THE CARD VANISHED - renderAmcCard(null) set display:none, so a supervisor could not tell 'no brief ran today' from 'this feature does not exist' or 'the page is still loading'. Worse, a skeleton is rendered in that card on first load, so the sequence was a loading state resolving into NOTHING: an answer erasing itself, on a surface whose whole promise is a brief every morning. On a missed morning the absence IS the news. It now stays visible, says no brief was generated for this shift, names the 6am cadence so the reader knows what was missed, points at the most recent brief the page already fetched (marked as not a substitute), and blanks the figure tiles so no number stands under a 'not generated' header. BOTH DIRECTIONS: with today's row absent the card speaks; with the real row it still renders the brief and does not claim absence - the second half matters, since a card that always cried 'no brief' would satisfy the first while destroying the feature. ★NO DATA IS MUTATED: only the today-scoped read (shift_date=eq.) is intercepted, so the historic query answers for real, which is what lets the empty state name the most recent brief. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the card reads shown=false.

converted-money-states-its-rate.label: T89: converted money states its rate — the owner's AI-cost oracle (2026-08-26). ai-quality's cost card is the owner's answer to 'what is this costing me'. Every peso figure on it - the hero, the per-call average, and the MODEST / TYPICAL / HEAVY verdict thresholds - came from one hardcoded constant, PHP_PER_USD = 56, which was neither dated nor shown. PHP/USD has moved between roughly 50 and 59 in recent years, so a drifting rate silently shifts both the number and the JUDGEMENT about it, while the card reads like a measurement. The figure is not so much wrong as unfalsifiable: an owner cannot tell whether ₱2,100 means 'heavy use' or 'the rate is stale'. The rate is now stated beside the figure, the way a source chip states a window. ★IT DOES NOT DEMAND A LIVE RATE - a fixed rate is a reasonable choice for a cost estimate; presenting the result as if nothing was assumed is not. Checked and found CORRECT rather than manufactured into a defect: the conversion itself is sound (php = totalCost * PHP_PER_USD, and the thresholds compare pesos to pesos), and the details table's USD figure is labelled as USD. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the rate is undisclosed and the gate names the line.

quota-warns-before-the-wall.label: T89: the quota warns before the wall — a count is not a warning (2026-08-26). _shared/rate-limit.ts returns `remaining` on EVERY allowed call, so the platform always knows how close a hive is to its hourly cap. NOTHING CONSUMED IT: there is no threshold anywhere in the codebase, and the only signal a worker ever got was the 429 AFTER the wall - mid-task, with the work half done. asset-hub was the single surface rendering the number at all, and it rendered it flat ('12 AI calls remaining this hour'), which reads the same at 12 as at 1. whQuotaNotice() now turns the number the server already sends into a warning at 5 or fewer and names the reset, so 'wait' has a 'how long'. ★THE UNKNOWN CASE WAS A BUG IN THE FIRST VERSION, caught by exercising the shipped helper rather than trusting it: Number(null) is 0, so a quota the server did not report was announced as 'No AI calls left this hour' - absence rendered as a value, alarming and false.
