An absent reading is not a reading of zero; it is now silent. ★IT DOES NOT REQUIRE EVERY AI SURFACE TO SHOW A QUOTA - most never receive `remaining`, and demanding that plumbing everywhere would make this a migration rather than a gate; it holds the surfaces that DO show it to showing it usefully. ★AND ITS OWN MATCHER WAS BLIND FIRST: it looked for 'whQuotaNotice(' while utils.js defines it as 'whQuotaNotice = function', so it reported the helper missing while it sat ten lines above - it would have failed forever on a correct file. Teeth: pre-fix it flags both the bare render and the absent helper.

verdict-needs-a-denominator.label: T65: a verdict needs a denominator — ai-quality's trust-card oracle (2026-08-26). The Worker Trust card is where an owner decides whether the AI is worth paying for. It turned thumbs into a percentage and then into a VERDICT: HEALTHY in green at 70%+, WATCH in amber, LOW TRUST in red below 50%. FOUND: no sample floor. With a SINGLE rating the card read '100% · HEALTHY' in green, or '0% · LOW TRUST' in red - a confident judgement about the whole AI layer from one tap. The zero case was already handled honestly ('NO DATA') and the raw counts already sat beside the figure, so the gap was narrow and specific: a percentage needs a denominator before it can carry a verdict, and below about five ratings a single tap moves it twenty points or more. The number is still shown - hiding it would be its own dishonesty - but it is not dressed as a verdict until it can support one, and the card says what would make it meaningful. Exercised against the shipped branch: 1 and 4 ratings read TOO FEW RATINGS in grey, 5+ resolve to a real tag, and a genuine 2-up/8-down still lands as LOW TRUST in red. ★THE POINT IS NOT TO HIDE BAD NEWS - the gate also fails if the real verdicts disappear, since a card that never judges is its own failure. ★SAME DISCIPLINE THE RELIABILITY WORKBENCH APPLIES to a Weibull fit with too few failures: say the sample is too small and what would fix it, rather than fitting a curve to three points.

search-button-is-not-dead.label: T78: the search button is not dead — the spine's dead-control oracle (2026-08-26). nav-hub.js is on every page and lazy-loads search-overlay.js asynchronously, so window.WHSearch is briefly absent on EVERY page load and permanently absent if that request fails - a cache miss, a bad deploy, a flaky plant connection. ★THE HANDLER HAD ONLY THE HAPPY BRANCH: `if (window.WHSearch) { open() }` and nothing else, so a press with the script missing did nothing whatsoever. MEASURED with search-overlay.js answered 404: the overlay never opened, NOTHING was said, and there were zero page errors - the exact shape of a control that looks alive and is not, on the one element every page carries. It now retries the load once (the usual cause is a request that had not landed yet) and then says why it cannot open. A search that will not start is a small failure; a button that swallows the press teaches the worker the platform is broken and gives them nothing to do about it. BOTH DIRECTIONS: healthy opens the overlay and does not cry unavailable; script-dead does not open and says so - the first half is what stops the fix from being 'always claim it is broken'. Driven at 390, because the hub is the phone's only navigation. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the dead-script case reads saysUnavailable=false.

filter-vocabulary-is-complete.label: T64: the filter vocabulary is complete — audit-log's compliance oracle (2026-08-26). The feed reads the newest 500 rows, which is right for a scrolling feed. The filter dropdowns were then built from THAT array, so the choices offered were whatever happened to fall inside the cap. MEASURED on the fixture hive: 3,402 audit rows, 4 distinct actors and 22 distinct actions overall, but only 3 actors and 18 actions inside the newest 500. A supervisor could not filter to one of the four people who acted, or to 4 of the 22 action types, and nothing said the list was partial. On a compliance surface 'no option for that person' reads as 'that person did nothing' - the opposite of what an audit trail is for. ★SAME CLASS THIS FILE HAD ALREADY FIXED FOR THE CSV EXPORT, one function away, which is the tell: the cap was removed where someone had looked and left where nobody had. The options now come from their own complete pass, paged past the cap with the same hive scope, reading only three short columns, and falling back to the capped set if that pass fails - a short list beats no list. THE ASSERTION: the option lists match the DISTINCT values in the DATABASE, which is the oracle, so it cannot drift into checking the page against itself. ★THE FIX'S OWN FIRST VERSION FAILED LIVE: it declared its cache with `let` further down the file than the async path that reads it - a temporal dead zone - so the page threw ReferenceError on first paint and every dropdown came back EMPTY. No syntax check sees that, which is why this gate is live rather than static. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the page offers 3 actors and 18 actions against the database's 4 and 22.

freshness-stamp-tracks-content.label: T39: a freshness stamp tracks its content — alert-hub's background-upgrade oracle (2026-08-26). The AMC card serves the stored 6am brief instantly, then calls analytics-orchestrator as a background UPGRADE. renderAmcCard stamps the meta 'stored brief, generated <time>', which is exactly right while the stored copy is showing. ★THE UPGRADE REPLACED THE SUMMARY AND LEFT THE STAMP: on success the pane held a freshly composed action brief under a line saying it came from this morning's stored row. Not a stale number - a stale CLAIM ABOUT a number, harder to catch because everything on screen looks internally consistent, and it lands on a supervisor deciding what to do with their shift. ★THE FAILURE PATH WAS ALREADY HONEST and is deliberately untouched: it keeps the stored summary AND the stored stamp, which agree - a silent keep is right for a background upgrade, since the reader still has a brief. BOTH DIRECTIONS are driven, because a fix that stamped 'live' unconditionally would satisfy the first while making the second lie. Found while censusing T39's real question: 11 of 12 AI-invoking surfaces already distinguish a quota refusal from a network failure - this was the twelfth, and its answer turned out to be a stamp rather than a message. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD a successful upgrade still reads 'stored brief'.

engineer-lens-is-one-lens.label: T52: the engineer lens is one lens — asset-hub / nav-hub coherence oracle (2026-08-26). There is no engineer ROLE on this platform: hive_members.role is CHECK-constrained to worker | supervisor. 'Engineer' exists TWICE as a lens - nav-hub's localStorage 'wh_nav_mode' (which filters TOOLS) and asset-hub's 'wh_asset_view' (which decides PANELS) - independent keys sharing one user-facing word. TWO DEFECTS, both user-visible: (1) someone who picked the Engineer lens in the hub still landed in asset-hub's WORKER view, because an unset wh_asset_view reads as false - they declared themselves once and had to declare it again, with nothing saying a second switch existed; (2) _syncAssetView ran from exactly two places (the toggle's click handler and loadDetailFmea), so on a fresh load the button kept its markup default and read 'Show Reliability Workbench' - i.e. OFF - even for someone whose stored choice was engineer, who would then press it to enable what was already enabled and disable it. ★THE FIX IS A DEFAULT, NOT A MERGE: the scopes genuinely differ, so only the UNSET case derives from the hub lens and an explicit local toggle still wins. Four cases are driven for exactly that reason - a fix that merely mirrored the hub would pass the first two and destroy the local choice. ★AND THE ORACLE TOOK THREE TRIES, which is the transferable part: asking the helper directly failed pre-fix with 'noFn' (a fact about the patch, not the user); reading the reliability CARD failed the other way, since it lives in the detail pane and is hidden at load regardless of lens; the honest signal is the toggle's aria-expanded, set straight from the lens and present in the pre-fix world so the comparison is real. Teeth: pre-fix, cases 1 and 4 both fail.

old-draft-says-its-age.label: T57: an old draft says its age — the dormant-return oracle (2026-08-26). whAutoSaveDraft is X2 interruption resilience, and it is careful work: it refuses a draft belonging to another worker (the shared-device leak), detects an untouched SELECT by its default rather than by emptiness (the 'Critical' urgency that silently reverted to 'Normal'), and says where drafts live. ★BUT IT CARRIED NO AGE: a draft typed three months ago restored into the form exactly like one typed three minutes ago - silently, into fields the worker is about to submit. On a logbook entry that means filing a stale reading against today's shift with nothing having said the text was old. Interruption resilience is measured in minutes and hours; a draft that survives a WEEK has stopped being an interruption and become a leftover. ★IT SAYS THE AGE RATHER THAN DISCARDING THE TEXT - the work is still the worker's to keep or clear, and throwing a note away because it is old would be the opposite failure, since X2 exists precisely so typed work is never lost. FOUR AGES ARE DRIVEN, because a notice that always fired would be noise and one that never fired would be the bug: 0d and 6d restore silently, 8d and 90d restore and say how old they are. ★THE PROBE MUST SIGN IN - the owner check compares against wh_last_worker, and unauthenticated the page redirects to index where the owner reads null, so the draft is correctly refused and nothing restores; an earlier run reported restored:false four times and looked like a broken fix. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD the 90-day draft restores with saysAge=false.

maturity-says-yes-too.label: T187: the maturity ladder says yes too — the month-three oracle (2026-08-26). maturity-gate told a hive what it could not have yet ('unlocks at Stair 2', 'reach Stair 3') on every gated surface, and said NOTHING when the hive crossed one. A plant that spent three months building logbook history earned Stair 2 in SILENCE: the refusal simply stopped appearing, which nobody notices, because noticing an absence is not how people work. The entire premise of the ladder is that patience is rewarded, and the reward was never announced - a one-directional system that only ever refuses teaches people it is a wall. It now says so once, on the first gated surface loaded after the crossing. ★DETECTED CENTRALLY in checkMaturityGate, because every gated page already calls it and only the FIRST after a crossing should speak - per-page detection would have congratulated the same climb on every surface visited. ★KEYED BY HIVE, so a multi-hive contractor never gets one hive's progress announced as another's. ★RISE ONLY, deliberately: readiness DECAYS if logging stops, and telling someone unprompted that they have been demoted, on whatever page they happened to open, is a different and crueller feature - the refusal messages already explain what is missing at the next gate. ★AND FIRST SIGHT IS SILENT: with no previous reading there is no crossing, only a baseline, and without that every worker's first page load would congratulate them. Exercised against the shipped helper (first sight silent, 1->2 announces, repeat silent, 2->3 announces, 3->1 silent) and verified live: a gated page still locks, the baseline is written per hive, 0 page errors. Teeth: against pre-fix HEAD there is no announcement at all.

invite-code-round-trip.label: T6/T7/T185: the invite-code round trip — the briefing-room exchange (2026-08-26). The platform's whole onboarding rests on one exchange: a supervisor creates a hive and reads a six-character code aloud; a worker types it on their phone and is in. It was walked on prod as a smoke test and GATED BY NOTHING - T6 sat at 90% and T7 at 85% with no gate registered against either, so the most load-bearing flow on the platform was protected by nobody. ★TWO BROWSER CONTEXTS, because this is a two-person exchange and a single-context test cannot fail the way the real thing fails: the supervisor's browser creates the hive, and a SEPARATE context signed in as a DIFFERENT real account joins with the code, with nothing passing between them but the six characters - exactly the channel the real flow uses. THE ASSERTIONS: the code is six readable characters; a different account joins and lands in the SAME hive, confirmed in the DATABASE rather than by reading a success banner (a banner is what a broken join would also show); and a WRONG code is refused out loud without joining anything. ★DIRECTION THREE RUNS FIRST, deliberately - a join that accepted anything would sail through the other two, and checking the wrong code before the right one means a permissive join cannot hide behind a later success. ★AND IT CLEANS UP: the probe hive and its memberships are removed and re-counted; two consecutive runs left 0 probe hives, an unchanged membership count on the joining account, and 0 orphaned memberships. This is also the first slice of T185's day-one choreography, which is the same exchange at six-context scale.

no-raw-enum.label: CE: no raw enum reaches a person (2026-08-26). `in_progress`, `rate_limit_exceeded`, `cancelled_by_provider` are how a COLUMN stores a state, not how a person says it - and when one reaches the screen the reader translates the schema in their head. The states that leak are usually the ones that matter: a refusal, a failure, a half-finished job. ★THE SHAPE IS THE TELL, which makes this decidable rather than a matter of taste: a short visible text leaf matching lowercase_with_underscores is a raw token with near-certainty, because nobody writes English that way. ★WHY THIS GATE EXISTS AT ALL: the PROVER did not run. tools/prove_no_raw_enum.mjs was built, works, and was invoked by NOTHING - an audit of 106 prove_*.mjs harnesses found 3 that no file in the repo mentions, and this was the most valuable. It passes 22 pages with 0 failures and 0 ungraded, so the property was already true; what was missing was anything to keep it that way, and a working oracle nobody runs is indistinguishable from one never written. ★AND THE AUDIT THAT FOUND IT OVER-REPORTED FIRST: scanning only the gate registry and validate_*.py wrappers called 15 provers orphaned; widening to every .py/.mjs/.js/.md/.json/.sh/.yml cut it to 3 - the same correction the double-submit census needed when 118 flagged handlers turned out to be 4. ★A ZERO DENOMINATOR IS NOT A PASS: if the prover grades 0 pages the gate FAILS, because that means its matcher or roster broke rather than the platform being clean.

longest-truncates.label: CF: the longest realistic value truncates (2026-08-26). Real plants name things badly - a part called 'Bearing, spherical roller, 22320 E1 XL C3, SKF, for kiln drive gearbox non-drive end' is not a stress test, it is Tuesday, and the card holding it was laid out around a nine-character example. THE ORACLE: the longest realistic title truncates VISIBLY rather than overflowing its card or pushing the price out of view, measured by INJECTING the long value and watching the layout rather than reasoning about CSS - the only way to catch a container that grows silently until the thing beside it is off-screen. ★WHY THIS GATE EXISTS: the prover ran nowhere. An audit of 106 prove_*.mjs harnesses found 3 that no file in the repo mentions; this was one, and it works - 18 pages pass, 0 fail. The property was already held and nothing was keeping it that way. ★UNGRADED IS NOT PASS, and the prover already knew it: 4 pages report UNGRADED because no rendered row title existed to lengthen, and it says so rather than counting them clean. The wrapper carries that through and also FAILS on a zero tally, because nothing-measured means the roster or selector broke, not that the layout is sound.

join-names-the-namesake.label: T185: two people who share a name both get into the hive (2026-08-26). A plant pilots WorkHive and five workers are handed ONE invite code at the morning briefing; two of them are named Juan Dela Cruz, which in a Philippine plant is not a contrived edge case, it is Tuesday. The first joins. The second - a different human being, a different auth identity, the correct code - hit `duplicate key value violates unique constraint hive_members_hive_id_worker_name_key`, and hive.html rendered it VERBATIM via 'Could not join: ' + joinErr.message. Three failures at once: he cannot join his team, he is shown database internals, and he is offered no way forward, on the pilot's first morning. ★THE CONSTRAINT IS RIGHT AND STAYS: worker_name is the attribution key across many tables, so two identical names inside one hive would make every by-name rollup ambiguous. The defect was never the constraint - it was that the function let the constraint speak to the user. ★TWO CASES RAISE THE IDENTICAL 23505 AND MUST NOT GET THE SAME ANSWER, which is why this gate runs a REAL race rather than reading the source: a genuine namesake must be refused BY NAME (HIVE_NAME_TAKEN) so the page can offer a distinguishing one, while the SAME user double-tapping Join must be told 'you are in' - two concurrent calls both read no membership under READ COMMITTED and both insert, so the idempotent path is BYPASSED by the race and only the exception handler can tell them apart by re-reading who won. Measured: pre-fix, the double-tap surfaced the raw violation too. ★THE RACE IS MADE DETERMINISTIC by holding an UNCOMMITTED insert in one session while the RPC runs in another, so it blocks on the unique index and takes the handler for real. ★AND THE REMEDY MUST BE WALKABLE: the join form carries only a code input, so naming the cause without offering a name field is a dead end - the gate asserts the branch, the revealed input, and that the chosen name is persisted to wh_last_worker, since otherwise the roster would show the new name while every later write attributed to the old.

records-linked-is-true.label: CF: the signup notice may only claim what was actually linked (2026-08-26). After creating an account index.html could announce 'Your existing records as <name> are now linked to your account' - and it decided that by COUNTING v_worker_truth rows matching the display name. That view exposes worker_profiles.display_name and is security_invoker, so under RLS a brand-new user can see exactly ONE row: the profile the very same flow inserted moments earlier. ★MEASURED on a fresh identity with no hive: c2_count = 1, visible_rows = 1 - so the count was always >= 1 and EVERY new signup was told their existing records had been linked. For someone who had none that is false; for a namesake it claims another person's work history, which is the same identity-by-name trap that let a second Juan Dela Cruz be refused a hive. ★THE CHECK AND THE ACTION READ DIFFERENT ROWS: the reassurance was computed from PROFILE rows while the actual linking is done by resolveActiveHiveContext(), which reads MEMBERSHIP. The notice now rests on that function's return value - non-null exactly when a membership was found and linked - and NAMES the hive it landed in, so the claim says what it rests on. ★THE GATE RUNS THE DB HALF LIVE rather than only reading the page, because the page assertion alone would not explain itself: it re-seeds a membership-less identity and re-measures the self-match, so if that count ever stops being 1 the gate says the PREMISE changed instead of passing quietly.

hive-seating-is-by-identity.label: I-pillar: which hive a session is seated in is decided by AUTH, not by a name (2026-08-26). resolveActiveHiveContext() in index.html chooses the tenant a signed-in session lands in, and it selected memberships with .eq('worker_name', displayName) - where worker_name in v_worker_truth is worker_profiles.display_name. So the query asked 'which memberships belong to this NAME' and depended entirely on the profiles_read_own RLS policy (auth_uid = auth.uid()) to turn that into 'which memberships are MINE'. ★CORRECT, AND FOR THE WRONG REASON - which is the whole point: measured, a caller sees exactly ONE profile row, so the name filter could only ever match themselves and there was no live defect. But the safety lived in the POLICY, not in the query, and widening profile reads even slightly - a co-member roster is an ordinary thing to want - would have let a NAMESAKE's memberships resolve here and seated a person in a hive they do not belong to. The view already joins membership on hm.auth_uid = wp.auth_uid, so the name filter bought nothing the identity does not buy more safely. Verified no behaviour change on a real multi-hive account: both filters return the same two memberships. ★THIS IS THE THIRD FACE OF ONE DEFECT, all found the same day: a hive join that refused a second Juan Dela Cruz by unique index, a signup notice that counted its own freshly-written profile row, and a tenant seat chosen by name. A name is not an identity. ★BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED because either can rot: the page must filter by identity AND worker_profiles SELECT must still be self-scoped - if that policy widens, the gate says so rather than passing quietly, since that widening is precisely what would have made the old code dangerous. An unknown identity must mean SOLO MODE, never a name guess. Teeth: reverting the filter to worker_name goes RED on both assertions.

invite-code-is-unguessable.label: T185/security: the one credential that admits a stranger to a plant (2026-08-26). A hive's 6-character invite code is the whole of what stands between an outsider and a plant's maintenance records - hand it over and you are in - and it was generated with Math.random(), a plain PRNG whose internal state is recoverable from a handful of observed outputs, making later codes from the same page predictable. There was no compatibility excuse: createHive already REQUIRES crypto.randomUUID() (a null id aborts the create), so the page depended on modern crypto two lines away. ★THE CENSUS IS WHY THIS GATE IS NARROW AND NOT A BAN: 31 Math.random() uses across the production pages and exactly ONE was a credential - the rest are element ids, upload filenames, retry jitter and an analytics session id that already prefers randomUUID, all cases where collision resistance matters and unpredictability does not. Banning Math.random outright would have raised 30 false findings and taught everyone to ignore the gate. ★IT ALSO GUARDS THE MODULO, the part a future editor breaks silently: mapping random bytes with `b % len` is unbiased ONLY when len divides 256. The alphabet is 32 characters (O/0/I/1 omitted so a code survives being read aloud in a noisy plant) and 256 % 32 = 0, so each character gets exactly 8 byte values; add one character for readability and the first 256 % len characters quietly become likelier. The gate COMPUTES that rather than trusting it - teeth-proven by a 30-character alphabet, which it caught as favouring the first 16. ★COLLISIONS WERE ALREADY SAFE and were checked before being claimed: hives carries UNIQUE (invite_code), so a repeat is a clean create failure routed through whWriteError ('Nothing was made; try again'), never a cross-tenant join into the wrong plant.

password-change-reachable.label: T59: a signed-in worker can find how to change their password (2026-08-26). MEASURED, and the answer was that the surface does not exist: there is no settings, account or profile page anywhere in the roster, and the ONLY password write on the platform runs inside the PASSWORD_RECOVERY auth event - so changing a password meant leaving the app, finding 'Forgot your password?' on the LANDING page, and waiting for an email. Nothing anywhere said so, leaving a security-conscious user hunting for a settings page that was never built. ★THE ROADMAP'S BAR IS 'findable and walkable, OR honestly stated absent' AND IT WAS NEITHER - which is why this was fixable without waiting on the product decision. It does NOT build the account surface (active sessions, sign-out-everywhere, 2FA remain Ian's call); it surfaces the flow that ALREADY WORKS, in the one place this platform keeps account actions - beside Sign Out on the ops-home header - reusing window.forgotPassword, whose copy already handles the case that matters most here: the many field workers with no email on file are told to ask their supervisor. ★THE GATE IS LIVE BECAUSE A STATIC CHECK CANNOT ANSWER THIS: a button whose handler throws, or which renders behind a hidden panel, reads identically in source to one that works. It signs in at 390, asserts the control is VISIBLE, meets the 44px touch floor a gloved hand needs, and that CLICKING it produces a prompt with an input and copy explaining what will happen. ★FIL PARITY IS PART OF THE FIX, not an afterthought - the new [data-i] key carries 'Palitan ang Password', verified live by flipping the toggle, because a data-i the swapper does not know silently stays English for every Filipino user. Teeth: removing the control reports that a signed-in worker has NO way to change their password.

return-promise-survives-reauth.label: T8: re-authenticating costs one sign-in, not your place (2026-08-26). When a token expires, session-timeout.js sends the worker to index.html?signin=1&return=<where they were>, and index.html validates that value before honouring it - an open-redirect guard, and the right instinct. But the guard's character class did not include characters the platform's OWN pages write into their URLs. ★MEASURED BY ROUND-TRIPPING THE REAL CHAIN (page writes filter -> session-timeout captures -> index re-reads): URLSearchParams.set() encodes a space as '+', and audit-log.html mirrors its filters into the URL including `actor`, which is a worker's NAME - so `audit-log.html?actor=Leandro+Marquez` and `audit-log.html?q=pump+seal` both failed the guard and were dropped IN SILENCE, landing the supervisor on the dashboard. That is T28's exact scenario, someone mid-investigation into who changed what, losing their place to a token refresh with nothing on screen explaining why. ★WHY WIDENING TO + , : IS SAFE, ARGUED NOT ASSUMED: the guard's job is to refuse a scheme, a protocol-relative //, and a foreign absolute path, and its ANCHOR already requires the value to begin with <name>.html or /workhive/ - so those three can only appear AFTER the ? or #, where a colon cannot read as a scheme and a plus is just a space. The gate proves both halves rather than trusting the argument: 8 real destinations survive AND 10 attack shapes (javascript:, //evil.com, https://, ../../, backslash-UNC, index.html@evil.com) are still refused. ★IT EXTRACTS THE REGEX FROM index.html instead of restating it, because a gate holding its own copy proves only that the copy is fine - and it FAILS IF THE THREE GUARDS DISAGREE (sign-in, signup, entry bridge), since a fix reaching one path and not the others is how this class survives. Teeth proven on both: the pre-fix class resurrects the two dropped destinations, and reverting a SINGLE guard is caught as disagreement.

signout-says-why.label: T8: the sign-in screen says WHY the worker is looking at it (2026-08-26). A worker mid-task looks up and finds a sign-in modal with no explanation, which is indistinguishable from being logged out at random - and the question in their head goes unanswered: did I lose what I was doing? ★ONE FUNCTION, THREE EVENTS, THREE DIFFERENT TRUTHS: session-timeout.js's clearIdentityHard() runs for an automatic idle timeout, for the worker deliberately pressing Sign out, AND (via the storage listener) for a sign-out in another tab. Telling someone who just pressed Sign out that their session 'timed out' is false, so the reason is now a parameter, the deliberate path passes none, and the gate asserts that separation - collapsing it is the easy mistake, and passing clearIdentityHard straight to addEventListener would make the click EVENT the reason. ★THE REAL ASSERTION IS THE CLAIM'S PRECONDITION, NOT THE WORDING: the notice tells an idle-timed-out worker 'your drafts are still here', which is true ONLY because clearIdentityHard wipes identity keys alone (wh_last_worker + the hive keys) and never touches whAutoSaveDraft storage. Add a draft key to that wipe list and the copy silently becomes a lie no test would catch - so the gate READS the wipe list and fails on anything draft-shaped. A claim has to rest on something; this is the something. ★AND THE COPY IS A WHITELIST, NOT INTERPOLATION: ?reason= comes from the URL, so it is looked up in a fixed table and written with textContent, and an unknown value renders NOTHING - verified live across four cases (idle and othertab show; a deliberate sign-in and a nonsense reason stay silent). role=status so a screen-reader user is told too. Teeth proven on all three.

collision-is-not-try-again.label: CE: a permanent collision must not be answered with 'try again' (2026-08-26). whWriteError is the write-error taxonomy, and it already understood this principle for DELIBERATE refusals - it passes 23514/42501/P0001 through in the guard's own words, with a note in the source explaining why: a seller told 'Save failed. Try again.' instead of 'Listing needs PHP50 credits held and you have 0 available' will retry forever, because retrying is precisely what cannot work. ★23505 HAD THE SAME PROBLEM AND WAS NOT ON THE LIST. A unique violation is permanent - the name, tag, code or username is TAKEN - so it fell to the caller's fallback. Measured before fixing, by calling the real function: a duplicate asset tag and a raced username BOTH returned 'The save did not go through. Nothing changed; try again.' It reaches real surfaces on day one: asset_nodes is UNIQUE (hive_id, tag), so two P-101s collide while a plant registers its equipment, and worker_profiles is UNIQUE (username). Now says the value is already taken and to change it - an action that CAN work. ★THE SENTENCE STAYS GENERIC ON PURPOSE: the only clue to WHICH field collided is the constraint name, a schema word no reader should see, and the gate asserts that no constraint name, 'duplicate key' or error code reaches the sentence. ★IT EXERCISES THE FUNCTION RATHER THAN GREPPING FOR THE BRANCH - a grep proves a line exists; only calling whWriteError with real error objects proves what a person is TOLD, and the same call guards the two things that must not change (deliberate refusals still speak for themselves; unrelated errors still fall through). ★AND ITS FIRST TEETH TEST WAS A FALSE RED: Node 24 makes `navigator` getter-only, so the shim threw and the prover exited 1 for a reason unrelated to the code under test. Fixed with defineProperty and re-teethed honestly - a RED you did not cause is not proof of anything.

day-one-parallel-join.label: T185 slice 1: five workers, one invite code, the same minute (2026-08-26). The scenario the trajectory is named for - a supervisor reads ONE code out at the morning briefing and the crew types it in at once. It is the first thing that has to work on a pilot's first day, because if two of the five silently fail to join, the pilot is over before anyone logs a repair. ★DISTINCT FROM join-names-the-namesake, which proves the RPC's behaviour for a SINGLE caller (named refusal, idempotent double-tap). This puts N DISTINCT identities on the same hive row and the same unique index CONCURRENTLY - spawned, not awaited in turn, so the contention is real rather than staged - and asserts the three things that can go wrong: nobody is silently lost, nobody lands TWICE, and the one who shares a teammate's name is refused BY NAME rather than by the raw index. Measured: 5 workers, 4 joined exactly once each, 1 HIVE_NAME_TAKEN, 4 rows for 4 identities. ★IT CHECKS THE DATABASE, NOT THE RETURN VALUES - what each session reported is only half the story; the row count and the DISTINCT identity count are what would expose a double-join under a race. ★AND IT CLEANS UP AND RE-COUNTS, because a prober that litters a shared database is a defect of its own; every row it makes carries a WH-T185-PARALLEL marker and residue is asserted at 0. ★ITS FIRST RUN REPORTED THE PLATFORM BROKEN AND THE PLATFORM WAS RIGHT: the fixture gave 'the namesake' its own distinct name, so 5 distinct names correctly produced 5 joins and the collision assertion fired against nothing. An assertion is only as good as the situation it actually sets up. Teeth: against the pre-fix RPC worker 2 hits the raw unique index under the same concurrency.

hive-at-scale.label: T61 slice 1: the people surfaces at 20 members (2026-08-26). Every seeded hive on this platform is small - 8 members in the largest - so the roster, the standings and the assignee pickers have only ever been read at a size where nothing can go wrong. A roster of 8 fits on a phone; 20 is where ordering, truncation and find-a-person begin to matter, and where a count that disagrees with its list stops being invisible. ★THE FIXTURE IS ON-DEMAND, NOT STANDING, and that is the design decision worth keeping: a permanent 20-member hive would move the numbers every OTHER gate reads - member counts, standings, per-hive rollups - and a fixture that quietly changes someone else's denominator is worse than no fixture at all. It grows a marked hive, measures, removes it, and re-counts to prove the removal. ★IT ASSERTS AGREEMENT, NOT TASTE: the roster read returns EVERY member (a silent cap at 10 or 20 makes a 20-person crew look like a small team and nothing on screen says so - the row-cap class); the count equals the list; the ordering is TOTAL, name plus a tiebreak, so two members cannot swap places between refreshes; and no duplicate names slipped in, which at 20 generated members is a real test of the per-hive unique index rather than a formality. ★THE NAMES ARE FILIPINO AND DELIBERATELY COLLIDE-PRONE (shared given names, mixed lengths) so the ordering assertion means something - 'Worker 7' twenty times would sort perfectly and prove nothing. ★AND IT READS THE GLASS, NOT ONLY THE ROWS: rows agreeing is necessary and not sufficient, because the failure this trajectory is about is a COUNT that says 20 beside a LIST that shows 10 - which no database assertion can see. A second phase tops a real hive up to 20, signs in, expands the roster, and compares the rendered row count to the number printed next to it and to the database, then removes ONLY the marked fixtures so the hive's own members are never touched. Measured: 20 planted / 20 returned / 0 duplicates / order stable / residue 0, and live: 20 rendered, count '· 20', database 20. Teeth proven three ways - a silent cap, a non-total order, and a capped RENDER, which fires both live assertions at once ('rendered 10 of 20' and 'the number and the thing it counts disagree on the same screen').

export-reads-its-own-set.label: T129/T49: the file that leaves the building must be complete (2026-08-26). A logbook export is what an auditor reads, and it is the one artifact whose incompleteness the reader CANNOT see: a short LIST shows a Load more button, but a CSV carries no total, no window and no hint of omission. ★THE RECORDED INCIDENT: the team-branch export handed over `_teamEntries` - only what the feed had fetched, one 30-row page plus whatever Load more added - while the page said '517 entries'. A supervisor exporting a filtered team view for a DOLE/ISO trail got a file that looked whole. The mine branch had been fixed in an earlier arc; the team branch was the one nobody had walked. ★THREE ASSERTIONS: every exporter reads its OWN set by PAGING (a loop with .range) rather than reusing the render buffer, since an export sourced from a screen buffer inherits that buffer's cap; the paging carries a TOTAL order (sort key AND tiebreak), because a non-total order over a paged read can repeat one row and drop another - a file of the right LENGTH and the wrong CONTENTS, worse than a short one; and the property is NON-VACUOUS, checked against the database (largest hive 1,700 rows against a 30-row page) so it cannot pass on a table too small to fail. ★IT NAMES THE BUFFER IT FORBIDS rather than pattern-matching 'looks like an export', because the bug was one identifier. ★AND ITS FIRST VERSION MADE TWO FALSE ACCUSATIONS: a fixed 4000-character window ran past the function's end, through the next one and into the click handler, so it reported BOTH exporters as reusing the feed buffer when neither does - one hit was a COMMENT describing the old bug, the other the handler's ANNOUNCED fallback (which is correct behaviour: it exports the loaded window and says so in a toast). Bodies are now delimited by matching braces. A window sized to today's code is wrong the day someone documents something. Teeth proven on both the buffer reuse and a missing tiebreak.

print-is-readable-on-paper.label: T124: the printed page must not be the dark theme (2026-08-26). Plants run on paper - a PM schedule goes on the noticeboard, an audit trail into a folder for DOLE - and this platform is DARK. Printed without rules that is either a black sheet that empties a cartridge or, because most browsers drop backgrounds, pale grey text nobody can read. Neither failure appears anywhere ON SCREEN, which is exactly why it needs a gate: print CSS is invisible until it has already wasted someone's trip to the printer. MEASURED: the three pages a plant demonstrably prints already do this properly - white sheet, #111 text, the reset applied to DESCENDANTS (each card and chip carries its own dark background, so a rule on body alone leaves them), the hub/FAB/toasts/dialogs/buttons hidden, and page-break-inside on cards and table rows. This is a RATCHET over work already done, and the held set may not SHRINK - deleting the rules is not a way to pass. ★ITS FIRST VERSION MANUFACTURED FIVE FINDINGS AND ALL FIVE WERE WRONG, which is the part worth keeping: (1) it treated every @media print block as a claim to be printable, but asset-hub's block says in its own comment that it exists so the rule is 'reachable from document.styleSheets' for a DIFFERENT gate, and the report pages already render as light document panels where a dark-to-light reset would be redundant; (2) it read only the FIRST print block, and analytics-report carries SIX - the first being a one-line rule about a field's min-height - so five pages were graded on whichever rule sorted earliest; (3) its skip-list matched substrings against the ABSOLUTE path, and this project lives under '.../Self-learning Road-Map/...', which contains 'learn' - so it excluded EVERY page and reported '0 printable pages examined' while still failing. Three instrument errors before one true reading. ★AND ITS PASS LINE OVERSTATED until corrected: it claimed all 8 pages met the contract when only 3 are held. Teeth proven on a weakened rule AND on deletion.

xp-belongs-to-one-person.label: T17/T51: an XP ledger keyed by NAME merges two people who share one (2026-08-26). achievement_xp_log carries worker_name, achievement_id, xp_earned, source_action, source_id, earned_at, reversed_at - and NO auth_uid, NO hive_id - while its RLS reads `worker_name IN (SELECT auth_worker_names())`, so a row belongs to whoever answers to that name. ★THAT IS A HAZARD RATHER THAN A CHOICE because worker_name is unique PER HIVE, not globally: two different people in two different hives may both be Juan Dela Cruz, which in a Philippine plant is ordinary, and this table cannot tell them apart. Their totals merge, their LEVELS are computed from each other's work, and because the RLS predicate IS the name, each can READ the other's ledger - source_action and source_id describing work done in a hive they have never belonged to. ★MEASURED: it is NOT happening - 982 rows across 20 names, zero names held by two auth_uids - and that is precisely why the gate exists NOW. While every name still resolves to one person a backfill onto auth_uid is unambiguous; once two namesakes accumulate history the ledgers cannot be untangled, because nothing recorded which of them earned what. ★IT DETECTS THE TRIGGER AND DOES NOT PRETEND TO FIX IT: the remedy is an auth_uid column, backfilled while it is still possible, with the four read sites (achievements x2, logbook, pm-scheduler) and the RLS predicate moved onto it - a schema change to a ledger carrying reversal semantics, which is Ian's call rather than something to smuggle in. This fails the moment the condition appears, so the window to fix it cleanly cannot close unnoticed, and it PASSES ITSELF OUT once auth_uid exists rather than policing a dead condition. Teeth proven by creating a cross-hive namesake, which it named exactly.

rejection-reaches-the-submitter.label: T20: a refusal must reach the person who was refused (2026-08-26). A supervisor clearing the approval queue rejects an asset, a part, a change order; the item leaves the queue and their job is done - but the WORKER who submitted it is the one who has to act, and if all they ever see is 'Rejected' they resubmit the same thing, give up, or go and ask in person. A refusal that names no cause is a loop the platform opened and did not close. ★BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED because either alone is useless: every path writing status 'rejected' records a REASON in the SAME update (a reason captured later, or optionally, is a reason usually missing), and every surface that knows about the rejected state RENDERS it back (a column written and never read is the write-only class, and the submitter is the only person it was written for). ★IT PAIRS WRITES TO RENDERS BY TABLE, NOT BY PAGE, because the halves deliberately live apart: the supervisor rejects from hive.html and the worker reads the reason on inventory.html - a check demanding both in one file would fail the working design. MEASURED: all three paths already comply (hive's queue for asset_nodes AND inventory_items, asset-hub's own reject, project-manager's change orders), rendered as 'Why: ...', 'Why rejected: ... - fix it and resubmit via Edit', and 'Rejected: ...' - and asset-hub even says 'No reason recorded.' for rows predating the column rather than showing an empty box. Nothing was broken; nothing was guarding it, and a fourth reject path added later would have no reason to know the contract exists. ★ITS OWN FIRST RUN WRONGLY ACCUSED asset-hub, by matching a capitalised 'Rejected' caption when that page branches on `status === 'rejected'` inside a template - the state is a VALUE there, not a caption. Teeth proven on both halves.

asset-pm-handoff-carries-context.label: T21: scheduling a PM must not lose the asset (2026-08-26). A supervisor approves a new asset and the next thing they do is give it a maintenance program. If the link carries the asset that is one tap; if it does not, they arrive at a list of everything and have to re-find the asset they were just looking at - which on a phone, in a plant, is where the task gets abandoned. ★BOTH ENDS ARE ASSERTED, because a parameter nobody reads is a promise only the sender believes it is keeping - the declared-but-never-wired class: every pm-scheduler link rendered with an ASSET in hand carries its identity (?tag / ?asset / ?asset_id), AND pm-scheduler actually consumes them (it reads all four: asset_id, asset, pm_id, tag). ★EMPTY-STATE LINKS ARE EXEMPT AND IT IS NOT A LOOPHOLE: asset-hub's two bare links both sit under 'No approved assets in this hive yet', where there is no asset to name and demanding a parameter would be demanding a lie - and the exemption is decided by the surrounding TEXT, not by an allowlist a later edit could quietly join. MEASURED: 2 links carry the asset, 2 are bare in genuine empty states. ★ITS FIRST RUN ACCUSED A COMMENT - 'Canonical PM frequencies (match pm-scheduler.html's FREQ registry)' - because it matched the bare filename anywhere; a mention is not a navigation, so it now matches only href= and .href= assignments. Teeth proven by dropping the asset from a real link.

flagged-post-tells-its-author.label: T24: a reported post must not vanish on the person who wrote it (2026-08-26). When a teammate reports a post the platform hides it from the hive until a supervisor rules, and the easy way to build that is ONE predicate - hide every flagged post from every worker - which is wrong for exactly one person: the AUTHOR, who wrote something, watched it disappear, and was told nothing. They re-post it or conclude the app is broken, and either way the moderation nobody has done yet has already cost their trust. ★THREE PARTIES, THREE OBLIGATIONS: the author keeps seeing their OWN flagged post (the feed query must EXEMPT their rows, not merely filter flagged=false); the author is TOLD in words what happened, who decides, and that teammates cannot see it meanwhile (a post that reappears unexplained is barely better than one that vanished); and the SUPERVISOR sees the REPORTER'S REASON on the card, because judging a flag without knowing why it was raised means opening the audit log first, and a queue that costs a tab is a queue that waits. ★IT CHECKS THE QUERY PREDICATE, NOT JUST THE BADGE, and that is the half a page-level check would miss entirely: if the row is filtered out server-side the badge is unreachable, so the render can be perfectly correct while the author still never sees their post. MEASURED: all three hold today - the author exemption, the UNDER REVIEW state carrying its explanation, and the reporter's reason inline for the supervisor. Teeth proven on the predicate and on the notice.

absent-money-is-not-zero.label: T94: a peso amount that did not arrive must not render as zero (2026-08-26). '₱0.00' is a confident statement that something moved nothing, and when the number is actually ABSENT - a read that failed, a view column reported nullable, a join that missed - printing zero trades a VISIBLE defect (₱NaN) for an INVISIBLE one. Recorded incidents: a filed top-up of ₱300 rendered as ₱0.00, and a ledger line of unknown value as '+₱0', which says the entry moved nothing - the most misleading thing a ledger can say. ★THE GUARANTEE IS CENTRAL, so the gate checks the centre first: whFmtPeso returns a GAP for null/undefined/'' and for anything non-finite, while a REAL zero still prints ₱0 - a person can act on 'we do not know' and cannot act on a wrong number. ★AND IT CHECKS THE BYPASS, because a helper is only as good as its use: `'₱' + Number(x || 0)` is the exact resurrection, since Number(null) is 0 AND finite. That is permitted ONLY as the else-branch of a `typeof whFmtPeso === 'function'` fallback, for a page whose utils.js did not load. ★IT MATTERS THOUGH THE BASE TABLES ARE NOT NULL: Postgres does not propagate NOT NULL through a VIEW, so every v_*_truth column reports nullable and these reads go through views - the door is already open and the helper is what stands in it. ★FOUR DELIMITERS BEFORE ONE THAT WORKED, all kept in the source: a 260-char lookback found an UNRELATED helper's typeof check two lines up and exempted a real bypass (this clause's teeth test passed GREEN); the nearest brace cut the expression at the `{` inside `{ decimals: 2 }` and accused three legitimate fallbacks; a statement walk starting one line UP walked past the bypass's own `const` into the helper above and inherited its check - green again. Only a walk beginning at the hit's OWN line is right. Teeth proven on both clauses.

watchlist-says-what-it-does.label: T95: a bookmark must not imply a subscription (2026-08-26). Tapping a star on a listing looks like 'tell me when this changes'. Here it is a BOOKMARK - nothing consumes marketplace_watchlist to send price or stock alerts - and a buyer who believes otherwise STOPS CHECKING the listing and misses the very change they were watching for. The feature would do harm precisely by seeming to work. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY HANDLES THIS WELL, which is why this is a PARITY check and not a defect report: marketplace.html says outright "WorkHive doesn't send watchlist alerts yet." Stating an absence plainly is the honest answer to a capability you have not built. ★AND IT IS ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which most claim-checks are not: while nothing consumes the watchlist the disclosure must be PRESENT (deleting the sentence silently restores the implied promise), and once something DOES consume it the disclosure must GO - a stale 'doesn't send alerts yet' under a feature that now sends them is the same defect pointing the other way, and it teaches people to ignore the one place the product tells them the truth. A claim and a capability drift apart in either direction; a gate watching only one of them is half a gate. ★A CONSUMER MEANS AN EDGE FUNCTION OR CRON, not a page reading its own list to draw stars - the distinction is what stops the gate flipping on the rendering code. Teeth proven BOTH ways: deleting the sentence, and adding a function that touches the table.

search-term-survives-punctuation.label: T99: a comma in a search box must not 400 the read (2026-08-26). MEASURED against the live REST endpoint: or=(machine.ilike.*bearing, spherical*,...) returns HTTP 400, 'failed to parse logic tree'. PostgREST's or=(a,b) grammar splits on top-level commas, so an unquoted comma inside a value ends the condition early and the ENTIRE filter is rejected; parentheses do the same. ★THE TERM THAT BREAKS IT IS THE ORDINARY ONE: 'Bearing, spherical roller, 22320 E1 XL C3, SKF' is how a real part is named - it is this platform's OWN example in the longest-truncates gate - and typing it into the logbook feed, the logbook EXPORT, community, or the global search overlay produced a 400 the page renders as a FAILED READ. A legitimate search looked like an outage, which is worse than no results: the worker concludes the system is down and stops looking. ★TWO DIFFERENT JOBS, AND ONLY ONE WAS BEING DONE. Escaping % and _ stops a wildcard changing WHICH rows match; removing the delimiters stops the filter failing to parse at all. FOUR sites did the first and not the second. marketplace.html was the exception - it strips them - which is why the same phrase worked there and nowhere else, and why nobody had noticed. ★FIXED CENTRALLY with whSafeSearchTerm (delimiters removed, wildcards escaped, capped), applied at all four sites. Delimiters are REMOVED rather than escaped because PostgREST offers no escape for them inside an unquoted value, and a space keeps word boundaries so the phrase still matches. VERIFIED END TO END: the same read that returned 400 now returns 200 with an empty array - an honest no-match instead of an error. ★AND THE SAME BUG WAS IN THE EDGE FUNCTIONS, where it is WORSE because it is SILENT. agentic-rag-loop's logbook lane sanitises a natural-language QUESTION - where commas are not an edge case but the common case - and read the result as `const { data: logs } = await q`, DESTRUCTURING THE ERROR AWAY. supabase-js RETURNS {data:null,error} rather than throwing, so the rejected filter never reached the surrounding catch and `logs || []` turned a 400 into an ordinary empty result: the AI answered with less grounding and nothing anywhere said why. Its comment reads 'Escape LIKE wildcards in user input (per data-engineer skill)' - the author followed the skill exactly, and the skill covered wildcards but not delimiters. visual-defect-capture passed an asset TAG into an .or() with no escaping at all. Both fixed, and the error is now logged instead of discarded. The gate covers the edge functions too, including the `const { data } = await q` shape that makes the failure invisible. Teeth proven on four clauses: the helper weakened, a page interpolating a raw term, an edge fn dropping the delimiter strip, and an edge fn discarding the error again.

money-trust-confirmed.label: T67: money and trust writes confirm — T67's owner-cockpit oracle (2026-08-26). Most admin verbs are reversible; two are not. Verifying a service-credit top-up MINTS credits into a provider's wallet, and once spent this console cannot pull them back — the mirror action refuses a top-up somebody actually PAID for. Setting kyb_verified / cert_verified is the platform VOUCHING for a stranger to a buyer who is about to send them money; it is the same claim trust-claim-backed keeps honest at the render end, and this keeps it honest at the GRANT end. ★THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT A CHANGE OF MIND, IT IS THE WRONG ROW: both live in per-row button lists in a queue worked at speed, so a misclick does not undo the last action — it applies a real one to the wrong person. FOUND: founder-console carried six writes and ZERO whConfirm; svcTopupDecide minted credits on one click while toasting 'Credits minted to the provider's wallet', and the verify-kyb/verify-cert branch granted the badge asking nothing. platform-actions held the same three (an optimistic status lock stopped a DOUBLE press there, which cannot stop a wrong-ROW press). All six now name the consequence, and the trust ones name WHO. Verified live: the dialog carries the real text and cancelling sends ZERO writes. Teeth: 6 of 6 unconfirmed against pre-fix HEAD, 0 of 6 after. ★NARROW ON PURPOSE — it does not demand a confirm on every admin verb; approving a listing is reversible, and a dialog there is friction that trains people to click through. ★AND THE GATE'S OWN UNIT WAS WRONG FIRST: it took the NEAREST enclosing braces and called platform-actions unconfirmed with the confirm four lines above, just outside the `try` — guarding before the try is the CORRECT place, since a cancel there leaves the button untouched. It now accepts a confirm that precedes the write in ANY enclosing scope, up to the handler.

feedback-round-trip.label: T157: feedback-round-trip - T157: the feedback loop actually goes somewhere (2026-08-26). 'Email us with corrections' and a feedback button are TRUST CLAIMS. A widget that thanks somebody and stores nothing is the worst version of this: the person believes they were heard, nobody was told, and the silence reads as being ignored rather than as a bug. Measured from the public /about/ page ANONYMOUSLY - the hardest case, because an anon insert must pass RLS with no session behind it. It does: platform_feedback carries a `feedback anon submit` policy admitting inserts only as status 'new', not public, with no admin_note - so a stranger can report a problem and cannot forge a resolved one. Six assertions, and the REFUSAL half is the point. A loop that works when every field is filled is easy; the failure that costs trust is a submit that quietly does nothing. So: a complete submission lands as status 'new'; an incomplete one (no kind chosen) is refused BEFORE any network call, names what is missing in a VISIBLE element, and does not clear what was typed. *** TWO FALSE READINGS ON THE WAY, NEITHER BANKED. *** The first run clicked send without choosing a kind, got no row, and could have been written up as 'public feedback never reaches the table' - it reached nothing because the widget correctly refused and said so in an element the probe was not reading. The second reused the panel from that refusal, and WHFeedback.open(prefill) deliberately fills only EMPTY fields (it must never clobber typed text), so the row landed under the OLD subject and the probe again read zero. The product was right both times; the probe was reading the wrong element, then reusing dirty state.

last-unit-race-is-told.label: T11: a deduction that moved NOTHING must not read as success (2026-08-27). Two workers finish repairs on the same part; inventory_deduct locks the item FOR UPDATE so the race is serialised, and the loser's call runs against an empty shelf. ★WHAT THE LOSER GOT, MEASURED LIVE (real item set to 0 inside a rolled-back transaction): `v_qty := GREATEST(0, v_qty - p_qty)` CLAMPS instead of refusing, so asking for 1 with 0 on the shelf returned 0, wrote a ledger row with qty_change 0, changed nothing, and raised NO error. Every caller checked only `error`, so the worker was told 'Entry saved' while their entry claimed a part the shelf never gave up — the shelf and the system disagreeing silently, which is the one thing this trajectory exists to prevent. ★AND THE RETURN VALUE CANNOT TELL THEM APART: it is the new quantity, and 'took the last one' and 'there were none' both end at 0. The LEDGER row can, because it records what MOVED — so callers pass p_txn_id (the function always accepted one) and read that row back through whDeductMoved(); verified under RLS that a member can read their own hive's inventory_transactions row. ★THREE SITES, NOT ONE: logbook's SAVE path, logbook's EDIT path, and inventory's Use modal — and inventory additionally cached `addTransaction(..., -qty, ...)`, recording the amount ASKED, so the page's own transaction list claimed a movement the database never made; it now records what moved. The first version of this GATE had the same disease it was built to catch, grading only the first call it found with re.search while two others kept the defect. ★TEETH (--selftest): the pre-fix error-only shape goes RED, an id passed but never read back goes RED, id+readback+comparison passes, and every live site is asserted green. The DB half rolls back and re-reads the shelf to prove it.

alert-scope-is-told.label: T19: hiding a plant alert is a HIVE action and must say so (2026-08-27). alert_dismissals is keyed onConflict 'hive_id,alert_key' — ONE row per alert per hive — so every control that writes it changes what the WHOLE CREW sees: marking handled, snoozing, and marking seen alike. Nothing about the surface said that. The local state is `_seen`, the control is an aria-pressed toggle, the copy was two words: everything reads personal bookmark while the write is shared state. ★THE FAILURE IS WRITTEN IN dismissAlert's OWN COMMENT — 'a plant alert quietly blinded for the whole crew by someone who thought they were tidying their own view' — and that path was fixed when it was written while its SIBLING acknowledgeAlert was not: nothing about scope on the way in, and on the way out (un-marking DELETES the hive's row and returns the alert to unseen for everyone) nothing at all, so the crew could watch an alert reappear with no idea who or why. Both now name the scope and the actor, in EN and FIL. ★THE RULE: every user-facing message on a successful alert_dismissals write must name the scope, matched by MEANING across both languages rather than a fixed sentence — the copy ships bilingual via _t(en, fil), and a gate that pins wording punishes improving it. ★TEETH ARE THE PRE-FIX WORLD VERBATIM (--selftest, 5 cases): the old `_t('Marked seen', 'Minarkahang nakita')` is the 'two words with no scope' RED, and the old un-mark is the 'silent write' RED; a read-only query owes nothing and stays green. ★The gate's own window was wrong first and its selftest caught it: a fixed 900-char scan ended before both announcements (they sit past a writeAuditLog call and a long comment) and reported two correct paths as silent, so the search is now bounded by the `catch (` that actually ends the success path.

kicked-rejoin-is-explained.label: T7: the code still works, and the door is still shut (2026-08-27). A removed worker usually still HAS the invite code — read aloud at a briefing, sitting in a chat thread — so rejoining is not an edge case, it is the next thing that happens, and it has two halves that must agree. ★THE DOOR, asserted LIVE: join_hive_by_code refuses a kicked member twice over — by auth identity, and again by (hive, worker_name) so a second account cannot walk a ban back in. Both are driven, because 'the function has an IF' is not 'the function refuses', and the second branch only fires for an identity with no membership row at all, which is exactly the shape a reading of the source talks itself out of. ★AND THE SENTENCE: a refusal reaching a person as a raw code, or as 'could not join', says the app is broken rather than that a decision was made about them. hive.html must key on HIVE_MEMBER_KICKED and say WHAT (removed) and WHAT NOW (a way that is not retrying the code, since retrying is the one action that cannot work) — matched by MEANING, not a fixed sentence, because a fixed sentence is a gate that fails when someone improves the wording. Distinct from removal-tells-the-worker (T25), which covers the removed worker's ARRIVAL; this covers the door they knock on afterwards. ★SAFETY: the kicked state is created inside a transaction and ROLLED BACK, verified by re-reading the member's status. ★TEETH (--teeth): Postgres has transactional DDL, so the run replaces join_hive_by_code with a permissive version INSIDE the same transaction — both branches then report 'allowed' and the gate fails naming both, while the definition is re-read afterwards to prove the real function came back. A green teeth run would mean this gate cannot see an open door. ★The copy check itself was caught wrong by its own selftest first: a naive quote-to-quote regex paired the closing quote of one literal with the opening quote of the next and read the CODE between them, so a correct page looked silent.

report-clobber-guard.label: INSTRUMENT INTEGRITY: a spot-check must never destroy a full sweep's report (2026-08-27). MEASURED, not hypothesised — prove_retry_path.mjs wrote retry_path_report.json on EVERY run, whether it walked 22 pages or 1, and a single `--page <fixture>` probe replaced the whole sweep's verdicts with one UNGRADED row. ★WORSE THAN A LOST LOG: tools/bank_prover_reports.py READS these files to bank whole families and run_platform_checks registers several as a gate's `report`, so a truncated report does not announce itself — it just looks like a small run, and a narrowed probe can quietly feed one page of verdicts into a bank that believed it was getting twenty-two. ★AND IT WAS A KNOWN CLASS THAT NEVER TRAVELLED: prove_journey.mjs carries the fix in its own header ('a fixed filename let a one-page test DESTROY a 66-persona run'), written for ONE prover — 29 others had the identical shape and none had the guard. A lesson recorded in one file's comments is not a lesson the platform has learned; this gate is where it becomes one. THE RULE: if a prover accepts a narrowing flag (--page/--case/--journeys/--only/--lane/--family), the path it writes its report to must DEPEND on that flag; the guard's SHAPE is not prescribed (a ternary at the write site or a variable derived from the flag both satisfy it). All 29 were fixed in one pass — full runs still write exactly the same filename, so no baseline moved and no banked row was disturbed — and the retry sweep was re-run to repair the damage (22 pages, 21 PASS / 1 NO-RECOVER). Now 67 narrowing provers, 0 offenders. Teeth (--selftest, 5 cases): a fixed filename behind a narrowing flag goes RED; a ternary, a derived variable, a non-narrowing tool and a non-report write all stay green.

photo-survives-queue.label: T14's LAST PROBE (LIVE Playwright): the dead-zone entry a worker most wants to keep is the one with the PICTURE on it — the cracked bearing, the leak, the burnt contactor. logbook puts it in the row's `photo` column and offline the whole row goes to IndexedDB, so this asks whether the picture comes back intact after the phone was pocketed and the app closed. SCOPE STATED: it does not re-drive the save form (prove_offline_queued's logbook-entry case already covers form→queue, including that the save is a form SUBMIT and not a click on a zero-width button); what was never covered is photo FIDELITY across storage and a restart. The photo half IS driven for real — a genuine hand-built PNG goes to the page's own #f-photo input and the page's own pipeline (FileReader→Image→canvas→toDataURL plus its 700KB re-encode guard) produces the data URL, 36,783 chars from a 420x320 source. FOUR assertions: PRODUCED, QUEUED (zero server traffic), SURVIVES (byte-identical after a full document restart), STILL AN IMAGE (decodes back to a real bitmap). Writes NOTHING to the database — the row never leaves the queue, so no PM mirror, XP ledger or embedding is disturbed; the queue entry is removed and the removal verified. ★TEETH, and they are the interesting part: `--teeth` stores a photo of exactly the SAME LENGTH with ONE character changed. SURVIVES goes false while both lengths still read 36783 — the only way to show the comparison is byte-wise rather than the 'roughly the right size' check that lets a corrupted image pass. That run also shows STILL AN IMAGE staying TRUE for the corrupted photo, because a one-character JPEG corruption still decodes: either assertion ALONE would have passed it, and only the pair is honest. Retry-once.

queue-survives-restart.label: T14's THIRD HALF (LIVE Playwright + psql): the offline family proves a write is HELD, the drain gate proves it leaves EXACTLY ONCE — and both stay inside ONE page life. This puts a full document RESTART between the enqueue and the reconnect, which is what actually happens: the worker logs the job in a dead zone, pockets the phone, and the PWA is gone (OS-reclaimed or closed) before signal returns. ★NOT A VARIATION — A DIFFERENT SURFACE, and T14 already paid to learn why: the queue is created by a `_ensure<X>Queue()` accessor with auto-sync attached INSIDE it, so the drain only ever happens if a FRESH page life calls it, and pm-scheduler's measured defer race lost that queue on 2 of 5 loads silently. A queue whose rows persist but whose sync is never re-attached is WORSE than no queue: the work is neither sent nor lost but INVISIBLE, and the worker was told it was saved. FIVE assertions: HELD (zero server writes offline), PERSISTS (still in IndexedDB after the restart — read from the store DIRECTLY, never through the page object a restart destroys, which would be asking the wrong witness), REWIRED (the fresh life re-creates the queue and re-attaches sync), DRAINED, ONCE (one row after a further settle, store emptied). The restart document is fetched with the transport up ON PURPOSE: serviceWorkers are blocked so there is no cached shell, and a goto under setOffline dies at ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED — a failure of the SHELL, which is a real question but a different one (T44's). The window stays write-tight regardless (route still aborted, navigator.onLine still false via addInitScript) and the DB is re-checked to prove it. TEETH: `--teeth` suppresses whCreateQueue on the restarted document, reproducing the defer race's end state — REWIRED goes false and the row is left STRANDED in the store, while PERSISTS stays true, so the assertions are shown independent and the prover is shown to see its defect. Writes a MARKED row, deletes it, ABORTs on dirty state. Retry-once.

engineer-lens-covers-its-lane.label: T52: what the Engineer lens SELECTS — the TOOLS-registry content oracle (2026-08-27). The sibling gate asks whether the two switches called Engineer agree with each other; this one answers the question T52's own note left open, whether the nav-hub engineer filter selects the right tools. ★THE INVARIANT WITH TEETH: no tool may be tagged `engineer` WITHOUT also being tagged `supervisor`. That is not tidiness. There is no engineer ROLE here — hive_members.role is CHECK-constrained to worker | supervisor — so `roles: ['engineer']` alone puts a tool in NO role's default spine: reachable only by someone who had already gone into the hub and switched the lens by hand, and invisible to the supervisors who ARE the engineers on this platform. nav-hub.js says so at the line that added supervisor to Eng. Design — 'no separate engineer auth exists (the engineer persona IS supervisors in practice, T52); a supervisor needing a calc could not find Eng. Design here' — and the same reasoning applies to every future tool, with nothing holding it. This is the retired-page class (a live control reachable only through a door most people never open), caught at the registry rather than after someone loses a tool. ★AND THE LANE: T52 established the design-and-reliability set (Eng. Design, Analytics, Asset Hub, Project Manager, Project Report, PH Intelligence); each is asserted to keep its engineer TAG so a tool cannot quietly leave the lens while the lens still calls itself Engineer. Tagging, not visibility: isVisibleInMode also drops every hidden:true tool from EVERY mode, and two of the six are hidden Phase-B pages reached from a parent button, so a visibility check would fail them forever for a reason unrelated to engineers. The lane is a FLOOR, not a ceiling — extra engineer-visible tools are allowed, because whether Reports belongs is a judgement the registry records with a reason, not one a validator should overturn. Teeth (--selftest, 5 cases): an engineer-only tool and a lane member leaving the lens both go RED; a universal tool and an absent tool stay green.

journal-says-what-survives.label: T77/T164: the most private surface must say what you can take back (2026-08-27). A worker speaks or types something personal into the voice journal, and two facts govern whether they should - neither guessable. THE NOTE IS PERMANENT: ai-gateway persists the row inside the same call that generates the reply, so it exists before the worker has seen anything, and renderHistory's only per-entry action is 'Speak again' - no edit, no per-note delete. AND THERE IS SOMEWHERE TO GO: the privacy policy's Data Rights Request route, which validate_erasure_path_intact already proves the database honours. ★THE IN-APP ERASURE IS VOICE-ONLY AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ADVERTISED AS THE REMEDY - the gate FAILS if the page starts offering it. voice-handler's _isErasureRequest does detect 'delete my voice history', but it is reached from _onStopRecording alone, so only after a voice recording; this page's typed fallback exists, in its own words, for 'a loud plant floor, a denied mic, or a worker who cannot speak', and pointing those people at a spoken phrase offers a remedy that excludes precisely whoever most needs it. ★AND IT ASSERTS THE DISCLOSURE APPEARS ONCE, because the first attempt at this fix was DUPLICATION: the permanence was ALREADY stated on the primary surface, and a new paragraph restating it landed inside a collapsed <details> nobody opens - a second home for information that already had one. Reverted; the fix became a single clause completing the sentence that was already there. Teeth proven on the missing route and on the duplicate.

draft-survives-reauth.label: T38: typed work must outlive a session expiry (2026-08-27). A worker half-fills a logbook entry, the token dies, they sign in again - and whether their typing is still there depends on a three-link chain no single file makes visible, with every link in a different place: whAutoSaveDraft persists the text; session-timeout's clearIdentityHard wipes the IDENTITY keys and must not touch draft keys; and the draft is restored only to the worker who typed it, by an OWNER CHECK that reads wh_last_worker - the very key the expiry just deleted. ★SO THE DRAFT SURVIVES ONLY BECAUSE RE-AUTH PUTS THAT KEY BACK. Sign-in rewrites wh_last_worker, so by the time the worker returns the owner check matches again and the text reappears. Re-key that check to something sign-in does NOT restore and every draft on the platform is silently discarded after an expiry: the form comes back empty and nothing explains it. That is the assertion - the key the owner check reads must be one the sign-in path writes. ★THE OWNER CHECK IS NOT THE BUG, it is the shared-tablet protection: worker A's draft must not appear in worker B's form. Removing it would 'fix' the expiry case by leaking someone's typing to the next person on the device, which is worse. ★AND THE ASSERTION HAD TO BE 'AT LEAST ONE LINK', NOT 'EVERY LINK': the check is a fallback chain (wh_last_worker || wh_worker_name) and utils.js records that the alias reads are dead - 'never written anywhere in the codebase (get-without-set)'. Demanding every link be restored flagged that dead alias and called a working chain broken. Teeth proven on both clauses: sign-in ceasing to restore the key, and an expiry that starts wiping a draft key.

marketplace-warns-before-payment.label: T101: 100% of the money risk sits at one step (2026-08-27). This is a CONTACT-ONLY marketplace - no escrow, no held funds, no reversal - so a buyer contacts a stranger and pays them off-platform, and every peso of risk lives at that single moment. RA 11967, the PH Internet Transactions Act, requires consumer education on the red flags in internet transactions, which makes this a legal floor as well as a decent one. ★STATING A FACT IS NOT WARNING: 'payment is off-platform' is true and tells a buyer nothing about what to DO. The page carries an actual warning at the decision point - inspect the item, meet at the seller's business address or a public place, avoid paying in full up front to a new seller - and the sentence that sets expectations correctly: WorkHive never holds your payment, so we cannot reverse it. ★THE OPPOSITE FAILURE IS WORSE THAN SILENCE, so the gate also refuses escrow / buyer-protection / money-back / guaranteed-refund language on the marketplace surfaces: a buyer who believes there is protection behaves as though a loss is recoverable. It strips COMMENTS before matching, so prose ABOUT a promise is not read as the promise. ★AND IT HOLDS TWO SUBTLE CLAIMS THE PAGE ALREADY GOT RIGHT: 'credits back' must carry that credits are spend-only and cannot be withdrawn, because the bare words read like money returning; and the trust bar must say 'ID-Verified badge per seller' rather than 'ID-Verified Sellers', which as a bare heading reads as a property of the RESULTS - the same false claim the source chip carried when 3 of 9 listings actually had a verified seller. Teeth proven on the removed reversal sentence and on an introduced protection promise.

status-survives-the-outage.label: T71: the page that reports the outage must load during it (2026-08-27). whReadError sends a person to status.html when a read fails on good internet, because 'is it me or them?' is the one question a failure state can actually answer - and that pointer is only honest if the status page works when the platform does not. ★TWO WAYS A STATUS PAGE LIES, and both are asserted: (1) IT DEPENDS ON WHAT IT REPORTS - a page that needs the database cannot report a database outage; it fails exactly when someone finally needs it, and the reader concludes the whole product is gone. So status.html must carry no Supabase client, no getDb, no table read. (2) IT IS HARDCODED GREEN - 'All systems operational' baked into the markup is a trust signal with no living producer: it stays green THROUGH the outage and is worse than no page at all, because it actively contradicts what the person is experiencing. ★WHAT IT DOES INSTEAD IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, and the measurement confirms it: no database reference anywhere, and it pings each edge function's public /health endpoint, rendering one card per service, ambering when a round-trip exceeds the interactive SLO, with a Refresh to re-check. Live per service, independent of the database - which is precisely why it can still answer when the database is the thing that is down. ★IT ALSO HOLDS THE POINTER ITSELF: if utils.js stops sending a failed read to status.html, every failure state goes back to answering 'is it me or them?' with silence. Teeth proven on both lies - a Supabase client introduced, and a hardcoded green.

audit-is-reachable-from-a-record.label: T28: an audit nobody can reach is write-only (2026-08-27). 'Who changed this?' is asked while looking at the RECORD - an asset whose details are wrong, a reported post, a decision someone disputes. If the only way in is to know the page exists and open it cold, the trail is technically complete and practically useless: the supervisor gives up or goes to SQL, and the compliance story the platform tells about itself is one nobody can walk. ★A LINK THAT DROPS THE RECORD IS BARELY BETTER - arriving at an unfiltered log of every power action while holding the id in your head is the same scavenger hunt with extra steps. So BOTH ends are asserted: the links must carry the subject (asset-hub sends ?q=<tag>, community sends ?action=report_post) AND audit-log must CONSUME those parameters, or the context is written into the URL and thrown away - a promise only the sender believes, which is the declared-but-never-wired class. MEASURED: two context-carrying links, audit-log consumes all four of q/actor/action/target. ★THE HIVE MENU ENTRY DOES NOT SATISFY THIS: audit-log is a hidden page, so a menu item makes it reachable only to someone who already knows to look; the record-level affordances are what make it findable at the moment the question is actually asked, which is why bare links are reported but do not count toward the requirement. Teeth proven on both halves - links stripped of their record, and the audit page ceasing to read what it is sent.

removal-tells-the-worker.label: T25: being removed from a hive must not arrive as an empty screen (2026-08-27). A supervisor kicks someone; the supervisor's side is a confirm and a roster that shrinks. The WORKER's side is the one that matters - they open the app and their hive is simply gone, and without a word the honest readings available to them are 'the app broke' and 'my work was deleted', one of which is frightening enough to end their use of the product. ★THREE THINGS A REMOVED PERSON NEEDS, all asserted: WHAT HAPPENED (removed from the named hive, BY A SUPERVISOR - without an actor it reads as a malfunction), WHAT SURVIVED ('your personal records are still yours', which is the fear underneath, and silence about it is read as loss), and WHAT NOW (join another hive or create one - otherwise the notice tells someone their place is gone and leaves them there). ★AND IT MUST BE HELD LONG ENOUGH TO READ, which is the part usually missed and is asserted as part of the disclosure rather than as styling: the page's toast hides at a fixed 3s and this notice overrides it to 12s. Three seconds is fine for 'saved'; it is not enough for two sentences about your identity and your work, and a message nobody finishes reading was not delivered - the zero-millisecond-refusal lesson wearing a longer coat. Teeth proven on the hold (dropped to 2.5s) and on the records reassurance (removed).

md-twins-current.label: T3/T154: the markdown twin must say what the page says (2026-08-27). Every public page ships a clean twin at <page>.md - the llms.txt convention, served deliberately (_headers: 'Markdown twins ... every page also exists at <page>.md') so answer engines read structured text instead of scraping markup. That makes the twin a PUBLISHING CHANNEL, and a stale one is worse than none: an agent fetching it gets a confident, well-formed, WRONG version of the page. ★MEASURED 2026-08-27: 107 of 119 twins had DRIFTED, including privacy-policy and terms-of-service - an answer engine could quote retired legal text. The sharpest instance was T3's recorded defect surviving in the machine channel after being fixed in the human one: 60 calculator twins still said 'free, no sign-up needed' on a link INTO engineering-design.html, which redirects to sign-in, while the HTML had already been corrected to 'A free account takes about 30 seconds'. Zero served pages carried the claim; sixty twins did. ★THE VALIDATOR ALREADY EXISTED AND WORKED - tools/validate_md_twins.py, with a source_sha per twin and the right reasoning in its own docstring - and NOTHING RAN IT: it appeared in no gate registration, the same orphaned-prover shape as the three unreferenced provers found earlier this session. A working oracle nobody runs is indistinguishable from one never written. Fixed by rebuilding (118 rebuilt, 119/119 current, 0 twins still carrying the claim) and by REGISTERING the validator, so the next HTML edit that forgets the twin fails here instead of shipping a confident wrong answer to a machine.
