FIX ON FAIL: python tools/build_md_twins.py

safety-isolation-visible.label: T15: the READ path shows LOCK-OUT (2026-08-27). The whole point of searching fault history before opening a machine is to learn how it was worked on last time, and 'the last person locked this out / worked under a permit' is the most consequential thing on the card. logbook CAPTURED loto_applied and permit_reference on the form, STORED them on the row, and RESTORED them when an entry was EDITED — and never showed them to anyone READING. 419 of 3,811 entries carry that data, so this was 11% of the fault history withholding its safety-isolation fact from the person about to open the machine. ★THE ORACLE COMPARES COUNTS, not existence: the rendered badge count must equal what the database says is visible on that worker's most recent page, because a badge that renders on the WRONG rows is its own defect. Verified live at 20 cards / 3 badges / 3 expected, sample 'BF-001 MECHANICAL CLOSED LOTO PTW-2026-9385'. ★AND THE SUBJECT MUST HAVE SOMETHING TO SHOW: the first run used an account whose recent 20 entries contained no LOTO, read 0 badges, and 0 was CORRECT — a pass that proved nothing. The gate now FAILS rather than passes when the chosen account has nothing to display, because a check that cannot fail is not a check. Read-only.

report-window-parity.label: T23: the window on the CHIP must be the window in the EMAIL (2026-08-27). The four selectable reports cover wildly different periods — Shift Handover is the last EIGHT HOURS, Failure Digest the last 7 days, Predictive the last NINETY DAYS, PM Overdue a current-status snapshot — and the chooser showed a coloured dot and a label. A supervisor could send an 8-hour snapshot and a quarter of history to their boss in one email with nothing on screen distinguishing them, which is T23's own open question ('what is actually IN each of the 4 chips') answered as a defect. ★THE WINDOW WAS NEVER UNKNOWN: send-report-email's REPORT_META has carried it all along and prints it INSIDE the delivered email — it simply never reached the person CHOOSING. Now on every selectable chip, verified live: 'PM Overdue · current status as of this report', 'Shift Handover · last 8 hours', 'Predictive · last 90 days'. ★AND THAT PUTS A SECOND COPY OF A SERVER FACT IN THE CLIENT, the hazard this repo already names (two windows, one metric name) — two copies that can drift are worse than one copy nobody can see, unless something asserts they agree. This gate is that assertion: every offered id must exist in REPORT_META and every stated window must match the server string exactly; a phase3 chip may omit its window because it cannot be sent, so it promises nothing. ★ITS OWN SELF-TEST CAUGHT ITS OWN BUG: the first parser put an OPTIONAL window group behind a lazy prefix, and a lazy quantifier always prefers to skip the optional group — five logic cases passed while the live check reported four chips 'stating no window' that plainly stated one. Matching the row first and reading inside it fixed it. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. a drifted window, a selectable chip with none, and an id the server does not know. Static, read-only.

success-is-checked.label: T63: a page may not ANNOUNCE a write it never confirmed (2026-08-27). The mirror of unconfirmed-write-is-not-a-failure, and the worse half — telling someone their work failed when it landed costs a retry; telling them it SAVED when it did not is a lie they act on: they close the tab, walk away from the machine, stop chasing the payment. ★supabase-js DOES NOT THROW WHEN A WRITE IS REFUSED — it resolves with { error } — so `try { await db.from(t).delete()… } catch` is not protection: the catch only ever sees THROWN errors and an RLS refusal never throws. Same root as the bare-builder class seen from the other end (there the promise was never sent; here it was sent, refused, and the refusal discarded). ★IT FOUND ONE, IN THE WORST PLACE: integrations' rollbackBatch ran three writes — delete from external_sync, delete the imported rows from the target table, mark the audit entry rolled back — discarded all three results and said 'Import rolled back successfully.' A refusal on any step left every imported row in place while the person was told the import had been undone. On a REVERSAL that is the worst available lie: they stop looking and the bad data stays in the hive. Fixed, so this gate carries NO baseline — any hit is new. ★A ROWS-RETURNED CHECK COUNTS: pm-scheduler verifies with `if (upgraded && upgraded.length)` instead of reading `error`, which is equally valid; an earlier draft of the detector called that a defect, so the rule accepts either shape. Teeth (--selftest, 5 cases) incl. both valid check shapes and an error-toast that is not a success claim. Static, read-only.

unconfirmed-write-is-not-a-failure.label: T176: an empty RETURNING is an UNCONFIRMED write, not a failed one (2026-08-27). supabase-js resolves `.insert(...).select(...)` with { data: [], error: null } when the INSERT SUCCEEDED and the RETURNING read was refused — RLS gates SELECT separately from INSERT. So `if (!data || !data.length)` has learned exactly one thing: the write is unconfirmed. It has NOT learned that it failed. Eighteen sites branch this way; eight told the user their work was lost, and two were actively dangerous because the advice was 'try again': re-hailing broadcasts a SECOND job to every nearby provider for work the client wants done once, and re-registering creates a second provider profile for the same hive. ★EACH OF THOSE WAS TWO SITES, NOT ONE — the hail has a catalog path and a custom-scope path, registration has a hive path and a freelancer path — and the sweep's dedup-by-message had hidden the twins; the editor refusing an ambiguous match is what exposed them. All four now say what is actually known ('may have been sent — we could not confirm it') and point at the LIST rather than back at the button. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY SPOKE CORRECTLY in four other places ('the job may have moved on', 'that top-up was already decided', 'changed since you opened it, reloading'), which makes the eight a drift rather than a gap. ★THE BASELINE IS FULLY TRIAGED AGAINST THE SCHEMA, never waved through: every survivor is an idempotent UPDATE, an UPSERT with onConflict, or an INSERT the database makes un-duplicatable (service_vouchers_code_key UNIQUE on code; marketplace_reviews_one_per_request_direction UNIQUE). Where a retry cannot cost anything, 'try again' is honest advice even if 'didn't save' is imprecise — a wording item, not a hazard. A baseline holding UNTRIAGED entries would launder unknowns as accepted, the failure na-premise-holds exists to prevent. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases). Static, read-only.

noun-slot-takes-a-noun.label: T176: whReadError's second argument is SPLICED MID-SENTENCE (2026-08-27). The helper does not print `what` — it composes 'Your session expired, so ' + thing + ' could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it.' — so it must receive a NOUN PHRASE ('your equipment list', 'the audit log'). Four callsites passed a whole SENTENCE, and what shipped was: "Your session expired, so Could not load your equipment list. Check your connection. could not be loaded. Sign in again to see it. Nothing you did was lost." MEASURED in the browser, not reasoned — the same call with a noun returns the sentence it should. ★THE MISTAKE HAD A GOOD MOTIVE, which is why it needs a gate and not a scolding: each site was CONVERTED from a hand-rolled message to the taxonomy helper — exactly the right move — and the old sentence was forwarded into the argument slot. logbook even carries a comment above it explaining that the upstream sentence belongs in console.error and never in the notice; the author understood the principle and still handed the helper a sentence. Converting to the taxonomy means REPLACING the sentence with a noun, not passing it through. ★AND IT IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY OTHER CHECK: the helper is present, so an adoption sweep passes it; the string holds no raw error text, so the raw-echo ratchet passes it; nothing throws. Only reading the composed sentence shows it — and that sentence only appears when a session dies mid-read, which is precisely when nobody is watching. whWriteError and whAiError are OUT OF SCOPE by design: their second argument IS a fallback message. Teeth (--selftest, 7 cases) incl. both out-of-scope helpers and a verb-opener with no period. Static, read-only.

no-write-only-tables.label: T105: a table the UI writes should have a READER (2026-08-27). The table-level twin of captured-columns-reach-a-reader — that one asks which COLUMNS never reach a person, this asks which whole TABLES the UI fills and never opens again. ★IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST RUN: marketplace-seller writes push_subscriptions when a provider enables job alerts and never reads one back, and the push card renders only while `Notification.permission !== 'granted'` — so the moment permission is granted the card vanishes forever and NOTHING ever confirms a subscription row exists. Browser permission and a live subscription are different facts: the endpoint rotates, the service worker is replaced, an upsert fails, a row is cleared, and permission stays 'granted' through every one of them — leaving the provider shown nothing while believing the page's own promise that they will 'hear new hails with this tab closed'. Measured at 0 rows. The table having no reader is precisely what let the page never check; the fix gave the card a third state ('granted but not actually subscribed', with a one-tap repair) and thereby gave the table its reader. ★READS THROUGH VIEWS COUNT, and that is the whole difficulty: naively 14 of 54 written tables looked write-only, including community_posts, hives and service_requests — all read constantly, through TRUTH VIEWS (community reads v_community_posts_truth). Resolving view→base-table from information_schema took 14 down to 2, and both survivors were real. A sweep that cannot see through a view manufactures a dozen false findings. ★A FAILED READ MUST NOT ACCUSE: the page's lookup returns null for UNKNOWN and only an explicit false warns, so a refused read can never tell a correctly-subscribed provider their alerts are off. Ratchet: the one survivor (early_access_emails — service_role-only RLS, an Ian decision on T67) is baselined with its reason. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. the view-resolution case in both directions. Needs the local DB for the view map; SKIPs rather than guesses when it is down.

captured-columns-reach-a-reader.label: T15: a column written for a PERSON must reach one (2026-08-27). logbook captured loto_applied, permit_reference, readings_json and failure_consequence on its form, stored them on the row, restored them into the EDIT FORM when an entry was edited, and rendered them to a reader NOWHERE — 1,767 of 3,811 entries carried equipment readings nobody could see. ★THE PHANTOM-COLUMN AUDITOR CANNOT CATCH THIS: it asks whether a column has a READ CONSUMER, and a `.select('loto_applied')` satisfies it. SELECTED IS NOT RENDERED — that gap is the whole finding. Asked platform-wide over 121 written columns it returned 9, and project_roles.assigned_by was a real one: 36 of 36 rows record who assigned a project role and the pill showed the name alone, so 'who put me on this?' had no answer in the app (fixed; the sweep now confirms it dropped off the list). A RATCHET, not a cliff — the survivors are baselined WITH their verdicts, because the triage is the valuable part. THREE are FIXED and deliberately absent from the baseline so a regression fails this gate: assigned_by, variance_reason (the provider's finished-job card now reports the amount, method, reference and the payer's reason) and provider_type (the quote card now says 'Hive team' or 'Freelancer' where a buyer chooses). Of the rest: 3 are NOT defects (timestamps whose fact the rendered status already carries; a total the page shows as its two parts), 2 are unused rather than withheld (MEASURED at 0 rows — live_location has never been populated, so no client is being denied it), and 1 is a raw auth uid whose display would trade this defect for the no-raw-internals one. ★SCOPE IS PLATFORM-WIDE ON PURPOSE: per-page it reported ~30 false candidates, because pages WRITE audit rows (actor/target_id/target_name/target_type) and the AUDIT-LOG page renders them. ★AND WRITERS ≠ RENDERERS: shared scripts count as renderers so a column shown by utils.js is not 'invisible', but treating them as writers too pulled in ten AI-telemetry columns (response_time_ms, model_confidence…) written for a machine, not a person. Credential columns (key_hash, p256dh, auth uids) are excluded outright — not rendering those is the security property. Teeth (--selftest, 6 cases) incl. cross-page rendering, form-restore-is-not-rendering, and secrets. Static, read-only.

na-premise-holds.label: T29: an exclusion's stated REASON must still be true (2026-08-27). Every declared_na removes a cell from the denominator, so a false one reads exactly like coverage. The banks carry 105 of them, each states a reason — which means most are CHECKABLE, and nothing was checking them. The prompt was the handoff N/A found the same day: a reasoned-looking exclusion whose premise was false, carried for weeks in the roadmap as product work. THE RULE, matching evidence to the CLAIM: 'no page writes / zero writes / pure render surface' means the page must not call .insert/.update/.upsert/.delete nor an .rpc() whose NAME carries a mutating verb; 'renders no peso/credit figure' means it must render no ledger-style money — a currency amount inside PROSE does not count, which is why index's anon landing citing 'replacing it costs ₱800K to ₱2.4M' as an industry statistic is correctly excluded. ★THE ORACLE MUST MATCH THE CLAIM, and this gate's own drafts prove why it is worth saying: the first version judged 'renders no peso figure' by whether the page WRITES (flagging alert-hub and analytics, since writing has nothing to do with rendering money) and treated any unfamiliar .rpc() name as a write (flagging achievements' plainly read-only my_service_provider_ids); the second added toFixed(2) as a money signal and fired on an animation duration, a risk score and a statistical range — two more false findings against earned exclusions. The signal has to be the CURRENCY, never the precision. Corrected: 28 premises checked, 0 contradicted. ★AND IT REPORTS WHAT IT COULD NOT CHECK (77 not mechanically checkable) — a gate that silently ignored the reasons it does not understand would claim the whole exclusion set is sound while reading a quarter of it, which is the shrunk-denominator move one level up. Teeth (--selftest, 8 cases) incl. both cross-wirings above. Static, read-only.

asset-reaches-its-history.label: T15: the machine reaches its own FAULT HISTORY (2026-08-27). T15's done-definition is a JOURNEY, not a field — 'machine → its history → a usable prior fix, under a minute' — and asset-hub failed it in the most pointed way available: it COUNTED the asset's logbook entries in a stat card and offered no way to open them. A number with no door, on the page a worker is standing in front of the machine with. ★TWO WAYS THE FIX COULD LOOK RIGHT AND BE USELESS, both asserted: (1) logbook.machine stores the TAG ('M-001'), not the asset NAME ('Siemens Simotics SD 200L') — the sibling chips on that page use tag-with-name-fallback, and copying that shape would land a NAME search on ZERO results for a machine with 47 entries, an empty page indistinguishable from an empty history; so the gate requires ROWS on arrival counted against the database, never merely a link that navigates. (2) Fault history is the TEAM's history — without ?view=team the reader sees only their own entries and reads a colleague's fix as ABSENT. Verified live: M-001, 47 entries in the table, one tap, tag survives the hop into the search box, team window on, 30 cards plus the page's own Load More. Read-only.

captured-fields-are-readable.label: T15: the READ path shows what the WRITE path captured (2026-08-27). Having found ONE captured-but-never-read column (loto_applied), this asked the general question — of the 15 columns logbook writes, which does a reader never see? FOUR sat in the identical shape: selected by the loader, mapped onto the entry, restored into the EDIT FORM when an entry is edited, and rendered to a reader NOWHERE. Two are T15's own scenario — someone searching fault history before opening a machine: readings_json on 1,767 of 3,811 rows (nearly HALF the logbook — what the last person measured, the exact thing you compare today's reading against) and failure_consequence on 1,075 rows, whose four values include 'Safety risk'. ★AND THE LOTO FIX WAS HALF A FIX, WHICH IS WHY THIS GATE CHECKS BOTH READ SURFACES: the badge went on the entry CARD only, so the safety flag DISAPPEARED on drill-down — the detail modal being precisely where a person reads carefully before working on a machine. The cause was structural: lotoBadge was declared `const` INSIDE renderEntries, so the modal could not have called it; it is now a shared top-level helper both surfaces use. ★THE ORACLE IS THE DATABASE PER SURFACE: the card list's consequence-badge COUNT must equal the rows on the visible page carrying one (verified live 20 cards / 3 badges / 3 expected), and a modal opened on an entry the DB says has readings must render them WITH UNITS — a bare '97' is the naked-number defect. Counts, not presence, because the first LOTO run read 0-and-was-correct and proved a presence check can pass while blind. Teeth: RED on all four assertions against the pre-fix page. Read-only.

failed-read-is-not-empty.label: A read that FAILED must not render as 'there is nothing' (2026-08-27). The shape: a loader catches, blanks its list, toasts, re-renders. The toast FADES; the empty state is what stays — so an unread table ends as 'No pending listings' or 'be the first to sell', factual CLAIMS about the world made at the exact moment the platform could not read it. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY KNEW, TWICE: marketplace.html carries the diagnosis in its own source from a deepwalk ('the toast alone was insufficient — it fades, leaving the GRID showing the first-run CTA on a full marketplace') and sets _loadError; marketplace-seller-profile carries its own ('Only a read that ANSWERED may license a conclusion about this seller') and sets _reviewsFailed. Both fixed. marketplace-admin — the MODERATION queue, where 'nothing to review' is the sentence most likely to make someone stop looking — never got the fix, and neither did dayplanner's plant-PM rail, which on a failed read returned '' and simply VANISHED (a worker cannot tell an absent section from a quiet day). Second fix-that-did-not-travel this session; a lesson in one file's source protects that file, a gate makes it the platform's. ★THE RULE: a catch that blanks a list on a page owning an empty state must record that the read failed. The flag's NAME is not prescribed — three pages spell it three ways (_loadError, _reviewsFailed, _readFailed.listings) and all three are correct. ★SCOPED TO LOADERS: the catch must wrap a query, because not every `catch { x = [] }` is a load failure — alert-hub falls back to [] when a legacy double-encoded parts field will not parse, which is correct, and the first version of this gate called it a defect. Teeth: 5 selftest cases incl. bare and property-style flags.

taxonomy-speaks-filipino.label: T45: the shared FAILURE VOICE speaks Filipino (2026-08-27). Every page is bilingual through _t(en, fil) and the error taxonomy they all delegate to was NOT, so a worker running the FIL toggle got Filipino chrome and an ENGLISH sentence at the exact moment something failed and precision mattered most. Seventeen branches across whAiError, whReadError, whWriteError and whVoiceError now return through _t. ★DRIVEN IN THE PAGE, twice per branch, once under each WH_LANG — because a source grep for `_t(` only proves the CALL was written, not that the returned string changes. ★AND TWO BRANCHES MUST NOT TRANSLATE, asserted as SAME rather than skipped: the caller-supplied fallback (the PAGE's own English sentence to own) and whWriteError's deliberate-guard passthrough, which carries a policy refusal that took the trouble to explain itself ('Listing needs PHP50 credits held and you have 0 available') — rewriting someone else's explanation in another language is replacement, not translation. A gate that only checked 'everything differs' would call both of those defects. 14 branches: 12 must differ, 2 must not. ★The FIL copy is article-aware: callers pass the noun with its English article ('the activity log') because the EN sentences need it, and Filipino carries its own — the first draft read 'ang THE activity log' until the output was read rather than the diff. Register matched to lines already shipping ('Hindi ma-load ang activity log. Suriin ang koneksyon at subukan muli.'). Read-only.

alert-loop-closes.label: T29: acting on an alert must make the ALERT GO AWAY (2026-08-27). An alert inbox that never empties is an inbox people stop reading, so the chain has to close: the alert names an action, links to where that action is taken, and DOING it removes the alert — with nobody marking anything by hand. ★THE CLOSURE IS STRUCTURAL, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST KIND: alert-hub's PM alerts are DERIVED, not stored — they come from v_pm_scope_items_truth filtered is_overdue=true, so there is no status to update and no second write to forget. Complete the PM and the row simply stops matching. PROVEN LIVE rather than reasoned: inserting a 'done' completion for an overdue scope item inside a transaction takes its overdue count 1 → 0 and moves days_until_due −34 → +7, then rolls back with zero residue. ★TWO ASSERTIONS, because either alone is a half-truth — THE LINK EXISTS (an href to pm-scheduler for the NAMED asset plus an action label; an alert that states a problem and offers no way to it is a notification, not an inbox item) and THE CONDITION CLEARS (a link to a surface that does not actually resolve the alert leaves the loop open while looking closed). ★The gate's own link check was wrong first: a lazy any-character match ending at the first closing brace stopped INSIDE the first nested brace — inside a template expression, well before href and actionLabel — and reported a correctly-linked alert as offering no way to act. Read as a plain forward window now, because that is what the block is.

audit-entry-readable.label:
T28: an audit entry must read as a CHANGE, not as JSON (2026-08-27). audit-log's own meta description promises 'every CRUD + approval + permission change with actor, BEFORE/AFTER, and timestamp' — and the data can deliver it: hive_audit_log rows carry changed_fields: {"sw": {"from": 768, "to": 1920}}, literally a before and an after. The page rendered the whole payload as 
JSON.stringify(detail, null, 2)
, so a supervisor reconstructing a disputed change read a JSON blob to find the two values that mattered. The claim was already on the page; the delivery was not. Now each entry is a labelled row and a from/to pair reads '768 → 1920'. ★ASSERTED ON THE RENDERED DOM, not the source, because the question is what a PERSON sees: expand a real entry and check the block carries no braces and no quoted keys. ★AND IT MUST RUN AS A SUPERVISOR — audit-log is supervisor-gated and a worker sees ZERO entries, which the first run of the probe reported as '0 entries with details': a verdict about the ACCOUNT, not the page. An empty feed is now a failure to measure, never a pass. Teeth: the oracle's regex flags the pre-fix JSON string (True) and leaves the current render alone (False), so it demonstrably separates the two worlds. Read-only; writes nothing.

held-credits-are-told.label: T94: a wallet must not offer credits that are already spoken for (2026-08-27). Listing HOLDS credits — guard_listing_requires_reservation writes a credit_reservations row, sweep_listing_holding_fee eats into it monthly, release_reservation_on_delist gives it back — and the seller page SAYS so at listing time ('holds ₱50 in credits'). Held credits are not spendable. ★THE PLATFORM ALREADY COMPUTED THE SPLIT: seller_credit_balance(worker_name) returns available / reserved / total, where available is the ledger balance MINUS everything held. The wallet card called provider_credit_balance() instead — the ledger sum alone — and labelled it the balance, so a seller with live listings saw a number larger than they could spend, on the same page that had just told them listing would hold some of it. Not a missing feature: the glass was reading the wrong one of three numbers that were already sitting there, the 'built but never called' shape with money in it. ★THE HEADLINE FIGURE IS DELIBERATELY NOT SWAPPED: provider_credit_balance distinguishes a person-owned provider (shows the PERSON's balance) from a hive-owned one (shows the HIVE's), and its own comment records why — 'two cards for one human showing different numbers is how this defect stayed invisible'. seller_credit_balance is person-keyed, so replacing the call wholesale would silently change WHICH ACCOUNT a hive-owned card reports: fixing one money defect by introducing another. The total stays; the HELD figure is added beside it, and renders only when something is actually held (a 'reserved ₱0' on every wallet teaches people to stop reading the card). ★MEASURED LIVE: credit_reservations is empty on this stack, so the gate CREATES a 50-credit hold inside a transaction and rolls it back — available=-50, reserved=50, total=0, split exact, 0 rows left. The probe row references a real listing because the table enforces num_nonnulls(listing_id, request_id)=1. Teeth (--selftest): a single-balance wallet goes RED, fetching the split but not showing it still goes RED, fetching AND naming it passes.

source-chip-names-a-real-relation.label: CF: a provenance chip must name a relation that EXISTS (2026-08-27). MEASURED: hive.html's readiness chip named `v_maturity_truth` and there is no such relation - its own comment states the promise it was breaking, 'every readiness number on the page is reproducible by querying this view', so a supervisor who followed the chip to run that ad-hoc query got `relation "v_maturity_truth" does not exist`. The numbers were correct; the TRACE dead-ended, which is the only thing a provenance chip is for. The real view is v_hive_readiness_truth (verified to carry composite_score, current_stair and the five dimension columns the card renders). A second chip cited 'at_risk' as a source when it is a TIER LABEL, not a relation. ★WHY prove_source_chip.mjs COULD NOT SEE EITHER: it asks the sharper question - does the chip name a relation the page actually REQUESTED? - from captured PostgREST traffic; but hive.html renders readiness through the compute_hive_readiness RPC, so the chip carries a `source-chip-allow` marker. That exemption is legitimate for the network check and was never meant to exempt the chip from being TRUE, yet nothing else tested the name, so it was checked by nothing at all. An exemption must waive the check it was written for, never the question of whether the claim holds. Scope is deliberately narrow so it cannot cry wolf: chip sources are free prose, so only identifier-shaped tokens are tested, and tables, views, functions AND column names all count as real (the first cut flagged 'qty_on_hand'/'min_qty'/'at_risk'/'get_hive_dashboard' - columns and an RPC - which would have trained readers to ignore it).

control-within-viewport.label: CF: a tappable control must not sit past the floor viewport's edge (T113, 2026-08-27). MEASURED: '← Back to Basic Worker' ran +45px past a 390 viewport on inventory and +35px on logbook, its parent computing overflow:visible — part of a real control simply off-screen on the smallest phone the platform supports. ★WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the page never SCROLLS horizontally. The navbar is a fixed-height flex row and the document's scrollWidth never grows, so every check asking 'does this page scroll sideways at 390?' — the usual Z2 / WCAG 1.4.10 shape — reads perfectly clean while a button hangs over the edge. Scroll is a SYMPTOM of overflow, not a definition of it, and that gap is what this gate closes. ★AND THE ROOT IS RARELY THE OVERFLOWING ELEMENT: shortening the button changed nothing (it was still at 438 in a 390 box at 101px wide). The row was over-full because a SIBLING would not shrink — a flex item defaults to min-width:auto and refuses to go below its content width — so min-w-0 on the group plus truncate on its long label fixed both pages with the full label intact. The oracle ignores fixed/absolute decoration and anything inside a scrolling or clipping ancestor, so it reports only what a thumb actually cannot reach. Resurrection-proved: removing min-w-0 turns it RED (exit 1, naming the control at +228px), restoring it GREEN. ★THE FLOOR IS 320, NOT 390 (corrected 2026-08-27): the first cut of this gate guarded 390 and called it the floor, but the platform's declared floor is 320 (T113 / WCAG 1.4.10) — 390 is merely the common phone. A gate on the wider box cannot see what only breaks in the narrower one, and moving it found TWO more offenders the same day: community's post action row gives a supervisor viewing their OWN post FIVE icon buttons instead of four, and the fifth — Delete, which also carries a deliberate 22px Z3 gap so a destructive control is never adjacent to a routine one — ran 15px off-screen, so the delete control was unreachable on exactly the posts its owner is most likely to manage; and analytics' 'Stage 3' badge sat 10px past, because .hdr-right is deliberately flex-shrink:0 (its EN/FIL buttons owe 44px on both axes) so the row had nowhere to give. Both fixed by wrapping, which preserves the Z3 separation and the 44px minimums instead of trading them away. --width narrows the run and writes its own report; 320 and 390 both green.

dialogs-fit-the-floor.label: CF: every dialog in the bank must fit the floor viewport, controls included (T113, 2026-08-27). ★ITS DENOMINATOR IS THE PLATFORM'S, NOT MINE: flow-fits-the-floor walks four flows I chose by hand, and a gate whose subject list I wrote can only find what I thought to look at. This one consumes tools/dialog_targets.mjs - already the ONE source of truth for how each V2/V3 dialog opens, every entry's path READ FROM SOURCE with its `ref` line - so any dialog added there is covered here for free. 42 subjects, 33 measured, 0 unreachable controls at 320x844. ★MEASURE THE SHEET, NOT THE SCRIM: marketplace's openSheet(name) opens BOTH `#overlay-<name>` and `#sheet-<name>` - the overlay is the backdrop and the SHEET carries the content - so measuring the overlay found it permanently empty even after a real listing click, and the gate was one step from filing 'tapping a listing opens a blank full-screen sheet' against a marketplace that is fine. Seven commerce dialogs went from unmeasurable to measured (21, 6, 6, 5, 4 and 14 controls), taking coverage 26 -> 33. Reaching them also took two corrections the gate reported honestly rather than passing over: listing cards bind by addEventListener on .listing-card[data-id], not an inline onclick, and openDetailSheet lives in the page's closure so page.evaluate cannot call it - the fix is to CLICK the card, which is the real user action anyway. The content opener lives in THIS file rather than dialog_targets.mjs on purpose: that registry is shared with the modal-exit and dialog-layout provers, and changing an opener under them is the one-shared-fix-expires-unrelated-claims shape. ★AND THE SUBJECT TEST IS THE WHOLE GATE: the registry holds fixed overlays AND in-flow panels/tabs/lists, and bottom-checking the in-flow ones flagged SIX 'unreachable' controls (asset-hub's FMEA panel, its Weibull panel, engineering-design's history tab, analytics' summary, alert-hub's AMC card, voice-journal's history list) that a reader reaches by simply scrolling the page. Every one would have been a false finding banked against a page that is fine. The property is UNREACHABILITY, not off-screen-ness: the bottom axis applies only where the surface is fixed AND neither it nor an ancestor scrolls, because a dialog is centred and does not scroll, so a control past its fold is a button that cannot be pressed - whereas page-flow content past the fold is what scrolling is for. ★A SURFACE WITH NO CONTROLS IS UNMEASURED, NOT PASSED: twelve of the first run's 'ok' rows held zero controls and proved nothing, so they are now reported as skipped rather than padding the denominator. Preconditions that fail are UNGRADED, per the registry's own rule. Opens and measures; never submits. Proactive guard, teeth are synthetic negatives 6/6, including the two that matter most - a FIXED sheet IS bottom-checked and an IN-FLOW surface is NOT.

printed-truncation-is-disclosed.label: CF: a printed artifact that shortens free text must SAY so (T49, 2026-08-27). export-reads-its-own-set holds the ROW axis - a CSV must not inherit the render buffer's cap, so no row goes missing. This holds the CELL axis on the same kind of artifact. MEASURED: project-report.html rendered every daily-progress log through `.slice(0, 200)` with nothing appended, and that page exists to be PRINTED and handed to a stakeholder. On paper there is no hover, no expand, no scroll - a 350-character blocker arrived as a complete-looking 200-character sentence, usually cut mid-word, and the reader had no way to know anything had been removed. Blockers is the field that carries WHY a project is late. ★THE RULE IS NOT 'NEVER TRUNCATE' - a printed column is real and text has to fit - IT IS 'TRUNCATE OUT LOUD': the cap stays, and a conditional marker plus a one-line table note now disclose it, appearing ONLY when the cap actually bites so a complete report carries no false alarm. Verified live on WO-2026-001: 6/6 rows render, zero marks and no note (no fixture value exceeds 200), while clip() on a synthetic 500-char value keeps exactly 200 and marks it, and a 50-char value passes through untouched. ★AND THE MARKER MUST REACH PAPER: a disclosure hidden by @media print discloses nothing to the person holding the printout, so that is asserted too. Proactive guard, teeth are synthetic negatives, 5/5: bare prose slice, unconditional helper, marker hidden in print, helper with no marker, and the real surface clean. One of those negatives initially replaced a string that did not exist in the source, so it tested the UNCHANGED file and passed vacuously - fixed to strip every marker token including the title attribute.

flow-fits-the-floor.label: CF: a flow's OPENED state must fit the floor viewport, not just the page at rest (T113, 2026-08-27). ★THE GAP: control-within-viewport walks 16 pages AT REST, but the controls that decide whether work gets RECORDED do not exist at rest - the PM completion sheet, the deferral control, the add-task sheet are built or revealed mid-flow, and each is a different layout from the page hosting it. The resting sweep can be green over every page while the Save button of the sheet a worker must press sits off the edge: the same class T113 already found twice, one interaction deeper than any resting check can reach. Walks T10 (complete a PM, and its honest alternative - record a DEFERRAL) and T13 (the clock-in handover read) at 320. ★IT ARRIVES THE WAY A WORKER DOES: alert-hub hands pm-scheduler an ?asset=, the detail opens, and a REAL scope item's mark-done control is clicked. An earlier cut called openSheet() by hand and measured an EMPTY sheet - the same seven controls whatever the task, because markDone() is what fills in the item text, asset name, frequency badge and findings fields. That would have proved the sheet's chrome fits, not the sheet. ★AND A FLOW THAT NEVER OPENED IS REPORTED AS UNREACHED, NEVER AS CLEAN: the first run passed page.evaluate three arguments where it takes one, and every flow errored - counted as an instrument failure, which is why the run did not read as three tidy surfaces. Read-only: it opens and closes, never saves. ★AND FOR AN OVERLAY THE EDGE THAT MATTERS IS THE BOTTOM (T17 added 2026-08-27): the level-up card is a CENTRED FIXED overlay, so a card taller than a 320x844 phone puts its only dismiss button below the fold, and because the overlay does not scroll there is no gesture that reaches it - the reward moment becomes a trap. Driven through showLevelUpModal() with a REAL achievement id so the card carries its badge, heading and tier line, since an empty overlay is a different height. The bottom axis is checked only where a flow asks for it, because an ordinary PAGE is meant to extend past the fold - that is what scrolling is for - and flagging that everywhere would drown the finding. PROACTIVE guard (the property holds today), so its teeth are synthetic negatives, one per independent failure mode, all six verified: an off-screen control, a required control that is absent, a surface that does not exist, the real sheet clean at the floor, an off-BOTTOM control caught when the flow asks, and the bottom NOT checked when it does not - that last one proves the flag actually gates the check rather than being ignored. A width negative alone is NOT sufficient - at --width 200 the handover went RED while both PM sheets still passed.

flow-speaks-filipino.label: CF: a flow's MESSAGES must speak the language the page is set to (T45, 2026-08-27). MEASURED: with wh_lang=fil, all three core field flows refused in English - logbook 'Please select an asset before saving.', pm-scheduler 'Please enter a task description.', voice-journal 'Write a note first, then send it.' ★WHY 100% FIL COVERAGE MISSED IT: the platform has TWO translation mechanisms and they cover different halves of the screen. data-i + whI18nApply swap STATIC markup at load - 442/442 here, which is where 'FIL is 100%' comes from - but every message the FLOW produces is born AFTER that pass, from showToast(...), which takes a raw string. The only translator that reaches those is _t(en, fil) at the call site. So the resting page was fully Filipino and the WORKING page was not, and no load-time DOM sweep can ever see it, because at load the message does not yet exist. ★THE EN CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT A MEASUREMENT: each step runs twice, fil and en, and only an identical multi-word message counts as untranslated - separating 'never translated' from 'same word in both languages'. ★AND AN EMPTY READING IS THE INSTRUMENT, NEVER A PASS: three earlier cuts of this prover scored a resting toast placeholder ('Entry saved.' is markup, not a message), a click that threw 'not visible', and a closed <details> whose hidden children still report layout rects - so the gate now refuses to grade any step it did not demonstrably reach. The steps are REFUSALS on empty required fields, so the walk writes no rows and needs no cleanup, and a refusal is the message a worker can least afford to not understand. Fixed by wrapping 14 call sites across the three flows, incl. a second inline refusal path for the same string. Resurrection-proved: the pre-fix logbook turns it RED (exit 1), the fix GREEN.

bounded-list-offers-the-rest.label: CF: a capped list must admit the rest exists (T129, 2026-08-27). A long list has to be capped - the DOM cannot carry two thousand rows and stay usable - so the danger is never the cap itself, it is a SILENT one: rows 1-20 of 548 rendered with nothing on screen admitting the other 528. That reads as 'this is everything', and a supervisor planning against it plans against a fifth of their own history. MEASURED at two volumes, which is what this holds in place: with the hive at 941 rows (314 for the signed-in worker) and again at 1641 (548), rows painted stayed 20 -> 20, DOM nodes 1458 -> 1396, first rows 1125ms -> 1221ms. A 75% growth in the reader's own history cost 96ms and NO dom weight, because the slice is constant - and the load-more wrap was offered rather than hidden, so the remainder was disclosed both times. THE PROPERTY IS THREE-PART because any one alone is not enough: the render must SLICE by a display count (or the page grows with the data), something must INCREASE that count (or the cap is a wall, not a page), and the control must be revealed exactly when more rows exist - toggle('hidden', count >= total). That third part is what makes the cap honest; without it a list can slice, own a hidden button, and still tell the reader nothing. Covers logbook and inventory, the two surfaces long enough to need it; teeth are a synthetic negative per part.

journey-na-is-earned.label: CF: a journey cell may only be N/A for a reason the walk actually observed (2026-08-27). An N/A is the cheapest verdict on the board - it removes a cell from the denominator without anyone having to see a failure - so it is the one that must be earned. MEASURED against journey_report.json, this found two ways it was not: (1) a handoff declared 'not measured' while several of its own candidates WERE in the roster - the chooser returned a single best candidate and discarded the rest, so a walkable hand-off was excluded because the FIRST pick happened to be off-roster (hive named 5 such, skillmatrix 2, community 1); (2) an abandon cell blaming its opener for 'never becoming clickable' when the persona had been REDIRECTED AWAY and never reached the page at all - the oracle could not tell 'the control is stuck' from 'we were never there', and both read as the same N/A. Both are fixed in prove_journey.mjs (the chooser now ranks every candidate and prefers a roster one; abandon distinguishes redirected / not-in-DOM / hidden-or-disabled / present-and-stuck) and this gate holds the line: it re-reads the live report every run, so a future N/A that names a reason the walk did not observe turns it red.

cross-tab-identity-propagates.label: CF: an identity change in ONE tab must reach the others (T148, 2026-08-27). Two events change what EVERY open tab is allowed to show, and both happen in a single tab. SIGN-OUT already propagated and did it well - measured with two real tabs, clearing identity in tab A sent tab B to index.html?signin=1&reason=othertab&return=<page>: it noticed, NAMED the reason, and kept the destination. HIVE SWITCH propagated NOT AT ALL: storage said Manila Electronics Assembly while the other tab still rendered Baguio Textile Mills - the cross-tenant confusion T51 exists to prevent, and worse than an ordinary stale number because the person JUST switched and believes they are looking at the new plant. ★THE HANDLER TELLS RATHER THAN RELOADS, and the gate enforces that as a FORBIDDEN clause: auto-reloading somebody's other tab would discard a half-typed entry to fix a DISPLAY problem, on a platform whose whole posture on interruption is that typed work survives. A reload the person CHOOSES (a 44px button) is correct; a reload done to them is not. The notice names BOTH hives so the reader knows which figures are in front of them. ★AND THE NAME MUST BE READ LATE: a switch writes several keys and storage events arrive one per key in write order, so reading wh_hive_name the instant the ID event landed read the name the switch had not replaced yet - the first cut said 'You switched to Baguio... still showing Baguio', naming one hive twice, which reads like a bug in the switch rather than a stale tab. Deferred one tick, with a neutral 'another hive' fallback. Teeth 8/8, one per clause plus the forbidden unprompted reload; the negatives remove EVERY occurrence of a pattern after one of them passed vacuously by replacing only the first.

selection-is-exposed.label: T125: which control is SELECTED must reach the accessibility tree, not only the pixels (2026-08-27). `.active` paints a violet background - invisible to a screen reader and to a forced-colors user. 20 pages appeared to use role=tab; 18 set aria-selected, asset-hub set NONE (3 reliability tabs announcing tab without ever saying which was current, no tabpanels, no arrow keys), and the 20th was this gate's own grep matching a COMMENT. Fixed by completing the widget; analytics.html aria-pressed toggles are the other legitimate answer and are honoured. The aria-controls gap on 17 pages is REPORTED every run, not failed - real owed work, neither enforced nor deleted.

shared-button-invites-the-click.label: T179 affordance parity (2026-08-27): 601 live interactive elements across 12 signed-in pages, and exactly ONE rendered without cursor:pointer - marketplace's .btn-ghost 'Preview as buyer', accepting a click it never invited. The class is used on 16 pages; tokens.css owned its 44px tap floor but not its cursor, and 15 pages happened to declare one locally, hiding the incomplete contract. Fixed centrally rather than in marketplace, because patching the instance leaves the trap armed for the next page. This gate holds the CONTRACT: the shared class invites the click when enabled and withdraws it when disabled.

animation-never-hides-content.label: CF: an optional API's absence must never hide CONTENT (T119, 2026-08-27). MEASURED by removing the capability an older engine lacks: index.html styled `.reveal { opacity: 0 }` and made those elements visible only when an IntersectionObserver callback added `.visible`, so on an engine without the API the constructor THREW, the rest of that script block never ran, and all 14 .reveal elements stayed invisible permanently - the landing page rendered 525 characters of text where every other page rendered 1146+. ★NOTHING WOULD HAVE REPORTED IT: no failed request, no error state, no blank shell - the page 'loaded fine' and simply never faded its content in, the same shape as a skeleton that never resolves. And the source SAID it was safe; the comment above the observer read 'all browsers', which is an assumption wearing the clothes of a check. ★THE GATE REQUIRES BOTH HALVES, because a guard alone is not enough: skipping the observer while leaving opacity:0 in place would pass a naive 'is it guarded' test and still ship a blank page. So every construction must have a feature check BEFORE it - positionally, since a check that runs after the throw protects nothing - AND the hidden class must have a reveal-everything fallback. Fixed at all five call sites, each failing OPEN: the main reveal shows everything, the stagger reuses its EXISTING reducedMotion branch rather than inventing a second path, the before/after rows are shown outright, and the sticky-CTA and nav-highlight observers (which only ADD behaviour) return early - the nav one was the loudest, constructing an observer PER SECTION. Verified both ways: without the API index renders 1061 chars and nothing throws; with it, .reveal still gains .visible on scroll. Teeth 4/4.

dead-end-has-a-door.label: CF: a read-failure state must offer a way OUT, not just a sentence (T193, 2026-08-27). whListError is the shared read-failure panel behind ~24 pages, so what it renders IS the platform's error state, and it must carry all three doors, each answering a question a stuck person actually asks: RETRY ('try again' - the answer when the failure was transient), STATUS ('is it just me?' - a link to status.html, the answer when it was not), and THE ESCALATION DOOR ('then who do I tell?' - into the feedback queue with page, error sentence and time PRE-ATTACHED, so a report describes the failure instead of saying 'it doesn't work'). Lose the third and someone who has retried, checked status and found the platform healthy is simply stuck. ★WHY IT GATES THE HELPER AND NOT A PAGE CENSUS: a first cut counted pages that call whListError and also ship the feedback widget, and reported ALL 24 as missing it - because no page ships it. nav-hub.js injects wh-feedback-fab.js centrally. The mechanism was fine and the census was measuring a per-page script tag that does not exist by design; absence of a per-page marker is not absence of the capability, so the property is held where it lives, in the one function that renders the state. ★THE DOOR IS CONDITIONAL ON PURPOSE - rendered only when window.WHFeedback.open exists, so it can never be a door onto nothing - which makes TIMING the real risk, since the fab is injected asynchronously and a read failing faster than it loads would build a panel with no door. Measured live under aborted reads: WHFeedback ready at 1200ms, before any panel built, and a panel rendered on demand carries retry + status + door at a 44px gloved-hand target. Teeth 4/4, one per affordance removed in turn.

typed-work-is-drafted.label: CF: a committing surface that holds TYPED work must be able to give it back (T38, 2026-08-27). A session dies, a phone is backgrounded, a tab is killed. On a page someone only READ, that costs a reload; on a page where they TYPED, it costs their words - and this platform's whole promise on a plant floor is that the work you did is the work that is recorded. So a page that both writes rows and offers a textarea must carry a draft mechanism. ★THE GATE'S OWN FIRST CENSUS WAS WRONG, WHICH IS WHY THE RULE IS SHAPED THIS WAY: checking for `whAutoSaveDraft` alone reported logbook.html - the flagship committing surface of the entire platform - as UNPROTECTED, when it has carried its own DRAFT_KEY / saveDraft / restoreDraft trio for months. Absence of the shared HELPER is not absence of the GUARD; a gate that recognises one implementation measures a naming convention, not the property, and would have sent someone to 'fix' a page that was already correct. Both forms count and a page is a finding only when NEITHER is present. MEASURED: 12 committing surfaces with typed work - 11 on the shared helper, logbook on its own, assistant exempt by reason (a chat turn is SENT immediately, so there is no compose-then-commit gap to lose) - and resume.html had NOTHING. Its #jd-input holds a job description the person PASTED from elsewhere, exactly the work that is expensive to reproduce: a session dying between the paste and the Tailor call sent them back to find the posting again. Fixed with the shared helper (which also stamps owner and age, so a shared plant tablet never hands one worker's paste to the next) and PROVEN LIVE - the paste survives a full reload byte-for-byte, restored into an empty field only. Teeth 4/4, including the one that matters: a page whose protection is page-local rather than shared must PASS.

earning-moment-is-announced.label: CF: every success path of an XP-earning action must name the award (T17, 2026-08-27). MEASURED: a pm_completions insert pays XP through trg_pm_achievement, and submitCompletion() has TWO terminal success paths - one when the worker also mirrors the work to the logbook, one when they do not. The first announced ' · +N XP'; the second was SILENT. Same action, same trigger, same award, two different receipts, decided by an unrelated toggle ('also log this to the logbook') that has nothing to do with earning. That is the sibling-drift shape this codebase keeps meeting: a fix lands on the path someone walked and not the one beside it. ★SO THE RULE IS NOT 'THE PAGE MENTIONS XP SOMEWHERE' - it is that every success branch routes through ONE helper, because two inline copies would satisfy a mention-count check and drift again. ★AND THE RECEIPT READS THE LEDGER, NEVER RECOMPUTES IT: the trigger's rule lives in SQL (20 XP, +20 more for a detailed entry) and a JavaScript copy would be a second source of truth for a number shown to a worker as fact, so the helper reads achievement_xp_log back by source_id. Verified live that it is RLS-scoped: a row the signed-in worker owns returns ' · +60 XP', another worker's returns '' - so the receipt can neither leak nor overstate - and a failed read returns '' too, making it quieter but never wrong. The dedup-upgrade path is exempt BY REASON, not by silence: it turns a deferral into a completion with an UPDATE, and the trigger fires on INSERT, so no award is paid and claiming one would be inventing it. ★ITS OWN MATCHER WAS WRONG FIRST: a regex window stopping at the first ')' landed INSIDE the message text ('...Analytics (SMRP).') and reported two already-fixed paths as silent - a matcher that stops at a bracket the COPY happens to contain is measuring punctuation, not code - so it now scans balanced parens. Teeth 4/4: silent sibling, a helper that invents a number, a helper that counts reversed awards, and the clean surface.

your-own-message-is-visible.label: T96 (2026-08-27): a person must see the message THEY sent, answered or not. Measured with two signed-in buyers on ONE code path - Romeo Beltran (replied) saw his thread, Pablo Aguilar (pending) saw NOTHING: no message, no state, no sign he had ever asked. One clause did it, .not(reply_text,is,null), so a thread appeared only once the other party got round to answering. An invisible sent message is indistinguishable from one that never sent, so the buyer cannot tell whether to follow up while the platform holds the record the whole time. Holds four things: the read is not filtered to answered-only; the pending state is RENDERED not merely fetched; the pending line carries a DATE (how long it has been IS the question); and the panel stays scoped to buyer_name, since one showing OTHER people's inquiries would satisfy the rest and be a privacy defect. Selftest 6/6. Its own first run FAILED on the fixed file by matching the fix COMMENT, which quotes the clause it removed - the gate now strips comments.

at-cap-fits.label: T130 (2026-08-28): the longest LEGAL value must not break the form that accepts it. A maxlength tells a person how much they may type and says nothing about whether the layout survives them typing it - a field can advertise 200 characters and blow its container at 180, with nobody knowing until a worker with a long part number meets it on a phone. ★A RESTING SWEEP CANNOT SEE THIS, which is why the prover drives flows open: filling capped fields at rest reached 10 of 66, because the other 56 live inside modals, sheets, composers and wizard steps that do not exist until something is clicked - inventory, logbook, project-manager, community and pm-scheduler each reported ZERO capped fields, not for lack of caps but for lack of an opener. Reporting '66 fields, 0 break' off that run would have been a skipped partition reading as a covered one. The value is a single unbroken run of 'W' on purpose: a cap-length SENTENCE wraps and hides the overflow, while a cap-length part number, serial or URL - what people actually paste - does not. ★TWO OF MY OWN CUTS WENT GREEN OVER NOTHING BEFORE THIS WAS RIGHT. First, measuring geometry without visibility produced 18 'defects' that were one CLOSED feedback drawer (visibility:hidden at x=754 against a 390 viewport) counted once per page. Then, guessing the surface selector as '#part-form, #add-part-modal, form' when the real container is #part-modal reached 0 of inventory's 4 fields and reported ok - a prover that opens the right form and measures the wrong box is indistinguishable from a clean run. So each flow now declares how many fields it EXPECTS and under-reach is a FAILURE, not a quiet zero. 18 capped fields across 7 flows at 390, 0 breaking. Teeth 7/7: every flow with fields goes red when its container is widened, each verified clean=0 first. Read-only - fills, measures, restores; never submits.

the-concurrency-guard-can-fire.label: T138 (2026-08-28): a guarded table must move its updated_at SERVER-side, not by caller discipline. Ten pages guard an edit by re-sending the row's last-seen updated_at as a filter, so a stale writer matches no row and is told. The stamp can move two ways: the CALLER sends updated_at in its payload (what inventory.html has always done, and it works), or a TRIGGER sets it. This gate ratchets the second. ★IT EXISTS BECAUSE I FIRST REPORTED THE FIRST ONE AS A DEFECT AND WAS WRONG: inventory_items had no trigger, so I probed with `UPDATE ... SET qty_on_hand = ...`, saw the stamp frozen and writer B overwrite writer A, and filed a guard that could never fire. The page does not send that statement - it sends `SET qty_on_hand = ..., updated_at = <now>`. Re-raced with two PRODUCT-SHAPED writers and the trigger dropped: A rows=1, B rows=0, A survived. The guard had always worked; I had measured a shape the product never sends, and the frozen stamp was an artifact of my statement rather than a property of the table. THE HONEST PROPERTY, which is what is gated: caller-supplied stamps work but are a promise every future edit path must keep, and the failure is SILENT - omit the field and the concurrency check quietly stops, with nothing erroring. A trigger cannot be forgotten, and it also makes the stamp server-authoritative instead of trusting new Date() on a device whose clock may be wrong. A red here means 'this table relies on caller discipline', NEVER 'this guard is broken'. 9/9 green, fails CLOSED when the DB is unreachable, teeth 2/2 by dropping the trigger inside a rolled-back transaction.

the-interrupted-action-completes.label: T5 (2026-08-28): the action a person tapped BEFORE the wall must finish after it. An anon visitor taps Save on a listing; the platform answers with a sign-in door, correctly, and what decides whether the door was worth walking through is what happens on the far side. Returning them to the PAGE is the easy half and was already done; returning them to the ACTION is this one - toggleWatchlist's anon branch stashes wh_pending_action, loadWatchlist replays it once the person has a name. Proven live 2026-08-25 and then left with NO GATE, which is why this exists: the replay is four lines inside a loader, invisible to every other oracle, and its failure is SILENT - nothing errors, the listing is simply not saved, and only the person who tapped knows. Holds four clauses, each of which a plausible edit removes: the intent is stashed (in sessionStorage, so it dies with the tab - one that outlived the session would fire days later against a listing they no longer want); it is actually REPLAYED (a stash nobody reads does nothing); it is SINGLE-SHOT, the key consumed BEFORE the call so a throwing replay cannot loop; and it is IDEMPOTENT. ★THE LAST CLAUSE IS THE ONE WORTH GATING: the other three fail visibly the first time anyone walks the flow, but this one fires only when state raced ahead - saved in another tab, saved another way - and since toggleWatchlist is a TOGGLE, replaying over an already-saved listing UN-SAVES the very thing the person asked for. Its symptom reads as 'the platform lost my save', not as a replay bug. Selftest 7/7, comment-stripped because the fix's own comment describes all four clauses and a prose-reading detector would pass a file whose CODE had lost them.

read-only-lane.label: T53 (2026-08-28): a person who only READS is never forced to write. Not every account operates the plant - a manager, an owner, a client on a site visit signs in to LOOK, reads, and leaves. That lane had no gate, because every existing journey asserts that an ACTION succeeds, and an action-shaped oracle cannot see this persona's defect: being stopped before reading anything at all. ★THE TRAJECTORY SPLITS AND ONLY HALF IS GATEABLE: whether the exec deserves a different LANDING is a design call and stays Ian's; whether a reader is FORCED INTO A WRITE is observable on arrival and needs no decision. Walks six exec-shaped surfaces signed in, settles, and requires no blocking modal, no body-scroll lock, no sign-in/pick-a-hive wall, no focus stolen into a text input (on a phone that opens a keyboard at someone who came to read), and no page error. ★THE SIXTH CLAUSE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, because the other five are all ABSENCES and a BLANK PAGE satisfies every one of them - an all-absence oracle grades a dead page as a perfect reading experience. So it also requires the reader actually got words, counting VISIBLE TEXT rather than figures: T53's own walk twice misread a healthy surface as thin, once by counting characters mid-render and once by counting figures on analytics-report, whose correct state is an instruction with no figures at all. The 220-char floor is deliberately low for exactly that page. Read-only by construction - never clicks, types or submits. 6/6 green at 1280. Teeth 5/5 via --teeth: each clause injected on a real signed-in page and asserted to fire, each checked non-vacuous (the clean page reported 0 first), because a gate locking already-correct behaviour has never been seen to go red and is otherwise a green light of unknown wiring.

a-dismissal-belongs-to-a-person.label: T121 (2026-08-28): a dismissal is a person's decision, not the browser's. The shared station tablet is this platform's normal deployment - one device, a crew signing in and out through a shift - and three dismissal flags stored the literal string '1', which belongs to the BROWSER: wh_onboarding_dismissed (index's first-run Getting Started ladder), wh_cmms_guide_dismissed (integrations' setup guide), and wh_guide_link_dismissed_<page> (learn-link's 'New to this page?' chip, which rides EVERY page). Worker A taps Dismiss; worker B signs in on the same tablet and is never introduced to anything. ★THIS LEAK RUNS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION FROM ITS SIBLINGS, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED THEM: the draft, filter and companion-history fixes all stopped A's CONTENT reaching B, so they read as privacy work and this did not - nothing of A's is exposed. What crosses is A's DECISION, and the cost lands on B as an ABSENCE: no card, no chip, nothing on screen to notice or report. The onboarding ladder made it sharper still - its three step-checks were ALREADY person-aware (workerName, jobs, pmDoneToday), so the card knew B had done nothing; it just never got to run, because the flag returned before the check. Correct logic behind a device-wide gate. Fixed centrally (whStateOwner/whIsDismissed/whSetDismissed in utils.js, replacing a FOURTH hand-rolled owner read) and at all three sites; a legacy '1' is nobody's, so the guide returns once - for HELP that is the safe direction, since re-showing a card costs a tap and hiding it costs the introduction. sessionStorage flags are exempt: they die with the tab. Live-proven at 390 (A dismissed -> B sees the guide -> A still dismissed -> legacy '1' belongs to no one), probe restoring the real owner it captured first. Selftest 9/9, including two non-vacuity checks: the first versions of both negatives swapped only the helper CALL, leaving the typeof guard inside the exemption window, so they passed while detecting nothing.

optimistic-ui-reconciles.label: Optimistic UI reconciles (marketplace's watchlist heart fills before the server answers, and a refused write takes the paint back AND says why; the optimism itself is asserted so the check cannot pass vacuously)

no-comment-inside-tag.label: No comment inside a tag (an HTML comment opened between an element's attributes is parsed as bogus attributes and silently drops what follows — the browser never errors)

celebration-proportionality.label: Celebration proportionality (the tier ladder and the round-number ladder live in different files and must not fire full-screen modals on consecutive level-ups — two celebrations in a row is one interruption, and it devalues the larger)

status-literals-are-classified.label: Status literals are classified (every status value the code WRITES must be one the consuming truth view classifies — a value permitted by a CHECK but bucketed by nothing is a value that means nothing)

import-undo-removes-the-import.label: Import undo removes the import (undoing a batch deletes the rows THAT batch created and leaves an unrelated row the same person made minutes later untouched; the toast states the count actually removed)

import-names-dropped-columns.label: Import names dropped columns (a source column mapped to nothing is NAMED in the preview with the step that can fix it, before any row is written; a fully-mapped file raises no notice)

status-cold-is-not-down.label: Status: cold is not down (a hung /health probe reads as silence naming a likely cold start, never DOWN, and never leaks the raw AbortError; a real 503 still reads DOWN; the unanswered surface leaves BOTH the healthy numerator and the DOWN count and is named)

reload-mid-flow.label: The CF `reload` oracle, measured by actually reloading mid-flow: a half-filled sheet either survives intact or is GONE, never restored into a state the person did not leave it in. 42 targets, 12 graded (all GONE, an acceptable answer), 29 not-applicable with the reason stated (a sheet with no text field has no half-fill to measure), 1 reach gap. ★REGISTERED 2026-08-28 FROM THE ORPHAN SWEEP. It was on disk, runnable, and invoked by NOTHING - neither listed as a board script nor called by any registered one. Thirteen provers were in that state; ten ran clean, and six of those EXIT NON-ZERO on failure, so they are real gates rather than recorders. The four that only record are deliberately NOT registered: a gate that cannot go red is a permanent false green, which is worse than no gate at all. ★AND THIS ONE WAS ORPHANED BECAUSE IT CRASHED: one dead context ended the whole run, so it reported five passes and a stack trace. Repaired at BOTH layers - reviving the context alone just moved the crash two targets along, because the browser process itself was dying.
