Thirteen provers were in that state; ten ran clean, and six of those EXIT NON-ZERO on failure, so they are real gates rather than recorders. The four that only record are deliberately NOT registered: a gate that cannot go red is a permanent false green, which is worse than no gate at all.

cta-activation.label: T1.2 (built 2026-08; REGISTERED 2026-08-28): every visible primary CTA, CLICKED, with an observable consequence. ★THIS PROVER EXISTED FOR WEEKS AND WAS NEVER ON THE BOARD - built precisely because 790 green gates coexisted with a dead 'Get Early Access' bar on the landing page, since every CTA oracle here asserts EXISTENCE (the element is present, named, 44px) and none asserted CONSEQUENCE (tapping it changes the world). It was referenced only inside ANOTHER gate's label text, which reads like registration and runs nothing. ★AND IT WAS UNREGISTERABLE WHILE IT LIED: run as shipped it reported a dead click on 'Open the AI Assistant', and the CTA works. Cause: the seeder serves each page at BOTH /learn/<slug>/ and /workhive/learn/<slug>/, 200 either way with identical text, but rewrites root-absolute hrefs only under the PREFIXED path - so at the unprefixed path the link pointed at /assistant.html, which 404s, and the prover recorded a working control as dead. A prover that cries wolf about the one class it exists to catch is a prover nobody registers, which is exactly what happened. Now walks ${ORIGIN}${PATH_BASE}/, verified by hand-clicking the control under the prefix (it navigates and lands on the assistant page). 29 probes across index, public-feed, marketplace and the learn/tools exemplars at 390 and 1280; 0 dead against a 0 baseline. Demands navigation | modal | scroll-delta | focus-move | DOM-mutation, and records a still-inert control as inert-stuck rather than skipping it.

a-shown-count-is-not-the-page-size.label: T15/T129 (2026-08-28): a number on the glass counts the WORLD, not the fetch. logbook's machine-history panel read .limit(5) and titled itself `data.length + past repairs on + machineId` - a sentence about the array wearing the clothes of a sentence about the plant. MEASURED: 94 machines in the fixture hold more than five fault_knowledge rows and M-003 holds 77, so the panel announced 5 past repairs on a machine with 77 - and this is the panel a technician consults BEFORE opening equipment. Under-reporting a machine's history to the person deciding how careful to be is the wrong direction to be wrong in. Fixed by fetching the true total (count:'exact', head:true - no rows shipped) and rendering '47 past repairs on M-001 · showing the latest 5', verified live; if the count read fails it falls back to describing the LIST ('Latest 5 repairs') rather than a number it cannot support. ★THE CLASS WAS ALREADY KNOWN HERE, which is why the gate holds the SHAPE: asset-hub hit the identical bug (AH16 - '500 reading(s) in the last 30 days' for an asset with 3,174, under-reporting 6x while every mean and sigma above it came from the same truncated slice) and marketplace solves it a third way by rendering an em-dash when the read was partial. Three surfaces, one property; logbook was the instance nobody had walked. ★DELIBERATELY SCOPED to the two sites where the cap is REACHABLE - founder-console (500 campaigns) and marketplace-admin (100 disputes) share the shape but hold 3 and 0 rows, and gating arithmetic that cannot happen yet is noise. Selftest 5/5; its exact-count negative was vacuous first, because logbook holds THREE such reads and the mutation edited an unrelated query 1,600 lines away.

the-calc-count-is-true.label: T151/T161 (2026-08-28): a public claim about how many calculators we have must match how many we have. Two surfaces were wrong: engineering-design.html's meta said '46 calculation types ... and Structural', and assistant.html's GROUNDING - the text the AI answers from - said '46 ... Structural, Machine Design, Vertical Transportation'. Counted from CALC_TYPES_UI, the file's own declared sole source of truth: 55 types across SIX disciplines (HVAC & Cooling 10, Mechanical 4, Electrical 14, Plumbing 10, Fire Protection 5, Machine Design 12), confirmed live in the browser and against the project's own substrate note. ★THE UNDERCOUNT IS THE FORGIVABLE HALF - the damaging half is the DISCIPLINE list: both named Structural and the assistant also named Vertical Transportation, neither of which exists here. An SEO snippet promising a structural calculator sends a searcher to a page that has none; the assistant's grounding is worse, because the AI states it confidently in conversation to someone who then goes looking. A wrong NUMBER is a stale fact; a wrong CAPABILITY is a promise the product cannot keep. ★THE GATE COUNTS THE REGISTRY RATHER THAN COMPARING TWO STRINGS, because the drift happened exactly as it always does - a human typed a number that was right at the time, and anything hand-maintained against a growing registry is a future defect with a date on it. ★AND THE /learn '60 free calculators' CLAIM IS DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE: it counts the 60 PUBLIC /tools pages, a different population, and folding two populations into one gate is how a CORRECT claim gets 'fixed' into a wrong one. Selftest 6/6.

a-pasted-identifier-still-matches.label: T123 (2026-08-28): whitespace must never decide whether the system works. People paste - a part number from a Viber message, a username from an email - and every pasted value can carry a leading or trailing space the person cannot see. Where the value is used for IDENTITY or MATCHING, that invisible character decides the outcome: a space on si-username/su-username and sign-in fails with correct credentials; a space in the inventory SEARCH and a part that exists returns nothing, which reads as 'we do not stock it' to someone standing at the shelf; a space in part_number/part_name on WRITE is baked into the record, so the row never matches its own search again; a space on a recipient email and the report bounces. All six are trimmed today and this holds them there. ★THE PROPERTY IS DELIBERATELY NOT 'TRIM EVERYTHING': dayplanner's note and logbook's knowledge field are textareas where a person may indent lines, so leading whitespace is CONTENT, and a gate demanding .trim() on every text field would enforce an opinion about prose and eventually be switched off. ★THE SCAN NEEDED CAREFUL READING, WHICH IS WHY THE SUBJECT LIST IS EXPLICIT: a search for untrimmed values reaching a payload flagged inventory's q and cat, both of which are the remembered-filter SNAPSHOT - restored into the input and re-trimmed at the point of use - so judging by the assignment rather than the use would have filed two defects against correct code. ★AND THE SELFTEST MUTATES COPIES, NEVER DISK: its first version rewrote the real product files and restored them in a finally block, which is one crash or one concurrent board read away from a corrupted source or a voided board. Selftest 7/7, each field mutated independently.

the-return-promise-is-kept-safely.label: T4 (2026-08-28): a wall that promises to send you back must send you back, and only somewhere safe. An anon or hive-less visitor tapping into Community is bounced to the hive gate, and that bounce used to DROP the destination - so a person who set out for one place arrived somewhere else with no way back and nothing explaining why. Now community stamps hive.html?return=community.html and hive.html renders a 'Continue to Community' banner honouring it. TWO HALVES GATED TOGETHER because they are ONE promise in two files: a stamp nobody reads is a query string, a banner with nothing to read is dead markup, and a fix to either side alone breaks the promise with nothing erroring. ★THE THIRD CLAUSE MATTERS MOST - IT IS A SECURITY PROPERTY HIDING INSIDE A USABILITY FEATURE: ?return= is user-controllable, and the naive implementation (location.href = raw) is an OPEN REDIRECT, a link to our own trusted domain that lands the person on an attacker's page wearing our reputation. The guard must be a strict same-origin FILENAME allow-list, never a blocklist - one rejecting 'http://' and '//' still passes '/\evil.com' and a dozen encodings. Nothing about the feature LOOKS security-sensitive, which is exactly why its shape is locked. Fourth: the label is built with textContent, so a crafted filename cannot inject markup even if the allow-list is ever loosened. Selftest 6/6.

a-removed-image-actually-leaves.label: T134 (2026-08-28): a listing's photo leaves the public bucket when the listing does - and when it is REPLACED. Deleting a listing removed the row and left the JPEG at a permanent public URL, so 'this cannot be undone' was true of the row and quietly false of the photo: anyone holding the link still had it after the seller believed they had removed the listing. ★THE FIX-EVERY-PATH PASS FOUND THE BIGGER SOURCE - deleting is rare, REPLACING an image on edit is common, and it orphaned the old object exactly the same way, far more often. A gate holding only the delete path would have locked the half that almost never runs while the frequent one kept leaking, which is worse than no gate because the board would report the class closed. Holds both sites and both of the edit path's guards: remove only when the URL actually CHANGED (re-saving an unchanged listing must not delete its own live image) and only when the old object is OURS by bucket-marker (a seller may paste an external URL, and we must not reach into someone else's host). Both cleanups stay BEST-EFFORT and wrapped, running after the write so a storage hiccup can never cost the seller the edit or delete they asked for - the inverse of the coupling T12 had to break. Selftest 5/5. ★THE OWNERSHIP NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS FIRST: a whole-file search for indexOf(_marker) is satisfied by the DELETE path's own copy, so removing the EDIT path's guard left the file matching and the case passed while detecting nothing - two near-identical blocks on one page is precisely the shape that makes a loose check vacuous, and it is now scoped to the edit block.

the-policy-matches-what-ships.label: T165 (2026-08-28): the privacy policy must describe the analytics that actually ship. It said 'we do not run third-party analytics... when we add web analytics in the future, this page will be updated' while GA4 (wh-ga4.js) was already live on 10 public pages. ★A STALE SENTENCE ON A LEGAL SURFACE IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF DEFECT: everywhere else drift means a number is wrong or a label is old, but here it means the document a regulator, an enterprise buyer or a worker reads to decide whether to trust us was making a FALSE STATEMENT about what we collect - false in the direction that flatters us, which is the direction nobody audits, and invisible because prose never looks broken. Gated as PARITY in both directions so it cannot rot from either side: if wh-ga4.js loads, the policy must NAME Google Analytics and must not carry the future-tense denial; it must state the IP anonymization the code actually runs (naming GA4 without it under-claims our own protection, which is still a mismatch); and if GA4 were ever removed, a policy still describing it over-claims what is collected - the same drift in reverse. Comment-stripped, and that is not a formality here: the fix left an HTML comment quoting the old denial verbatim so the correction stays legible, and a detector reading comments would find 'when we add web analytics in the future' in the FIXED file and convict the page for documenting its own repair - the single most reliable false positive in this whole gate family, hit three times on other subjects this session. Selftest 6/6, including a non-vacuity check that the GA4 page roster is not empty.

the-note-survives-the-reply.label: T12 (2026-08-28): a worker's note must outlive the AI that was going to answer it. voice-journal is where someone captures a thought mid-shift; the companion's reply is the nice part, the NOTE is the part that matters. ★THE ORIGINAL DESIGN LOST THE NOTE TO A QUOTA ERROR: the write happened server-side inside the voice-journal-agent call, so a 429 from the gateway meant the row was never written - the page was HONEST about it ('your note was not saved') and the note was still gone. On a shared free tier that is Friday afternoon, which is exactly when a worker is capturing something they will not remember later. Three clauses: (1) the page has its OWN EYES - noteLanded() re-reads for the note instead of inferring its fate from the call's outcome, because an error on the reply says nothing about whether the row exists and a page that guesses will tell a worker their words are gone when they are safe, or the reverse, which is worse; (2) it says the true sentence on BOTH paths - typed and spoken are separate catch blocks, so a fix landing in one produces a page that tells the truth depending on how you happened to enter the note; (3) the microphone failure NAMES ITS OWN CAUSE - one catch blamed 'permission denied' for every getUserMedia failure, so a mic-less desktop sent the worker to check a permission they never refused, and branching on err.name (NotAllowed/Security vs NotFound/Overconstrained) is the difference between a remedy and a wild goose chase, with every branch still naming the typed fallback. Selftest 5/5, with the two reply paths mutated independently.

the-ack-scope-matches-its-promise.label: T144 (2026-08-28): acking a plant alert hides it for the WHOLE CREW, and the page must say so. alert-hub's dismissal is HIVE state - the upsert is keyed onConflict: 'hive_id,alert_key', NOT on the actor - so one person marking an alert handled removes it from every teammate's feed. That is deliberate: a plant alert is about a machine, not a personal inbox, and it should stop nagging the crew once somebody has dealt with it. ★IT IS ALSO THE ONE FAILURE MODE THIS PAGE CANNOT AFFORD IF IT HAPPENS SILENTLY - a worker tidying what they believe is their own view can blind the entire crew to a live plant condition - so the scope and the SENTENCE are held as ONE property: the write is hive-keyed; the row still records actor (crew-wide AND anonymous would be far worse than either alone); and the toast says both, 'hidden for your whole hive now, recorded under your name'. The old copy said only 'Alert marked handled', which is true and tells the person nothing about who else just stopped seeing it: a scope this wide is defensible when stated and indefensible when discovered. Also gates convergence - setInterval(loadAll, 60000) so a second tab is not stale forever, and a visibilitychange pause so a phone in a pocket is not polling a plant database with no reader. Selftest 6/6. ★ITS ATTRIBUTION NEGATIVE WAS VACUOUS TWICE: a whole-file search for actor: WORKER_NAME also matched an UNRELATED upsert and two comments, so removing it from every dismissal still passed; and the mutation that fixed that deleted the upsert prefix too, tripping 'no upsert found' while the case was labelled 'losing attribution' - detecting something real and proving nothing about the clause it named. The mutation is now a named helper that removes ONLY the actor field, verified to leave the statement intact.

a-busy-button-says-working.label: T41 (2026-08-28): a locked control announces WORK, not unavailability. button-lock.js is the platform's single-flight guard - withButtonLock disables a committing control while its work runs, so a rage-tap on a slow plant connection produces one effect instead of five - and it set disabled plus an is-loading class and nothing else. ★DISABLED AND BUSY ARE DIFFERENT SENTENCES: `disabled` alone announces 'unavailable', the same thing a control says when it is not applicable or you may not use it at all. A sighted user never hears that sentence - they see the spinner and know the press landed. A screen-reader user hears only 'unavailable', reasonably concludes the tap did NOT register, and presses again, on exactly the controls where a second press costs the most. aria-busy is the state that means in-progress. THE PAIRING IS THE OTHER HALF: it must be REMOVED in the release beside disabled, because a button left announcing itself busy forever after an exception is worse than one that never announced it - the control is now permanently lying. ★AND IT MUST HOLD IN BOTH PAIRS: this file has TWO lock/release paths (withButtonLock, which awaits an async fn, and lockButtonDuring, which returns a release closure), and fixing only one produces a shared helper that is right HALF THE TIME - harder to trust than one consistently wrong, since three pages adopt it today and every future adopter inherits whichever path it happens to call. Selftest 6/6, with each pair mutated INDEPENDENTLY so a fix landing in only one path is caught.

the-photo-cannot-orphan-the-entry.label: T9 (2026-08-28): a repair entry and its photo land together or not at all. The logbook is the platform's core write - a worker on a plant floor, one-handed, recording what they just fixed - and attaching a photo is where that write goes wrong on most systems, because a photo normally means a SECOND write (upload the file, then insert the row) and two writes have two ways to half-succeed: an orphaned file with no entry, or an entry claiming evidence it does not have. ★NEITHER IS REACHABLE HERE, BY CONSTRUCTION: logbook.html contains NO storage.from(...).upload() at all - the photo is compressed client-side and carried INLINE as a data URL in logbook.photo (a text column) inside the SAME insert as the entry, so there is no second write to fail. The decoupling T12 had to ARGUE for on voice-journal is free here. That is precisely why it needs a gate rather than a comment: adding an upload to this page would read as an IMPROVEMENT in review ('move photos to storage, keep rows small') and would silently reintroduce a failure class the page currently cannot have. ★THE COUPLING RUNS THE OTHER WAY AND IS THE REAL RISK - one row carries the typed work AND the image, so a big photo makes a big row and a failed insert takes the worker's words with it. Both halves gated: an oversize file is refused BY NAME before compression ('Photo too large (max 20 MB).') so the worker learns the limit instead of watching a save fail, and the image is compressed rather than sent raw. Fourth clause: when the AI vision path fails it must say the entry is UNCHANGED, because an analysis failure is not a save failure and a worker who cannot tell them apart retypes work that was never lost. Selftest 5/5, comment-stripped - this page documents its single-write design thoroughly, which is exactly what would let a prose-reading detector pass a file that had lost it.

a-deferral-is-not-a-completion.label: T10 (2026-08-28): a task put off is not a task done. A worker who cannot do a PM today DEFERS it; one who does it COMPLETES it, and the gap between those is where a compliance percentage becomes a lie - if a deferral sets last_completed_at, next_due_date rolls forward, the item drops off the overdue list, and the plant's number rises for work nobody did. Nothing errors; the number just quietly stops meaning maintenance. ★THE ENFORCEMENT IS ONE CLAUSE IN ONE VIEW, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY IT NEEDS A GATE: v_pm_scope_items_truth's LATERAL join carries AND (pc.status = 'done'), so every consumer inherits the rule instead of re-implementing it - right design, and also a single dropped AND that would look like a harmless simplification in a diff. Three independent checks, because each can be true while another is false: STRUCTURAL (the view still carries the filter), EMPIRICAL (of the 5 scope items whose completions are ONLY deferrals, 0 carry a last_completed_at - structure can be right while a backfill or manual UPDATE made the data wrong), and LEXICAL (pm-scheduler's history still maps status to 'Completed'/'Deferred'). ★TWO OF MY OWN CUTS CONVICTED CORRECT CODE FIRST. I put analytics.html in the render list on the strength of this trajectory's own prose; analytics does NOT render PM status - its matches are comments about deferred CHART DRAWS and a deferred redirect. And I hunted raw-enum leaks with a regex, which flagged pm-scheduler's `status: isDefer ? 'skipped' : 'done'` - the DB WRITE. The enum SHOULD appear in code that talks to the database; what must never appear is the enum on the GLASS, so the check now reads the display ternary rather than pattern-matching a string with every right to be there. Fails CLOSED when the DB is unreachable. Teeth 2/2: rebuilds the view from its OWN definition with the predicate stripped, inside a rolled-back transaction.

presence-unavailable-is-not-absent.label: T141 (2026-08-28): a fact about the NETWORK must not be rendered as a claim about PEOPLE. hive.html's presence bar answers 'who is here right now'; when the realtime link failed its fallback said 'Members offline' and painted every member with a solid offline dot - a positive claim about people made entirely from a fact about the websocket. Presence unavailable is NOT everyone-absent: the teammate you decide not to call may be standing at the machine. ★THE COST IS A DECISION, NOT A PIXEL - nobody reads a presence bar for fun, they read it to decide whether to walk over, phone someone, or handle it alone, and a bar that says 'offline' when it means 'I cannot see' sends that decision the wrong way while looking perfectly healthy. Same shape as a failed read rendering as an empty list, and it needs its own gate for the same reason: the honest state and the alarming state are both quiet. Four clauses - the fallback names the LINK; it asserts nothing about members being offline; the dot renders UNKNOWN (hollow fill with an outline) rather than the solid away-dot, because the dot is what people read at a glance; and both strings carry EN+FIL. ★THE FOURTH CLAUSE KEEPS THE OTHERS HONEST: renderPresence()'s genuine 'No one online yet' must stay DISTINCT, since that is TRUE when the link is UP and nobody is there - collapsing the two would trade this defect for its mirror image, reporting a real empty room as a network fault. Two notices, two truth conditions. Selftest 6/6, comment-stripped. ★ITS OWN FIRST RUN PRODUCED TWO CONFIDENT FALSE FINDINGS about correct code: find('function renderPresence') matches renderPresenceFallback, which is defined FIRST in the file, so the gate audited the fallback against the live path's rules. The lookup now requires the open paren - the same prefix-matching class as 'end' inside 'trend', caught only by the clean-file selftest case.

a-secret-stays-masked.label: T170 (2026-08-28): a password arrives masked, and revealing it ANNOUNCES that it is revealed. Two halves, each useless alone. MASKED BY DEFAULT: every password field ships type=password, and the shared whPrompt honours inputType:'password' end to end - which had a real gap, since _mount read inputType but whPrompt built its own options object and never forwarded it, so a caller asking for a masked prompt silently got a plain text box and a secret was typed in the clear on a shared plant tablet. The caller was correct; the plumbing dropped it with nothing looking wrong. REVEAL MUST SPEAK: a show/hide toggle is a usability necessity because people mistype passwords on phones, but a control that silently changes whether a secret is visible is a shoulder-surfing hazard for exactly the person who cannot check by looking - so it must flip BOTH aria-label (what pressing it does next) and aria-pressed (what state it is in now). ★AND THE GATE ANCHORS ON THE ACCESSIBLE NAME RATHER THAN THE CODE SHAPE FOR A MEASURED REASON: a search for controls flipping an input type found ZERO, twice, because the pattern expected a quoted literal and togglePwd assigns a TERNARY. The three aria-labels reading 'Show password' were the only evidence the toggles existed - the accessible name was what the code-shape search could not see. Selftest 8/8.

internal-links-resolve.label: Internal Links Resolve (every internal href on all 155 pages — 42 app + 53 learn + 60 calculators — must land on a file OR a directory that serves an index.html; the directory-url shape the .html-suffix gate is blind to; markup only, scripts/styles/comments stripped)

404-notice-helps.label: 404 Notice Helps (a dead path names itself, pre-fills the slug the visitor asked for, and one Enter reaches matching guides; no-match says so; real pages stay silent)

csp-covers-what-ships.label: Prod headers cover what ships (Content-Security-Policy must permit every external script/stylesheet the pages load and every requirement written into the source; Permissions-Policy must permit every browser API they call — an empty allowlist like geolocation=() denies our own pages too. _headers has no local equivalent, so all of it fails only in production, silently)

seller-dashboard-is-reachable.label: Seller dashboard + hidden pages are reachable (the All Tools grid shows a seller their own dashboard, and global search finds curated-out pages like the audit trail by name — driven live in a browser, not asserted from the registry)

boundary-refusal-ratchet.label: T-arc boundary_not_emptiness, held as a forward-only line (2026-08-31). 34 bank rows carry ONE oracle - 'a permission boundary reads as not-visible-with-this-session, never as nothing-here' - and no gate covered it: empty-state-discrimination is about search-0 vs first-run, failed-read-is-not-empty is about a read that ERRORED, auth-boundary is about whether the server refuses. This is the third thing: the read SUCCEEDED, the server lawfully returned nothing, and the question is whether the page says 'you cannot see this' or 'there is nothing here'. ★WHY IT IS HARD AND WHY MOST SURFACES FAIL IT: RLS refuses by FILTERING, not raising - a USING clause returns zero rows and no error, so a foreign-hive read and a genuinely empty hive are byte-identical at the client unless the page makes a separate membership check and has somewhere to say so. MEASURED across 42 root surfaces: 26 own an absence state and 10 of those carry NO refusal copy at all. ★THAT NUMBER READ 25 FIRST AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, TWICE OVER, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE COUNT: the vocabulary was narrower than the product's ('needs a hive'; 'Create or join a Hive' where the regex knew only 'join or create'; 'does not have access' where it knew only 'do not'), AND an edit wrote literal BACKSPACE bytes (0x08) where   word-boundaries were intended, so the join/create clause demanded a backspace character in page text and could never fire. It went 25 -> 24 -> 22 -> 10 with no page changing. A census whose vocabulary is narrower than the product's measures its own wording and invents backlog - here, 2.5x the real one. The scenario is ordinary - a worker removed from a hive keeps wh_active_hive_id in localStorage, their next read is lawfully filtered to zero, and pm-scheduler answers 'No completions recorded yet.' ★THE ONE EXCEPTION IS THE FIX PATTERN, ALREADY IN THIS REPO: marketplace.html:1222-1226 keeps _rateLimited (429 + the wait), _authExpired (401, 'the remedy is signing in, not retrying') and _accessDenied ('a 403 is a REFUSED ROW with a perfectly good session, and signing in again cannot fix it'), reset per load so a since-granted permission stops reading as denied. So the work for the other 25 is to propagate an idiom this codebase already reasoned about. ★AND EVEN THAT EXCEPTION ONLY COVERS THE LOUD HALF: _accessDenied fires on a 403 the server announces; the silent case - RLS filtering, 200 with zero rows - is invisible to any HTTP status and needs the membership read. ★A RATCHET, NOT A FAIL, ON PURPOSE: 25 of 26 fail today, and a gate that is red the day it ships is one people learn to scroll past; this repo's ordering is fix first then enforce (retry_path did the same). The count may FALL, never rise - a NEW surface shipping an empty state with no way to say a refusal happened fails here by name. Comments are stripped before counting, because the first pass credited inventory.html with four refusal states that were every one a source comment or the toast 'Part removed from inventory.' Teeth proven by dropping a surface from the baseline: the check names it and fails.

psql-probe-suite.label: Re-executes EVERY psql recipe in tools/psql_probes/ - the 99 database invariants the page banks stand on. WHY IT EXISTS: 96 bank rows carry evidence kind `psql`, each naming a recipe file in its `replay` line, and until 2026-08-31 NOTHING RAN THEM. They were proven once at bank time and never again. The bank's freshness machinery expires such a row when its declared deps change, which is right for a claim ABOUT A FILE and says nothing about an invariant living in the DATABASE, where a migration, a policy edit or a dropped grant falsifies a recipe while every file it depends on sits untouched. The gap was not theoretical: public-feed__public_identity_only.sql is a REGRESSION LOCK written the same day, because an anonymous visitor could read every public post author's internal auth_uid (measured: 15 of 15 posts, 7 authors, 2 hives) - and a lock nothing executes locks nothing. ★IT EARNED ITS KEEP ON ITS FIRST FULL RUN: three of 99 recipes no longer held, and all three were INSTRUMENT faults rather than product regressions, which is exactly the split this gate exists to force someone to make. (1) assistant__feedback_attributable compared a before-count taken as postgres against an after-count taken as `authenticated`, whose SELECT policy shows only their own rows - postgres saw 1, the user saw 0 - so a perfectly good insert read as a refusal; it now counts the INSERT itself with RETURNING. (2) logbook__pm_mirror_idempotent assumed `completed_at + 1 day` was free, but its fixture worker had completions on CONSECUTIVE days, so the dedup index refused it exactly as designed and the probe called that a broken invariant; the free day is now computed from that pair's latest completion. (3) registry__ghost_retired asserted `marketplace_orders` holds zero rows - a PROXY for 'this relation is inert to clients' that our own test-data-seeder falsified by writing six lifecycle rows; the count leg is gone, the security legs (anon sees 0, INSERT refused by RLS, view is security_invoker) remain, and the genuinely unresolved half - marketplace-admin.html:1026 UPDATEs the table, so 'retired' is drifting - is recorded for Ian instead of quietly re-greened. ★RETRY-ONCE, REPORTED AS A FLAKE: the recipes take row locks and several SET ROLE, so 99 back-to-back reproduces this repo's known flake-under-load class - assistant__citations_resolve_lawfully failed inside the suite once and then passed three times standalone. A failing recipe is retried exactly once and a flake is PRINTED as a flake, never folded into the pass: a false RED sends someone hunting a defect that is not there and teaches the team to re-run reds until they turn green. Sequential on purpose, ~25s for all 99. No residue by construction - every mutating recipe wraps its teeth in BEGIN/ROLLBACK and most assert their own restoration.

anon-boundaries.label: ANON identity boundaries asked over the REAL gateway with the publishable key and NO session - and it was never being run (registered 2026-08-31). The script existed, passed 3/3, and was referenced by nothing: not this file, not another tool. It asks what a signed-in probe structurally cannot: verify_identity_boundaries answers the BE-ufai-I questions as a signed-in NON-ADMIN, which is a different threat model from a stranger holding only the publishable key. Its three checks are the ones that matter for a public API surface: BOLA_OBJECT - an unpublished listing that EXISTS, fetched by id as anon, returns HTTP 200 with 0 rows (an empty 200 is PostgREST's legible RLS refusal, and the row is real, so the zero is a refusal rather than an empty table); JWT_NOT_BODY - an anon INSERT claiming a seller_name in the BODY is refused 401 by the policy rather than trusted, which is the identity-from-the-JWT-not-the-payload rule that the worker_profiles and logbook recipes enforce on the DB side; TENANT_BOUNDARY - every unpublished listing across ALL hives asked for in ONE anon query returns 0 of 7, so the hidden set is invisible AS A SET, not merely one row at a time. ★FOUND BY AUDITING ORPHANS, and it is the same class as companion-delivery registered directly above and the 96 psql recipes nothing re-ran: 629 gate-shaped scripts exist, 96 are absent from this file, and after removing the ones invoked indirectly by a validator wrapper, SIX were referenced by nothing at all. one-clock-per-string.label: Cluster 1 (critic deepwalk): every rendered timestamp keeps ONE clock, and the ops-home shift line is plant-anchored + labeled. Walked live 2026-09-02 at GMT+12: logbook's card read 'Sep 1, 2026 - 12:09 AM' for a save made at 20:09 Manila - whFmtDate pinned the DATE to Asia/Manila while toLocaleTimeString (no timeZone) floated the TIME on the viewer's clock: a pair no clock on earth shows, and any worker east of UTC logging after local midnight filed under yesterday. Meanwhile ops-home derived 'Morning Shift' from viewer-local hours while shift-brain used the plant clock - three answers to 'what shift is it' in one moment. Fixed: formatDate's both halves pin Asia/Manila (whFmtDate + its timeOnly variant); index's _dateStr derives wholly from Asia/Manila and carries '(PHT)' beside the figure (the asset-hub '13:00 PHT' precedent - a shift belongs to the plant, a greeting to the person). This gate reddens on the concatenation shape (pinned date + floating time) anywhere, and on index dropping the Manila derivation or the PHT label. Resurrection: the pre-fix shape matches in self-test.

team-deeplink-survives.label: T29: a deep-linked team search survives init and keeps ALL-history scope. The alert->asset->'Fault history' chain hands off to logbook.html?q=<tag>&view=team; walked live 2026-09-02 (Pablo, PV-002) the supervisor-default init re-ran setViewMode('team') AFTER the URL handler had started searchTeam(), wiping the in-flight results back to the browse prompt - 36 real team rows invisible to the exact persona who walks the diagnostic chain (workers skip that branch, so only supervisors broke). Second half: loadTeamMembers() lands a 7-day date default ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so even a surviving hand-off got silently re-scoped to a week on the next search - 'has this failed before' is an all-history question, and the scoped-zero card's own copy admitted it ('Only that date range was searched - it is not proof the entry does not exist'). Both fixed: the default is view-guarded (_viewMode !== 'team') and the browse window applies only pre-search (!_teamSearched). Static shape-lock with resurrection teeth: the pre-fix unguarded default and an unconditional window both redden the self-test. Fix verified live: the same deep-link now renders 30 cards all-time.
